## nozone: the zone is the heap (agent/nozone, 2026-11-13)

- **His call:** replace the zone allocator with the system one (after "Save crash: Z_Realloc" and "norealloc").
- **vkQuake (research only, nothing copied):** its 85d526c "Replace all custom memory allocation with regular
  alloc/free" (2022-06-19) dropped the zone, the hunk and the cache together for `Quake/mem.c`: `Mem_Alloc` (always
  zeroed: calloc), `Mem_AllocNonZero`, `Mem_Realloc`, `Mem_Free`, plus `TEMP_ALLOC` macros (stack below 512 KB, else
  heap). The backend is mimalloc on Windows/Linux/macOS (CRT malloc elsewhere or under helgrind, SDL's optional); Debug
  builds turn on mimalloc's debug checks and guarded pages (`MI_DEBUG 3`, `MI_GUARDED`). No headers, tags, guards or
  stats of its own; no notes or numbers on performance in the commits (one-line messages; later ones: "Don't zero
  memory before reading files", "Paranoid instrumentation", "Replace PARANOID by regular Debug conditionals").
- **Now (zone.c):** `Z_Malloc` / `Z_Free` / `Z_Strdup` are thin wrappers over `VR_HeapCalloc` / `VR_HeapFree` (calloc
  and free, so vr_alloc_sites counts them; the bench's `heap_allocs` rose by them: ~0.8 a frame idle, Cmd_TokenizeString's
  arguments). Each block has a 16-byte header: its size (vr_limits' bytes, Tracy's ledger) and ZONEID, checked on free
  in every build ("without ZONEID", "freed a freed pointer"). Debug builds add a tail word after the caller's bytes,
  checked on free ("a block's tail was overwritten"). Tracy builds also link the live blocks (32-byte header) so
  `Memory_TracySnapshot` / `Memory_TracyValidate` still walk the zone. `Z_Free (NULL)` does nothing (was a Sys_Error).
  `vr_zone_threadcheck` still covers Z_Malloc/Z_Free (the counts and Tracy's map aren't locked).
- **Gone:** `mainzone`, the first-fit/rover code, `Z_TagMalloc` (only tag 1 was ever used), `Z_CheckHeap` (PARANOID),
  `Z_Print` (no caller), `DYNAMIC_SIZE` and `-zone` (the 32 MiB block at the bottom of the hunk: the hunk keeps it).
  `vr_limits`: "zone, KiB" in use / peak with no maximum, and "zone blocks" (e1m1 at start: 408 KiB, 8,323 blocks).
- **Audit (every Z_ user, ~70 call sites):** nothing outside zone.c read `memblock_t`, a size from a header, tags or
  `Z_CheckHeap` (doomgeneric has its own zone, untouched). Every `Z_Malloc`/`Z_Strdup` pointer is freed with `Z_Free`
  (cvar strings and defaults, aliases, command arguments, search paths and packs, keybindings, the clipboard (pl_win/
  pl_linux/pl_osx -> keys.c), sound codec streams, MD5 loading, QC's strzone strings, tunable overrides); nothing frees
  zone memory with `free()` or heap memory with `Z_Free` (cmd.c's buffers, `Cvar_RegisterVariable`'s copy, the
  knownstrings table and knownzone bitmap are VR_Heap*/realloc+free pairs). `PR_SetEngineString`'s "inside
  qcvm->strings" test can't match a heap pointer (as before: the zone was below the progs on the hunk).
  `SaveData_Fill`'s implausible-pointer guard stays. Tracy: pool 0 ("Zone") kept, same events.
- **Verified:** Release, Release-Tracy, Release-TracyFull and Debug 0 warnings. `vr_tracy_test_memory` under a
  tracy-capture: every `Tracy pool Zone/Hunk/Cache` line PASS (Zone 8,335 live blocks, 551,540 bytes). Debug run
  (tail guards on): e1m1 save, load, changelevel e1m2, `pr_knownstrings_check` 44/0, no guard error. id1 mutator

## clipneg: no shot from a clip that can't pay (branch agent/clipneg, 2026-11-13)

His flat report: "ERROR: weapon clip less than zero" firing the shotgun, a spent flare gun in the left hand.

- **How a shot got through.** `W_CheckNoAmmo` (weapons.qc) let a shot fire when the hand's weapon looked ammoless or had
  `> 0` rounds; the shot then spent its cost (`delAmmoOrClipAndUpdateCounter`), and a clip below the cost went negative
  (clamped, the bprint). Two holes: (1) "ammoless" read the hand's `.currentammo`/`.currentammo2`, a cache that
  `W_SetCurrentAmmoFor` writes; a hand whose cache was left at `AID_NONE` (the fist's, the flare gun's) by any path that
  changed its weapon without that call fired the shotgun put in it from an empty clip; (2) a fractional clip (0.5)
  passed `> 0`.
- **Not reproduced through his keys.** `vr_flatswap_test 5` drives each sequence the brief named through the game's own
  impulses (swap 48, swap twice, the menu's drop 78, H 47, either gun holstered and drawn by the menu's trades, R then
  swap, swap mid-reload, the drawn swap key, swap/reload in the left/swap back) with the empty shotgun right and the
  spent flare gun left: all pay correctly on `next`, each hand's cache matching its weapon. Cases 10 (the cache left at
  none) and 11 (half a round) set up the two holes directly: they FAIL on the old checks (1 unpaid shot each), PASS now.
- **Fix (one source of truth).** `VRGetCurrentAmmo` (vr_util.qc) now derives the ammo kind from the hand's weapon id and
  flags (`WeaponIdToAmmoId`); `.currentammo*` stays only as the engine's mirror. `W_CheckNoAmmo` needs a whole round
  (`>= 1`). `delAmmoOrClipAndUpdateCounter` returns whether the shot was paid; short, it empties what is there (never
  below 0), counts `vr_clip_short` and says it with `developer 1` ("ERROR: shot refused: hand, weapon, clip, cost";
  no more broadcast). `W_FireShotgun` pays first and dry-clicks an unpaid shot; the super shotgun fires one barrel below
  2 rounds (`< 2`, was `== 1`). Shared by VR and flat (the same attack path).
- **Verified:** `vr_flatswap_test 5` 46/0 (`-flatscreenmode`, map vrtesthall); flatswap 1 22/0; flatholster 38/0;
  `flatreload_test.sh` 54/0; the VR reload self-test (`vr_reload_test 9`) 77/0. Scene `flat_clip_unpaid`.

## continue: Continue on Select Campaign's and the Map Library's rows (branch agent/continue, 2026-11-13)

His design: Continue belongs where the game is chosen, not on the difficulty / Run Setup screen. Every Run Setup Start
is a brand-new run; continuing keeps the run's own choices (from the save) and skips Run Setup.
- **Select Campaign** (Official Campaigns, flat and VR alike: one VR page): a campaign with a loadable autosave gets a
  row under its own, "Continue (12 min ago)", with its run on the line under it ("Hard / Classic / Glass cannon": part
  of the row, selected with it; one line cut the run's tail at the page's width). Its help: the campaign, the map, the
  player's health and armour, the time into the level, the whole run. Pressed: that autosave loaded at once (the menu
  closed); the load sets the run from the save's `// qvr_run` line (runsetup::onLoadGame). Dimmed while the campaign
  can't be played. Arcane Dimensions has none (its own game folder's saves).
- **Map Library:** an installed package with an autosave gets a Continue button across the detail's column, above
  Uninstall / Reinstall: "Continue (12 min ago): Hard / Classic". The sticks reach it (down from the keyboard; up from
  Uninstall; right to the list), the laser and mouse press it.
- **Which save:** each game's newest loadable autosave in `autosave/` (its rotating slots too): a campaign's (its
  campaign, no package) or a package's (its sha256), by the save's own context lines, not its file name
  (vr_continue.cpp `refreshLaunchSaves`, read when the page is built: each showing; a file not changed since not read
  again). Quake's campaign also counts a custom map played in it without a package (Play Custom Map / Levels).
- **The run's summary without loading:** `runsetup::saveSummary(text, skill)` parses the save's `// qvr_run` line (the
  parser shared with the load's `readSaveLines`) and builds the same summary as the Run Setup screen (`summaryOf`); a
  save without the line: its own skill, the choices it doesn't say left out.
- **Removed:** the old skill menu's "Resume last game" row (menu.c; only Quake 64's New Game still opens that menu, a
  fresh start now) and `VR_AutosaveNameForLaunch` (its only user).
- **Debug > Tools:** Continue Rows Test (`vr_continue_rows_test`), List Continue Rows (`vr_continue_rows`: each game's
  Continue text and save).
- **Tests:** `vr_continue_rows_test` 16/0 (`developer 1;vr_continue_rows_test`, -QuitOn "continue_rows: [0-9]+
  passed"; self-driven phases: no Continue without an autosave; a Hard / Classic / Glass cannon run on e1m1 saved to
  autosave/: Quake's Continue row right under Quake's, "Continue (just now)" over "Hard / Classic / Glass cannon"; a
  fixture copy as a map package's autosave (its sha taken as installed: no network) gives the package's Continue the
  same text; with other run choices set, the row pressed on the opened page loads it: the menu closed, e1m1, the run and
  skill 2 back; its files removed, no Continue). `vr_runsetup_test` 73/0, `vr_runsetup_screen_test` 16/0,
  menu_shortcuts_test 14/0, `vr_menu_path_check maps/vrcalibration.map` 0 missing; menu_paths.txt regenerated (the two
  Debug rows). Not tested headless: the Map Library's button with a real installed package (the tests have none).
- **cltick1113:** retired 6 ticked checklist lines (dagger label, gore minimal, flashlight, lean, kd stir, dog gate; none had voice notes) and 3 unused scenes (flatlean, gore_presets, nav_tele_gate).

## vkfixes: small fixes after vkQuake (agent/vkfixes, 2026-11-14)

- **Freed edicts in physics** (after vkQuake 5dfca693, 43d02d34, f99e66cc, 96dae868, c664a5b3): `SV_PushEntity` no
  longer runs `SV_Impact` (nor `VR_MissileHitDebug`) when its `SV_LinkEdict (true)`'s trigger touches freed the mover
  or the entity it hit; toss physics, `SV_WalkMove`'s step down, `PF_droptofloor` and `SV_movestep` never set a NULL or
  freed `groundentity`; `SV_Physics_Step` returns after a freefall whose impact or relink freed it; the edicts loop's
  `force_retouch` relink skips one it freed; `SV_TouchLinks` stops firing triggers on an entity an earlier trigger
  removed (and skips freed triggers); `SV_Impact` never runs a freed e2's touch. **Kept as id's:** a freed e1 (a
  missile removing itself in its touch) still reaches e2's touch as `other` (vkQuake skips it: a gameplay change).
- **Sound list cleared at a game switch** (after vkQuake 5e58858c, which frees the oldest half of a full list and
  moves the rest, breaking held pointers): `S_PrecacheSound` now pins its sound (the engine's and the VR code's, which
  keep the pointer); the maps' precache lists (`cl_parse.c`, `vr_client.cpp`), `play`/`playvol` and `S_LocalSound` use
  `S_PrecacheGameSound` (not pinned). `S_ForgetGameSounds` (COM_SwitchGameInternal, after the cache flush) empties the
  unpinned slots no channel or game-time render (`VR_SndHoldsSfx`) plays and nulls `cl.sound_precache` pointing at
  them; no slot ever moves, a new name takes the first empty one. `vr_walltorch.cpp`'s crackle pointer compare pins its
  sound. `vr_limits`' "sounds known" counts the live ones.
- **WAV chunks read within their length** (after vkQuake d235ab8c): the LIST "mark" (24 bytes), the cue point (28),
  fmt (16) and RIFF's WAVE (4) checked against the chunk's length, else a warning; a loop longer than the data is a
  warning (was `Sys_Error`), played to the data's end.
- **The sample counter's wrap** (after vkQuake 03fa1ce8, which kept looping statics restarted): at `paintedtime`
  > 2^30 (~6h45m) `S_StopAllSounds` stopped every sound, the static ones for good. Now `S_RebaseSoundTime` moves
  paintedtime, every channel's end, the raw samples' end and spatial audio's carried render (`VR_SndRebase`) back by
  whole DMA buffers (and whole raw rings when the buffer is smaller): nothing stops or skips. GetSoundtime's statics
  are file-scope now; the wrap is told by `S_Update` (the mix may run on the pool).
- **Tests:** `vr_snd_wav_check` 5/0 (each malformed WAV against a PAGE_NOACCESS page; with the LIST check disabled it
  FAILs "read past the file"); `vr_snd_wrap_test` 1/2 on e1m1 with sound (`-Sound`, `SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy`): 14
  statics, counter jumped to 2^30, wrapped to 5434, 14 playing on, 5/0 (Debug > Other > Sound Counter Wrap runs step
  1 by hand); `Misc/quakevr/sound_switch_test.py <agent> 30` (id1 <-> AD `vr_campaign_native`, 60 loads, the SDL
  dummy audio driver): "sounds known" 415 in id1 and 552 in AD every cycle (before, the list only grew to the union).

  stand), the screen's mutators (rows without `apply`) become the run's with a new seed; the difficulty and the

## vkperf: vkQuake's pusher grid, FTE hull trace, faces on the job pool (agent/vkperf, 2026-11-14)

- **Pusher grid** (`sv_fastpushmove`, default 1; after vkQuake af387967, d6bf6c4c, 32f74820; sv_phys.c): from the
  second pusher moving in a tick, a spatial hash (256-unit cells, 4096 buckets, plain heap) of every edict's abs box
  hands SV_PushMove the edicts near its sweep (old and new box, +8 units for riders) instead of all of them. Exact by
  construction: clients always candidates (hanging at arm's length), big boxes and edicts allocated this tick
  (ED_Alloc hook) always, every SV_LinkEdict re-inserts, and an edict past the one under test that is linked or
  allocated mid-push re-gathers the rest; visited in edict order with the walk's own tests (riding, VR_ClimbHangsFrom,
  Box3D's skip, corpses). 0 = Quake's walk; 2 = the grid from the first pusher and every push checked against the
  walk (misses warned). `sv_pushgrid_stats [reset]`. Debug > Profiling and Memory: Pusher Search, Pusher Search Stats.
  Checks: sv_fastpushmove 2 on ad_sepulcher (awake monsters, 40 s) 12 pushes, 0 missed; prop_climb_test lift and
  liftlight PASS with 0 and 2, output identical; nav_lift passes with 0, 1 and 2 (its timing varies run to run with
  either: 18.6 / 32.7 / 22.7 s, one fail each way: flaky, not seeded). Idle AD maps (ad_tfuma, ad_azad, e4m7) never
  move two pushers in a tick: the grid is built only on maps with many movers; one door costs Quake's walk as before.
- **Hull trace** (`sv_fte_hulltrace`, default 1; after vkQuake world.c Q1BSP_RecursiveHullTrace, on since 13b4b73a):
  a whole move (fractions 0..1) traced by FTE's recursion; Quake's kept for 0 and for partial calls.
  `sv_hulltrace_compare [n] [seed]`: e1m1/e4m7/dm5, 100000 seeded moves per hull: 0-2 hit/miss differ, 13-24 ends
  more than 1/8 apart, 0 solid-flag differences, 0 ends in solid either way; FTE 28.6 vs 74.1 ms (e1m1 hull 0),
  22.5 vs 42.3 (hull 1), 1.7-3x quicker everywhere. Seeded hull walks (vr_hull_walktest 60 7): e1m3 stuck 0 / 1 hop
  failed both ways, e2m2 and e1m1 stuck 0; vr_portals_walktest dm5 184 carried, 0 walked through with 0 and 1. Some
  hull-walk runs (e3m3, e4m1, one e1m1) ended without their summary line in either mode (harness, not the trace).
  Debug > Profiling and Memory: Hull Trace, Compare Hull Traces.
- **Faces on the job pool** (after vkQuake 64ce1738; gl_model.c): CalcSurfaceExtents and Mod_CalcSurfaceBounds after
  Mod_LoadFaces's loop through `VR_ParallelFor` (a C bridge to jobs::parallelFor, sites in vr_jobs_sites), the
  "Bad surface extents" check after the join. `mod_surfhash`: ad_tears 532b2765, e1m1 64c21f98 with vr_jobs_parallel
  0 and 1. ad_tears: "map faces' extents" 4.5 -> 0.7 ms (vr_startup_times), of a 2.5 s load: alias models (581 ms:
  skins 106, normal maps 248, draw lists 139) are the bigger part; their skins upload through GL on the main thread,
  so vkQuake's parallel skin loading does not carry over; per-model draw lists are the next candidate (not done).
- **Not done:** the A/B benchmark tables (bench.sh --fast --reps 3, exclusive): the author's game was running.
  Settings for them (the agent worktree's scratch): vp_base.cfg (both 0), vp_grid.cfg (grid only), vp_all.cfg (both 1).

## rlvents: the rocket launcher's three vents are real recesses (agent/rlvents, 2026-11-14)

- **What:** the three vents painted at the back of the front shroud (the chevron on the top fin's rear end, an arch on
  each side fin's) are cut into `src_models/blend/v_rock2/v_rock2.blend` (frame 0) and exported with the add-on's
  pipeline (`blend_export.py`): each fin's rear end faces are rebuilt as a rim around an opening traced from the painted
  dark texels (its corners on texel centres, so the rim's skin maps as before), and the opening goes into the fin as a
  recess (walls and a back face, on a black texel of the vent paint). Depth 2.0 units on top, 1.5 on the sides; each
  recess runs along the body's surface under it (top: +x rising 0.12; sides: +x outward 0.121), so it never enters the
  body: the closest point is 0.14 units outside it, the backs 0.24-0.37 inside the fins.
- **Numbers:** 935 -> 1047 triangles (928 kept in place, 119 new), 97 new file vertices; every anchor `ok` (the off
  hand's sits on the left fin's outer corner, kept); holes check: 0 see-through, 0 flipped, cracks 1 -> 2 (0 wide);
  0 texels changed; the normal map re-baked; weapons.txt's `fx_gfx_mask` re-written on the new triangle count. A second
  export of the saved .blend writes the same files byte for byte.
- **The pickup:** map pickups draw the held model (`vr_pickup_prop_models 1`, the default), so they show the vents too;
  the classic `g_rock2.mdl` (vr_pickup_prop_models 0) is a separate low-poly mesh and was left alone.

## nohunk: the hunk and the cache are the heap (agent/nohunk, 2026-11-14)

- **His call:** follow vkQuake (85d526c): no hunk, no cache, plain allocation over mimalloc. **The heap was already
  mimalloc:** vendored in Quake/vr/external/mimalloc (MIT, 1.3 MB of sources, static library, vr_crtheap.c routes the C
  heap to it); `VR_HeapMalloc`/`VR_HeapCalloc` are counted malloc/calloc, so mimalloc's. Nothing to add.
- **Hunk (zone.c):** every `Hunk_Alloc*` is a heap block of its own (an 80-byte header: size, mark, name, sentinel,
  links; a Debug tail word), pushed on a stack. `Hunk_LowMark` is the bytes on the stack, `Hunk_FreeToLowMark` frees the
  blocks pushed since the mark, newest first: every lifetime is as before (the level at Host_ClearMemory, the loaders'
  temporaries at their frees, `Hunk_KeepLoaded` kept), and no call site changed. Gone: the 384 MiB block
  (`DEFAULT_MEMORY`), segments, `-heapsize`/`-minmemory` (a start-up line says they're ignored), `minimum_memory`.
  `Hunk_Check` walks every hunk and cache block (sentinels, Debug tails); `hunk_print [all]` (grouped by name, from the
  bottom) and a new `cache_print`. No Hunk_TempAlloc/HighMark existed (Ironwail had dropped them).
- **Cache:** `Cache_Alloc` is a zeroed heap block, `Cache_Free` frees it, `Cache_Check` is the pointer (no LRU, nothing
  purged or moved: Cache_Move, Cache_FreeLow, Cache_TryAlloc gone); `Cache_Flush` / `Cache_FlushExcept` (a game or
  campaign switch, `flush`) free them. `S_MixJoin` stays before every free.
- **The one contiguity user:** seven loaders built a model on the hunk and copied the range to the cache (`Cache_Alloc
  (end - start); memcpy (hdr); Hunk_FreeToLowMark (start)`: mdl, md3, md5 in gl_model.c; agarmor, agarmor_bridge,
  ragdoll, rig2). Blocks are no longer contiguous, so they call `Hunk_MoveToCache (start, &mod->cache, hdr, name)`: the
  blocks since the mark go to the cache entry (hdr's block its head, the rest owned by it), no copy; aliashdr_t's
  `intptr_t` offsets between blocks stay valid since nothing moves. `texels[]` was an `int` offset: now `intptr_t`;
  the four VR rigs copied their source's texel offsets verbatim (relative to another header): now rebased.
- **Hunk blocks are always zeroed, NoFill too.** With NoFill blocks left as malloc'd, idle_e1m1 drew world+brush 38%
  slower on the GPU (0.56 -> 0.78 ms) and the CPU's screen 0.3 ms slower, reproducibly (two after-runs), and AD/firing
  range maps not at all: something in the world's drawing reads a NoFill block before writing it (the old hunk was
  fresh zero pages). Zeroed, it matches the old numbers exactly (0.561 / 0.559). **Open:** find that read (r_brush.c /
  gl_model.c NoFill users); calloc costs nothing on fresh pages.
- **vr_limits:** "hunk, KiB" (in use / peak, no maximum), "hunk blocks", "cache, KiB" (in use / peak), "cache entries".
  e1m1: hunk 44,137 KiB in 2,591 blocks, cache 67,426 KiB in 308 entries; ad_azad: hunk 85,969 KiB, cache 119,767 KiB.
  **Tracy:** pools Zone/Hunk/Cache kept (the hunk's events per block, `VR_TracyHunkReset` on frees, a hand-over frees the
  blocks' Hunk events and adds one Cache event); the memory test's "cache move" step is now a hand-over test
  (`Tracy cache hand-over test: PASS`); `Memory_TracyCacheMove` gone. Release-Tracy/TracyFull build (not captured).
- **Verified:** Release, ReleaseLTO, Debug, Release-TracyFull 0 warnings. id1 mutator save/load loop 18/0 and
  `pr_knownstrings_check` 44/0; AD loop (ad_crucial, start, ad_swampy: saves, loads, changelevels) no error, 44/0;
  game switch id1 <-> AD (ad_azad / e1m1) 50 round trips: no error, the hunk (2,280 blocks, 45,196,800 bytes) and the
  cache (308 entries, 69,044,320 bytes) identical at cycles 1, 10, ... 50, mimalloc's commit flat (4.4 GB +-0.1);
  `load_models_test.sh` 4/0 (352/0); `scenario_check.sh` 142 files 0 errors, 142 run 0 failed. Debug (MI_DEBUG checks,
  tail guards, hunk_print's Hunk_Check x3): e1m1 save, changelevel, load, `r_enhancedmodels` 0/1 (every alias entry
  with its handed-over blocks freed and rebuilt), `flush`, hip1m1 (campaign switch) and back, `vr_heap test` PASS.
  Debug on ad_azad stops on a Box3D assert (b3HullBuilder_IsConsistent, hull.c:1463, a mover's hull from
  vr_box3d_mesh.cpp solidLeaves): **the same on origin/next's Debug build** (pre-existing, not this change).
  Not run: a Map Library package save/load loop (no package mounted in the agent base outside bench.sh's
  load_ad_grendel, which loaded cold and warm fine). Scripts: scratch/nh_*.sh.
- **Memory** (process, after the map's load; ThinLTO, one run): e1m1 working set 1,048 -> 1,064 MB, commit 3,998 ->
  3,776 MB; e1m2 1,092 -> 1,145 MB, commit 4,061 -> 3,879; ad_azad 1,547 -> 1,585 MB, commit 4,784 -> 4,624 MB. The
  384 MiB block's commit is gone; the cache no longer shares (and evicts from) the hunk's free space, so the touched
  pages rise by about the cache's size past what the hunk had touched. The cache is never purged now (vkQuake's too):
  it grows with the models and sounds a game uses until a game switch.
- **Load times** (vr_startup_times, ms, one run): e1m1 cold 2,146 -> 1,831, warm 201 -> 210; changelevel e1m2 368 ->
  370; ad_azad cold 3,100 -> 2,986, warm 1,840 -> 1,804. bench load_e1m1 (median of 3): cold 1,652 -> 1,665 (+0.8%),
  warm 188 -> 198 (+5.2%); load_ad_grendel cold max frame 66.4 -> 59.5 ms.
- **Bench** (`--fast --reps 3`, exclusive, ThinLTO; labels nh_before (origin/next 5b4685dcb), nh_after3 (zeroed hunk,
  merged)): frame p50 ms combat_48 3.844 -> 3.823 (-0.5%), ai_crowd_64 3.095 -> 3.172 (+2.5%), idle_e1m1 1.464 ->
  1.462, play_ad_tfuma_fight 7.167 -> 7.229 (+0.9%); CPU avg combat_48 +5.1%, the rest within 3%. Read "no change".
  heap_allocs a frame rose (combat_48 10.8 -> 35.0, ai_crowd_64 9.1 -> 35.2, the AD fight 6.2 -> 81.9): the per-frame
  temporary hunk lists (SV_PushMove, SV_TouchLinks, VR physics) are mallocs now. If they ever show in a profile, they
  can move to their files' mem::Scratch. nh_after/nh_after2 are the runs with garbage NoFill blocks (above).

## quest1: standalone Quest plan, SIMD layer, GLES compat mode (agent/quest, 2026-11-14)

Phase C1 of the Quest port (docs/vr-port/QUEST_PLAN.md: research, the audit with file:line, the decision, phases
C2-C7, the install list for his approval). Branch `agent/quest`, not shipped by the coordinator.

- **Decision:** one renderer with an OpenGL ES 3.2 profile (no PC cost: chosen at start-up), Vulkan as the long-term
  path and the fallback. The renderer's GL 4.4/4.5 extras already have fallbacks (safe mode's gates); 14 small groups
  of desktop-only calls remain (`vr_gles_report`). The Quest's real problem is the tiler's budget (full-screen passes,
  multiview into the swapchain for foveation), planned for C5/C6.
- **`Quake/vr/vr_simd.hpp`** (SSE2 / NEON / scalar backends): the AO bake's ray kernel, the audio anti-alias filter and
  the interpolation taps use it, so they build on ARM; the spin wait is Zancle's `ZA_CPU_RELAX`. `vr_simd_test`:
  58880 passed, 0 failed (SSE2 against scalar, bit for bit). Audio goldens bit-identical before/after; `vr_ao_bench
  sse reference soldier` the same bytes. NEON compiled for aarch64-linux-android with the PC's clang (not run yet).
- **`-glescompat`** (`QVR_GLES_COMPAT=1` for bench.sh): bindless, multi-bind, clip control, layered casters and NV
  foveation off; `VR_GLESCompat()` for C2's gates; `vr_gles_report` lists the live switches and the pending rows.
- `Misc/quakevr/bench/quest_budget.cfg` (Quest-like settings for budget runs), `Misc/quakevr/gles_audit.py` (the
  audit's counts). Budget runs (QUEST_PLAN.md section 6): the Quest-like settings halve the eyes' GPU time on the PC;
  the GLES profile adds 15-60% back (layered casters, bindless, clip control off), to split in C2.
- Not done: anything that needs an install (NDK, SDK, loader): C3 onwards.
## mp1: multiplayer audit, plan and test harness (agent/mp, 2026-11-14; never shipped by the coordinator)

- **docs/vr-port/MP_PLAN.md**: the state re-verified against the code and with real runs (what works, what is broken,
  what is missing, file:line), the research (NetQuake, QuakeWorld/ezQuake, FTE/QSS/Quakespasm-VR, DarkPlaces, Q3,
  rollback, VR multiplayer games), the chosen architecture (server authority, owner-authoritative head and hands,
  acked per-client snapshots and deltas, a VR player-state block drawn with the armed humanoids' arm solver,
  prediction of the local player, lag compensation, rules/preferences/cosmetics, layered compression, downloads through
  the map installer), the bandwidth budget, risks, phases B2-B13. MULTIPLAYER.md points at it.
- **The harness** (`Misc/quakevr/mp/`: `mp_harness.py`, `mp_proxy.py`, `mp_test.py`; MP_PLAN.md section 4): a hidden
  dedicated server or listen host plus clients (VR mock or flat), each with its own log (`-condebugfile`) and command
  inbox (`-cmdinbox`), driven by Python with waits on log conditions; a UDP proxy adds lag, jitter and loss and counts
  bytes. Engine aids in `Quake/vr/vr_mptest.cpp`: `vr_mp_watch` (wall-clock stamped joins, sightings, moves),
  `vr_mp_mark`, `vr_mp_status` (Debug > Reports: Network: Players Seen, Network: Watch Players).
- **Fixed:** a second client from the same IP (another port) closed the first one's connection (NetQuake's "back from
  a crash" rule, `net_dgrm.c`): two players behind one router could not both play. A hidden test run's dedicated
  server no longer opens a console window.
- **Found** (B2's work): the armed humanoids' arm poses are broadcast to every client every frame, unculled (about
  1.2 KB of each 1.4 KB datagram on e1m1: 97 KB/s down for two idle players); the move is 640 B (45 KB/s up);
  reliable messages go out in datagrams up to 64 KB (15 KB seen at signon).
- **Results:** `mp_test.py suite`: 11/11 and 11/11 (no lag; B at 150 ms each way and 2% loss); a listen host with a
  flat B: 10/10. Others' moves seen 40-64 ms after the input on loopback, 206-221 ms with 150 ms added; a player sees
  himself move a round trip late (no prediction yet): 357-368 ms at 150 ms each way.

## mpN (B2): protocol hygiene, culled poses, player avatars (agent/mp, 2026-11-14; never shipped by the coordinator)

MP_PLAN.md, "B2 results", has the details and numbers. In short:

- Reliable messages go out in 1200 B chunks, 16 in flight (`net_dgrm.c`), not one datagram of up to 64 KB; peers
  unchanged either way. The connect request carries Quake VR's network version (`QVR_NET_VERSION` 2): a VR server
  rejects another, with the reason.
- Every move since the server's last frame counts (buttons and VR bits ORed); a slot's move state is reset on connect
  and drop. Single player too: a press and release between two 72 Hz ticks (a 90 Hz headset) was lost.
- Armed humanoids' poses go only to the remote clients whose PVS has them (`vr_net_cullposes` 1, Debug > Reports >
  Network: Cull Poses); the loopback client gets them all. A coop client idle on e1m1: down 15.5 KB/s, was 97.
- Each player's head, hands and weapons reach the clients that see him (`QVR_SVC_AVATAR`, `vr_mpavatar.cpp`,
  `vr_mp_avatars`); not drawn yet (B2b).
- Harness: `mp_test.py bandwidth | version | avatar`, all in `suite` (5 scenarios, all pass).

## hunkfollow: nohunk's two follow-ups (agent/hunkfollow, 2026-11-14)

- **The uninitialised read (nohunk's "Open"):** `vr_extmaps.cpp` `signature()` (the 64 x 64 detail signatures that
  decide whether an animated texture's frames are one surface: `frameMatchRun`, VR_AnimSurfaces) read past the end of
  its `tmp` buffer: the optimised code for the blur's `& (sigSize - 1)` wrap gave row 0's cells 1-3 a term or two from
  after `tmp` (a 1000-filled guard region after it moved them by 40-80; the same formula written out by hand, and the
  fixed code, don't). With zeroed memory after the block that was a small error; with a reused heap block's garbage
  (about -1e19) the same huge value landed in both frames' signatures, every correlation came out 1.000 (moved 0.7998),
  so every animated texture's frames shared one surface, and E1M1's world+brush drew 38% slower. Found by bisecting:
  NoFill blocks filled with garbage (not zeroed) per call site, idle_e1m1's world+brush GPU time each (0.77 ms with
  vr_extmaps' blocks garbage, 0.56 with any other site's); a 0xCD fill didn't reproduce it (what lay after the block
  was what mattered). Fixed: the wrap is a modulo (`(y + dy + sigSize) % sigSize`, a row pointer). After it, garbage
  NoFill blocks draw the same: world+brush 0.562 (zeroed) / 0.560 (garbage) / 0.559 (0xCD).
- **Hunk blocks stay zeroed:** not zeroing NoFill blocks gained nothing measurable: load_e1m1 (3 reps, median) cold
  1,832 vs 1,807 ms, warm 191 vs 189 / 161 vs 163 ms: noise. calloc costs nothing on fresh pages; zone.c says why.
- **Temporary stack (zone.h, `Temp_Mark` / `Temp_Alloc` / `Temp_FreeToMark`):** the per-frame lists that were hunk
  temporaries (one heap block each since nohunk) go on grow-only chunks kept between uses (256 KiB first, each next
  twice as big up to 64 MiB, a chunk remade larger when a list doesn't fit; marks nest like the hunk's, across chunks).
  Users: `SV_TouchLinks`, `SV_PushMove`, the three VR touch lists in vr_physics.cpp (`VR_TouchLinks` and the two
  hand/weapon finds), `R_DrawSkeleton`. Host_Error / Host_EndGame (a touch's QuakeC erring mid-list) and
  Host_ClearMemory empty it. `hunk_print` shows its chunks and peak; `vr_heap test` also runs `vr_temp test` (nested
  marks over three chunks, a larger chunk, contents kept below a mark, no heap call warm: PASS). Late precaches from
  those touches no longer happen inside a hunk temporary (Hunk_KeepLoaded stays for any other).
- **Heap calls a frame** (vr_alloc_sites 300 frames, main thread, events incl. frees): combat_48 9.9 a frame (the
  rest is `new`/`delete`, 0.16 malloc); the AD fight 8.1, all Box3D's own (b3ComputeMeshManifolds, hull creation)
  which the old 6.2 also had.
- **Bench** (`--fast --reps 3`, exclusive, ThinLTO; before: nohunk's nh_after3 run, origin/next with zeroed hunk
  blocks; after: hf_after): frame p50 ms combat_48 3.823 -> 3.481 (-9%), ai_crowd_64 3.172 -> 3.115, idle_e1m1
  1.462 -> 1.457, play_ad_tfuma_fight 7.229 -> 6.747 (-7%); combat_48 p99 8.75 -> 5.92, max 36.8 -> 10.1. Heap allocs a
  frame (bench heap/fr): combat_48 35.0 -> 10.5 (pre-nohunk 10.8), ai_crowd_64 35.2 -> 9.2 (9.1), idle_e1m1 2.3 -> 0.8
  (0.8), the AD fight 81.9 -> 6.2 (6.2).
- **Verified** (merged with origin/next): Release 0 warnings; load_models_test 4/0; id1 mutator save/load loop 18/0 and
  `pr_knownstrings_check` 44/0; AD loop (ad_crucial, start, ad_swampy: saves, loads, changelevels) no error, 44/0;
  `scenario_check.sh` 129 files 0 errors, 129 run 0 failed; Debug (MI_DEBUG, tail guards, Hunk_Check): e1m1 save,
  changelevel, load, the firing range with spawned monsters, `vr_heap test` and `vr_temp test` PASS, no error (the
  temporary stack's peak there: 12,672 bytes in its one 256 KiB chunk); the release configuration (MSBuild ReleaseLTO,
  QvrReleaseVersion=1.1.0) builds with no error or warning.
- Scripts: scratch/hf_*.sh, hf_*.py (hf_bisect.sh: the per-site bisection; the fill switch was temporary, removed).

## Quest C2a: every program as ES 3.2 GLSL under -glescompat, the first ES call forms (branch agent/quest, 2026-11-14)

- **What:** `-glescompat` (or `QVR_GLES_COMPAT=1`) now compiles every shader as `#version 320 es` with precisions
  (`VR_GLShaderSource`, vr_glsafe.cpp: the one glShaderSource for the engine and the VR passes), so the PC's NVIDIA
  driver checks them the way an ES driver would; a failure there is printed and counted (`vr_gles_report`), not
  fatal; `-glesverbose` prints each error with its source line. The GLSL was made ES-valid (229 failing programs to
  0) without changing what the desktop compiles to; ES-only image formats (`VR_GLESImageFormat`); NIS off on ES.
  ES forms of glGetBufferSubData, glClearTexImage, glDrawBuffer, glClearDepth/glDepthRange, glPolygonMode
  (`gfx::readBuffer`, `gfx::clearTexture`, `gfx::drawNoColour`, the float forms, `VR_GLPolygonMode`). No PC default
  or behaviour changes without the flag. Details and open items: QUEST_PLAN.md section 5b.
- **PC fix (own commit):** the particles' `Support[16]` overlapped the fragment shader's `Taper`/`InkAlpha` uniform
  locations (20, 21): a link error on a strict linker; now 40-55.

  back the same both ways (hash 0b34a576). PC: scenario_check 129/0, load_models_test 4/0, vr_simd_test 58880/0.

## loadhang: vr_runpickups_test's "hang" at its last load (agent/loadhang, 2026-11-14)
- No engine hang. cdb (Windows Kits, `-pvr`: attached without suspending) at the "hang": host_framecount, sv.qcvm.time
  and cl.time kept advancing, signon 4, sv.paused 0; the main thread's stacks moved through server frames, physics and
  rendering. The test had finished: its last step runs just after `load mp_rpk_seed`, and its verdict was a dprint
  (VR_Test_Print without VR_TEST_LOUD), never printed at developer 0, so run.sh's -QuitOn waited out its timeout. A
  broadcast would not do either: that step runs between the client's spawn and begin, and SV_BroadcastPrintf skips a
  client not yet spawned.
- Fix (QC, tests only): `VR_TEST_ECHO` (vr_testutil.qc): VR_Test_Verdict echoes its line through the console
  (`localcmd echo`), seen at developer 0 whatever the client's state; VR_RT_End (vr_runpickups_test, vr_ironman_test)
  sets it.
- At developer 1 the test also failed 7 checks since 5daa7d776 (a typed `map` is a new game: the Run Setup screen's
  picks and a new seed): steps 2 and 6 now set `vr_run pickups 1` before their `map`, as a run's own map loads do
  (runSet keeps the run and its seed).
- Checks: vr_runpickups_test 1 32/0 five times at developer 0 and once at developer 1 (each ends on its verdict),
  vr_ironman_test 1 12/0, load_models_test 4/0. No engine change, so no watchdog line; scenario_check not rerun (no
  game or engine code touched).

## questN: Quest C2f, the world's textures in texture arrays for the bound path (agent/quest, 2026-11-14)

- **`vr_world_texarrays`** (tunable: 0 off, 1 under the ES profile (default), 2 any bound path; the PC with bindless
  never uses it) and `vr_world_texarrays_report`. vr/vr_worldarrays.cpp makes, at each map's load, sets of four
  `GL_TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY`s (texture, fullbright, normal, specular) for the world's textures alike in size, levels and
  format (`glCopyImageSubData` copies: mips, external packs, generated normal maps; shared defaults one layer); each
  call is checked against the maps copied (a changed map: the bound path that frame, the arrays made again).
- **Draws**: the world programs' array twins (`QVR_WORLD_ARRAYS`, gl_shaders.c `GL_WorldArraysProgram`; the retro,
  parallax and bump helpers spliced for both sampler types by `QVR_SAMPLER_TWINS`); r_world.c groups a flush's calls
  by set and draws each group's single-instance calls as one draw: their indices merged by a compute pass beside the
  gather (same barrier), each vertex's call from a static vertex-to-command buffer (r_brush.c) and the flush's
  command-to-call table. The liquids' programs keep a draw a texture.
- **Numbers** (idle e1m1, ES + clip control + `vr_quest_preset 0`): world+brush 118 -> 25 draws an eye, eye 151 -> 58;
  25 sets, 77 textures, 8.9 MB of copies. The eye identical with and without (also at PC defaults with normal maps and
  PBR companions). This PC's GPU and CPU unchanged within
  noise (8 core scenarios, ThinLTO; two repeats where it looked moved); a twin compiled in play (1.8 s frame) fixed by
  compiling them at the arrays' making.
- **Tests**: `gles_render_test` 18 checks (6 new: the arrays drawn, off draws none, identical to a draw a texture).

## uafsweep: dangling pointers after the hunk/cache removal; crowd_ad_40's p99 (agent/uafsweep, 2026-11-14)

- **`-memguard` / `QVR_MEMGUARD=1`** (zone.c, vr_alloccount.cpp `VR_PageGuardAlloc/Free`; a debugging aid, off by
  default, a start-up line and `hunk_print`'s USED line say when on): every zone, hunk and cache block on pages of its
  own, ending at its last page's end (the next page reserved: an overrun faults); its free decommits the pages and
  keeps them reserved, so the address is never reused and any later use through a kept pointer faults with that use's
  stack in the crash report. The environment variable reaches every child game (bench.sh, scenario_check.sh, ...).
  Release builds suffice (no debug-CRT dialogs). Proven on the known bug: with `cl_entities = NULL` undone, `map e1m1;
  map uf_nosuchmap; map hip1m1` (a failed map after Host_ClearMemory, then a campaign switch) faults at
  CL_ForgetModels (cl_main.c:153); load_reloads didn't fault (it never leaves a failed map before a switch).
- **Found and fixed:** `Mod_DecompressVis` read past the end of a map's vis data: a last row cut short by the compiler
  (e1m3, vrteleporters: Mod_CheckWaterVis at load) read the bytes after the block; harmless in the old one-block hunk
  (the next allocation's bytes), heap garbage since nohunk (wrong PVS bits for that leaf), a fault under -memguard.
  `qmodel_t.visdatasize` now bounds it; the rest of a cut row is zeros. No other hit.
- **Runs under -memguard** (Release): the id1 <-> AD switch loop 30 round trips (scratch/uf_gen.py: `game ad quakevr;
  map ad_azad` / `game quakevr; map e1m1`, with failed maps after Host_ClearMemory and campaign switches from there,
  disconnect + hip1m1, `flush` and `r_enhancedmodels 0/1` under a running map, restart, save/load, changelevel; 90 game
  changes) no fault; scenario_check 129 files 0 errors, 129 run 0 failed; load_models_test 4/0 (352/0); vr_run_check
  15/0 and runenemies 17/0 (mr_tests' runcheck script); load_reloads, load_changelevel, load_hip1m1, load_ad_restarts,
  saveload_e1m1 (their bench scripts, 120 frames) no fault, every load reported. A grep of the file-scope pointers to
  models and level data: the VR systems' cached world pointers (vr_envmap, vr_detail, vr_lighting, ...) already check
  `worldGeneration()`; the switch is a start-up option, so no Debug menu row.
- **crowd_ad_40's p99 (6.6 -> 9.6 ms): not a CPU cost but GPU back-pressure in the bench's unpaced `--fast` mode.**
  The hitch log (`vr_profile 1; vr_profile_hitch 0.8`, exclusive, ThinLTO, 2048 eyes) has ~15 window frames of 6-10 ms
  spent in `screen`'s own time (no child scope: the driver blocking the submit) and nothing else unusual. With 512
  eyes (same CPU work): p99 12.2 -> 6.2 ms and those frames gone. Paced at 90 Hz (`-RealTime`, as in the headset): CPU
  busy p99 6.8 ms, frame p99 11.37 (the 11.1 budget). The day's work made the CPU faster (median -12%) than the GPU's
  3.2-3.5 ms a frame, so unpaced frames now outrun the GPU and wait on it in bursts. The fight also plays differently
  (fewer bodies and particles) since a31689eab (every move since the last server tick counts: the bench's +attack
  presses land differently at 90 Hz input over 72 Hz ticks). Nothing to fix; for CPU p99s in --fast, read cpu_busy with
  the GPU unsaturated (a smaller --eye) or a paced run. Scripts: scratch/uf_crowd.sh, uf_hitch2.py.

## perfpicks: his five performance calls (branch agent/perfpicks, 2026-11-14; partial: see "Left")

- **Navmesh, big maps** (`1bc1a031a`, NAVMESH.md 20 "Big maps"): a class's first props' batch lands on
  `vr_nav_job_frames_first` (45, at least `vr_nav_job_frames`); a class's build or disk read on `vr_nav_build_frames` +
  the map's navmesh triangles / `vr_nav_build_frames_tris` (10,000; ad_tears 1.15 M -> 133 frames). Pure functions of
  the map and the game's events; the main thread still waits for a job late on its frame. `vr_nav_info` prints them.
  Decision: the scaled frame applies to every pool build (the load's classes too, which hitch the same way on a first
  play), not only those started in play.
- **Ragdolls** (`215487499`): `vr_ragdoll_per_frame` 4 new ragdolls a server frame (`syncEntities`), the rest in
  `World::ragdollQueue`, oldest death first; a queued corpse has no body until its turn; knockdowns at once; 0 no limit.
- **Armed humanoids' pose** (`220fc2240`). Profiled first (`profile_qc`, fast mode, nav_hunt_e1m1_3x, before: QuakeC
  5.14 ms a frame with the profiler on; prop think 3.76 incl.; `VR_AGP_Pose` 0.52 self / 2.49 incl. for 77,
  `VR_WP_Place` 0.34, `VR_AGP_TurnDir` 0.28 (532 calls), `VR_AM_Row` 0.10 (1,280 calls), `modelvertex` 0.11 (772)).
  Changes: `vr_agrunt_pose_lod` 1 (a holder no player can see, past `vr_agrunt_pose_lod_near` 384 and outside
  `vr_agrunt_pose_lod_cone` 80 degrees of each player's v_angle, doing nothing timed: no act, aim, guard, take, studio,
  posed every other server frame, its weapons carried by its move between: QC `VR_AGP_Lod`/`VR_AGP_LodCarry`);
  `vr_worn_backpack_lod_near` 1500 (a far unseen worn pack not placed that frame); builtin `unseenfar(e, near)` (C++,
  the players' server state only: multiplayer-safe); `VR_AM_Row` returns at once for the row it holds (`nosave`
  flag: a save keeps no vectors); `VR_AGP_TurnDir`'s cosines and sines kept per turn and its rotation in builtin
  `turnrpy` (QC's float steps in order, no FMA: bit for bit). Pose tests `vr_agrunt_test` 83, 84, 99, 79: all pass
  and their agtest lines are identical with the LOD on and off (fingerprints 835cdbe3, 721e80a4, 942267e5, 60ff0e05).
- **Disk cache** (`1a95237d3`): `write` no longer prepares the folder on the main thread; the job calls `prepare`,
  which now holds a per-product lock through the prune and `createDirectories` (no write before its folder exists or
  during the prune).
- **Before bench** (ThinLTO, `--fast --reps 3`, exclusive; `kit/benchresults/pp_before`): fight_ad_tears max frame
  140 / 26 / 24 ms, nav_hunt_e1m1_3x CPU p50 6.29-6.44, p99 12.5-13.4, combat_48 p50 3.6-3.9, ragdolls_32_active max

## Reset This Page and changes on the weapon and prop pages (branch agent/pagereset, 2026-11-15)

His 11-15 note: he changed the shotgun's two-handed hotspot by accident and had no way back. Every page with settings
now has the footer's Reset This Page (two presses within 3 seconds), the weapon and prop pages too (`slotPage`: the
Weapon Offsets main page and its parts, Weapon Weights, Held Object Offsets and Weights), which had none.

- **Reset This Page on a weapon or prop page** resets the rows shown, as on any page: the page's weapon's (or prop's)
  values back to that slot's own default (its `vr_wofs_*_NN` / `vr_prop_*_NN` stand-in's default: weapons.txt's,
  props.txt's), the slot the page edits (an inheriting weapon's page edits its parent's: those). On Two-Handed and
  Hotspots only the hotspot shown (the others stay); on Holstered only the holster kind shown. The page's other settings
  (Show Hotspots, Preview in Holster, the Weapon Weights page's global weight rows) go back too. Reset This Weapon,
  Holstered Back to 0 and the rest stay as they were. The page is rebuilt after (`slotPageReset`: a hotspot's type).
- **The menus' own state:** the Hotspot and Holster pickers (`vr_weapon_hotspot`, `vr_weapon_holster`) are no longer
  "changed" settings: no `*`, not on Changed Settings, never reset.
- **The `*`** by a changed row already compared with the stand-in's default (the slot's): unchanged.
- **Changed Settings** lists every weapon's and prop's changed values, not just the held one's, each under a header
  "Weapon: progs/v_shot.mdl (_02)" / "Prop: maps/b_explob.bsp (_01)", labelled by part ("Hand and Grip: Offset X
  (forward)", "Muzzle and Sights: Muzzle X", "Weight: Mass"), a hotspot's "Hotspot 2: Hotspot X", a holster's "Hip:
  Holstered X (off body)"; each row the page's own (its range, its help), changed or put back there.
  `listSlotChanges` (vr_menu_wofs.inc) builds each changed slot's pages for it (`SlotListing`: the slot, each hotspot,
  each holster kind; the pages' titles into their own strings, the pages' state put back after), skipping inheriting
  slots (listed under the parent) and Inherit From (its choices are the page's texts). A changed value no page variant
  shows (a manual curl while Fingers is Automatic) isn't listed; Reset This Weapon still resets it. The weapon pages'
  other settings stay under their page's title.
- **Test:** `Misc/quakevr/menu_pagereset_test.sh <agent>` (`menu_vr pageresettest`; the weapon pages pinned to the
  shotgun's slot, `pinSlotPages`: no map): hotspot 1 X changed -> `*`, on Changed Settings under the shotgun ->
  Reset This Page on Two-Handed restores the weapons.txt default; hotspot 2 X, Shot Pitch (another page), the
  nailgun's hotspot and the picker kept; a prop's Mass listed under its name. 14/0.
- **Audit** (pages with values): every VR menu page with a setting row gets Reset This Page from `addMenuDetail` (Debug,
  Tunables, the Armour Studio menu page, the presets' pages...); none other was left out. Without one, by design: Search,
  Console and Maps (drawn their own way), Changed Settings (the list itself), the presets' choices (as before). The
  studios' own windows (Weapon Studio, Rig Studio, Armour Studio's window, Pose Studio, the blade editor) are not menu
  pages: they keep their own resets (reset this slot, Reset This Pose, Reset Part/Kind, Reset Pose/Grips, Reset Blade)
  and draw no `*`; the weapon values they change show on Changed Settings now.

## palmgrab: closing a hand on a gun resting on or against it (branch agent/palmgrab, 2026-11-15)

His design (2026-11-15; MP_PLAN B3c, agent/mp's 0a203126f, whose 12 cm `vr_weapon_palm_grab_slack` is NOT taken): a
hand closing on a gun that rests on or leans against that hand's Box3D body (the open hand; a gun on the open palm sits
3-5 cm over the fist that closes under it) takes it, with no reach beyond the fist's anywhere:
- The fist reaches it (the same test as before: `held::grabTouch` with `vr_weapon_grab_slack`, the handle's
  `vr_weapon_grab_handle_leniency` / `vr_weapon_catch_handle_leniency`): as before, by the handle within
  `vr_weapon_grab_anywhere_min` (gun mode), a hotspot, or anywhere on it.
- The fist doesn't reach it but it is on or against the hand (`box3d::restsOnHand(..., minUp -2)`: any contact with the
  hand's body): taken where it lies against the hand, as a prop, anywhere on it (`twohand::anywhereSpot`: carried,
  QVR_WPNFLAG_FOREGRIP_CARRIED), never moved onto its handle or a hotspot the fist doesn't reach.
- Neither: nothing (a hand closing a few centimetres off a gun takes nothing, as before).

Code: `vr_physics.cpp` onWeapon (the slack computation split out as `weaponGrabSlack`; `weaponAgainstHand`), the view's
choice in `vr_view_hands.cpp` updateGroundSpots through `physics::weaponOnHandOnly` (one test, both sides).

player's hand has no anywhere hold: it takes handles only, as before), and only with `vr_weapon_grab_anywhere` on.

## Directional parry timing: the right direction always parries (branch `agent/parrytime`)

His rule (2026-11-15): "As long as the direction of the player's gun/sword/etc is correct for a directional parry, it should
count as a valid parry. But if it's early or late, the stagger effect should be severely diminished, as we want to reward
well-timed parries."

- **Test 78's 28/19 was not the parry.** It fails only when run with no `map vrtesthall` first (the bisect's and the
  queue's runs: `-Script "vr_agrunt_test 78"`), so the test ran in `vrstart`: the posed sword misses its axis (along it 0.66
  instead of 1.00) and the grunt stands 58 units off instead of 37, so every parry case fails, held early or not (the
  dog bite and case 9 included). On `next` with the map, drawn and undrawn: 47/0, as every baseline since 11-06 (11-06,
  11-12, 11-13, 11-14). The bisect's "first bad commit" 87172b999 changes only BACKLOG.md: noise from that. No commit broke it.
  The test now ends at once with one FAIL ("needs map vrtesthall first") anywhere else.
- **How early "held early" is** (the weapon held across from before the attack; the reference blow's time from its
  attack's start): an armed grunt's overhead 0.38 s, a knight's chop 0.50, an ogre's swing 0.40, smash 0.50 (its blade
  0.85), a fiend's claw 0.40, a shambler's smash 0.90, a dog's bite 0.31. The windows: well timed = in place at most
  `vr_dirparry_timed_window` 0.3 s before the contact; `vr_dirparry_stroke` 0.45 s = how long a monster's own blow is held
  back for its blade to reach your weapon (not a timing window); an armed humanoid's `vr_dirparry_window` 0.1 s.
- **What changed.** `VR_DRP_Timing` (vr_dirparry.qc), the one function for every directional parry (monsters' own blows,
  armed humanoids' swings; PvP later the same): the right direction parries at any timing, nothing through (as before).
  Its share (`VR_DRP_TimingShare`) is 1 when your weapon got in place within the timing window and, for a blow held back for
  your weapon, by its own moment (when its blade reaches your weapon's place, read along its way at the blow) plus
  `vr_dirparry_late_grace`; earlier or later it falls smoothly (smoothstep) to `vr_dirparry_offtime`. The share scales the
  parry's stagger and flinch (`VR_Parry_Interrupt`, the armed humanoid's opening flinch), its push on the attacker, the
  counter window and an armed humanoid's disarm chance (`VR_Parry_TimingShare`, combat.qc; 1 for the guard, crossed arms
  and flat-screen guard). "Well timed" (x1.3 strength) is unchanged.
- **Tunables** (Debug > Tunables > Combat > Directional Parry): `vr_dirparry_offtime` 0.2 (Early/Late Stagger),
  `vr_dirparry_offtime_fade` 0.15 s (Early Fade), `vr_dirparry_late_grace` 0.02 s, `vr_dirparry_late_fade` 0.06 s.
  So held 0.45 s or more before the contact: x0.2; 0.375 s: x0.6.
- **Test 78** (48 cases): held early now asks for a share of at most 0.5 (measured 0.2; the armed grunt's 0.39, in place
  0.40 s before), moved/turned in a share of 1, moved in staggering at least 1.5x held early (knight 1.10 s vs 0.16, armed
  grunt 1.50 vs 0.58); a last case checks the share's curve (full, the fades' middles 0.60, the floor, never rising).
  Case 12 no longer compares its swing's end (it ends with its parry's flinch, now as long as the share makes it).
  48/0; 35 6/0, 18 24/0, 60 6/0.
- **Not covered by a test:** a late parry end to end (an armed humanoid's held blow can be late by 0.1 s at most; a
  monster's by up to 0.45 s): the scene `parrytime` (an ogre and a sword grunt) is for him; `developer 1` prints
  `dirparry: timing: in place X s before, Y s late: xS`.
## flat1115b: flat aim per weapon (ironsight placing, zoom), Classic in flat, Autosave Now (agent/flat1115b, 2026-11-15)

- **Ironsight placing per gun (his item 5).** There were none: the flat ironsight is solved from each gun's sight line with
  no number per weapon (the old `flat_ads_*` keys were retired 2026-11-05); only the globals (`vr_flat_ads_relief`,
  `_screen_x/_y`, `vr_flat_aim_fov`) moved it. New weapons.txt keys `fsight_fwd`, `fsight_right`, `fsight_up` (units in the
  view's frame, forward adds eye relief; clamped to 10) and `fsight_pitch` (degrees, muzzle up about the rear sight; 20),
  applied in `flatsight::sighted` so the reach, stance and wall code all see the moved gun; shots still go to the
  crosshair's point. Live: Weapon Offsets > Sights > Flat-Screen Aim (the held gun) or `vr_wofs_fsight_up_NN` on the
  console; saved as config overrides, `weapons_data.py promote` makes them defaults. All 0 shipped.
- **Zoom per gun (item 6).** `fsight_mode` 1: the right button narrows the view exactly as the ironsight does (same
  `st.adsT` travel, FOV, look speed) but the gun stays in its pose and the crosshair stays. Shared code, one switch:
  `sightPosed` / `posedT` in vr_flatsight.cpp gate everything that moves the gun or reads the sighted pose (the solve, the
  wall's back way and tilt, the stance's armSight, keepRecoil, crosshairFade, the picture's screen shift, stance turn and
  lean), and `flatsight::poseShare` replaces `adsShare` in flatplay's keepNear, rideShare and walk bob. `adsShare` (the
  FOV and sensitivity travel) is unchanged. Zoom picks (weapons.txt, promoted with `weapons_data.py promote`): nailgun,
  super nailgun, grenade launcher, rocket launcher, laser cannon, proximity gun, grapple (slots 3,4,5,6,9,10,17; the
  alternates 11-14 inherit). Ironsight kept: shotguns, lightning/plasma, grunt gun, enforcer rifle, flare gun, revolver,
  nail pistol, crossbow, AD guns. Global override `vr_flat_aim_zoom` (-1 per weapon, 0 all ironsight, 1 all zoom),
  Locomotion > Right Click Aim. `vr_flat_sight_check` prints a `zoom` line for a zoom gun.
- **Classic in flat (item 7).** Flat play reloads by its own `vr_flat_reload` (QC `VRIsWeaponReloadingEnabled`, the

  the player reloads nothing as played (flat or VR).
- **Autosave Now (item 11).** `vr_autosave_now` (host.c, beside Host_CheckAutosave; Debug > Tests > Saves): the game's

## Quest C4c: the black world on the headset, first part (branch `agent/quest`, 2026-11-14)

QUEST_PLAN.md section 6j has the detail. On the Quest 3 over adb, with the headset unworn:
- **OpenGL ES errors that Adreno reports (`-gldebug`) and a desktop driver under `-glescompat` accepts, fixed:** TexMgr
  uploads from `GL_RGB`/`GL_RG8` internal formats are now RGBA8 under the ES profile, so every texture uploads; the
  light-cluster and palette-LUT image textures are now immutable (`glTexStorage3D`); eyeshots read back as RGBA; the
  depth-only array/multiview twins now get an empty fragment shader. After the fixes, `-gldebug` shows no error in a frame.
- **Android:** `EXT_clip_control` is used when the driver has it (the Quest 3 does; `-glesnoclipcontrol` turns it
  off). While VR runs there is no window image and no swap (`vr_android_window` 0). The APK is debuggable.
- **New debug tools (Debug > Startup):** `vr_gl_probe 1` (the eye framebuffers by numbers, the scene's primitives,
  the frame data's upload read back, a clear-and-read self-test) and `vr_android_export <path>` (files copied to where
  `adb shell run-as` reads them).
- **Still black:** the eye's composite is 0% non-black even though the scene draws 31-35 k primitives, the frame
  UBO uploads byte for byte and the self-test reads back. The vertex side is fine, so the next suspects are on the
  fragment side (depth/stencil state, the world fragment shader's inputs). The PC's ES mode draws the same scene.
- **"Save error."** is Android only and now says why: e1m1's autosave hits "string -14: a freed engine string".
- PC unchanged: every change is behind the ES profile or `__ANDROID__`, except that eyeshots now read RGBA (same files)
  and "Save error." gives a reason.

## The detailed ranger head on the body (worktree `takeslight`, branch `agent/rangerhead`, 2026-11-14)

His ask (2026-11-15): Dawn of the Machine's ranger corpses (its `start` map) have a nicer, more detailed head: use it
on our body. **What the corpse is**: `misc_corpse` with styles 17..22 (`vr_mg_corpses.qc`: `progs/player.mdl` frames
49..102). No player model ships in MG3's pak, and in Quake VR `progs/player.mdl` is Quake VR's own
(`quakevr/progs/player.mdl`: 733 vertices, 1062 triangles, a 256 x 256 skin, 144 unnamed frames; the quakevr folder is
the highest on MG3's path). So the head he saw is ours, shipped already: nothing of the re-release is needed or read.
(KEX itself draws the re-release's `id1/progs/player.md5mesh`: 945 vertices, 26 joints with Head/Neck, a 256 x 256
`player_00_00.lmp`; reference only.) Its "rigs and ragdolls" are ours too: the player ragdoll rig (`player_bones.json`,
11 bones from the same model; its head bone is cluster 5, these two islands); the corpses already ragdoll with it, and
`limbmodel` can already cut its head as a limb (`progs/player.mdl#limb<head>`) for player gibs later.

**Comparison** (offline flat renders, same light: `qvr-kit/scratch/rangerhead_shots/heads_compare.png`): Quake's head
27 triangles, 8.5 x 7.5 units, a 296 x 194 skin; Quake VR's 131 triangles in two islands of their own (a hood with ear
guards, 89; a sculpted face, 42), 8.1 x 9.5 units, its own 256 x 256 skin's islands (s 88..252, t 61..142): too spread
over the skin to paint into the body's 512 x 57-texel head block as Quake's is.

**Built** (`vr_rangerhead.cpp`): `vr_body_ranger_head_model` (new, archived, default 1; Appearance > Ranger Head >
*Detailed Head*; latched at the next start like `vr_body_ranger_head`). 1: the first `progs/player.mdl` like Quake VR's
(400..3000 vertices, frame 13 = stand1 40..70 units tall), its islands wholly above 0.2 of the height from the top
(the next island down is 9.8 units lower), else Quake's head as before (0 too), else the placeholder.
- The body's mesh: the placeholder's head triangles dropped and the neck's top ring narrowed as before; his head is
  not added there but as a mesh of its own after the body's (and the bare bodies' cuff shell): `VR_RangerHeadExtend`
  appends it to the body's md5 text (shader `vrrangerhead`, every vertex the `head` joint's), `VR_RangerHeadMesh` (now
  told the mesh number) places it in the bind pose (1.05 x the placeholder's width, bottom 1.5 units below it) and
  `VR_RangerHeadSkins` gives it his own skin (palette indices from his file, kept for the session, one persistent
  texture for every body and skin number). So every draw of the body has it as it had the old one: the eye views
  collapse it with the head joint, the mirror clone, third person, shadows, other players' bodies.
- The Ranger Head page's sliders (size, sink, place, turn) place it live as they did Quake's (its vertices rewritten
  in its own mesh, the neck ring in the body's).
- `VR_AliasSurfaceNext` (bodies with the cuff shell) now draws meshes after the shells; `vr_wounds` accepts a body
  with the head's mesh (its masks are the body's; the head reads them at its own texels: a known imperfection).
- `vr_body_head_check <detailed|classic|off>` (verdict `rangerhead_check: N passed, M failed`); `-rangerhead_nodetail`
  makes the detailed search fail (the fallback test).

**Verified** (mock, `map start`): "the detailed head of .../quakevr/progs/player.mdl (131 triangles, 100 vertices)",
both bodies loaded (vrbody, vrbody_bare) with his mesh and skin, `vr_body_head_check detailed` 3/0; with
`-rangerhead_nodetail`: Quake's head painted on, `vr_body_head_check classic` 3/0. Shots front/side/back:
`rangerhead_shots/detailed_ingame.png`, `classic_fallback.png`. Dev build 0 warnings.

For him in VR: a mirror or the Ranger Head page's clone: its size and height over the neck (Size/Neck Sink apply to it),
front, side, back; nothing of it in your own view when looking down or leaning.
## classic3: Classic recoil, no enemy weapon drops, the burst rifle always bursts (agent/classic3, 2026-11-15)

- **No recoil in Classic:** the Gameplay preset's Classic row set `vr_weapon_recoil` 0 (a "?" taste call: "Quake has no
  gun kick"), but the models' own baked kick is always cancelled (`vr_kickcancel.cpp`), so a Classic gun had no kick
  at all, VR and flat (flat draws the same `weaponfx` recoil). Classic now leaves it at the default (1), as Light and
  Unleashed; GAMEPLAY_PRESET.md marks it decided.
- **Grunts still dropped burst rifles:** Classic already had `vr_enemy_drops` 2 (never), but that is only id's random
  extra drops (`TryEnemyDrop`); a dying grunt's own gun (`army_die` -> `VR_DropEnemyGun`), an enforcer's rifle, a
  knight's sword, an ogre's chainsaw, an armed humanoid's held and stowed weapons and AD's soldiers' and melee monsters'
  always fell. New `vr_enemy_held_drops` (1; Classic 0, Light/Unleashed 1) and `vr_enemy_held_drops_linger` (4 s):
  at 0 such a weapon still falls (the death frames are drawn without it: `vr_monstermods.cpp`) but as scenery
  (`VR_EnemyHeld_Scenery`, vr_enemyguns.qc: no hand touch, no force grab, no loot pillar, not taken by armed humanoids,
  not counted by the drop cap), then fades as the cap's do. Every death-drop path calls it (the grunt/enforcer gun,
  knight sword, ogre chainsaw, `VR_AG_Dying`'s held and stowed weapons, AD melee swords, Freddie's nailgun); a disarm's
  drop (alive) and the Gremlin's stolen gun stay real. Backpacks unchanged. Rows: VR Settings > Combat > Enemy
  Weapons, "Lying About" (and the Gameplay Presets page); menu_paths.txt regenerated.
  **Decision:** scenery that fades rather than vanishing in the hand (the death frames have no weapon) or lying forever.
- **The picked-up Burst Rifle fired like a shotgun:** not a wrong slot. `vr_grunt_burst` 0 (Classic and Light) turned
  the grunts' fire back to id's shotgun and, by design, the dropped gun's too (six pellets, a clip of shells), though
  its model is the burst rifle. Now `vr_grunt_burst` is the grunts' own fire only: the gun in your hands always bursts
  (`VR_EnemyGun_Attack`), its clip is always rounds, it is always named the burst rifle; AD's pellet spread treats yours
  as bullets (`AD_FirePellets`). An armed grunt holding one at `vr_grunt_burst` 0 still fires id's shotgun (no preset
  has both). Happened outside Classic too (Light, or the toggle by hand).
- **Tests:** `vr_gameplay_preset_test` 29/0 (Classic: recoil on, no enemy weapon drops); `vr_gameplay_classic_check`
  4/0 (adds recoil on, `vr_enemy_held_drops` 0 and `vr_enemy_drops` 2); new `vr_classic_drop_check` (QC
  `VR_Classic_DropCheck`, its lines with `developer 1`: the nearest plain grunt gibbed: backpack, gun takeable or
  scenery by the cvar, then a burst rifle at `vr_grunt_burst` 0: clip 30 rounds, a pull begins a burst): Classic on
  e1m1 8/0 in VR and in flat, default with `vr_agrunt_repl 0` 7/0. Run: `developer 1;vr_classic_quake 1;map e1m1;
  wait10;vr_gameplay_classic_check;vr_classic_drop_check`, `-QuitOn "classicdrop: [0-9]+ passed"`. `vr_recoil_test` 126/1 after it in Classic, VR and flat; the same single FAIL (the
  burst rifle's two-handed return time, 0.0750 vs 0.0750, a back-time tolerance) in the default preset: not this
  change. Armed grunts unchanged: `vr_agrunt_test` 2 4/0, 28 2/0, 47 110/0. Scenario `classic_drops` (runall OK).
  Dev and ReleaseLTO (1.1.0) builds 0 warnings.

## Quest C4c continued: the black eye scene bisected (branch `agent/quest`, 2026-11-14)

QUEST_PLAN.md section 6j ("The bisection") has the numbers. On the Quest 3 over adb, the headset unworn, e1m1's start:
- **New probes (Debug > Startup):** `vr_gl_probe 2` paints the eye blue after its clear (no depth test), `3` paints red
  after the scene where the depth still holds the clear value, `4`/`5` draw the world's own vertices and indices in
  green through the frame UBO's ViewProj (5: the first instance's SSBO matrix too), `6` to `8` add the world's clip
  distances. `vr_gl_probe 1` also reads back the world's GPU-written buffers (cull commands, indices, vertices), the
  instance upload, the draw state and each program's validation and buffer-block layout at the first world draws;
  `vr_gl_probe_fix` (1 clip distances off, 2 culling off) acts on the world's draws.
- **Found:** the scene target, its copy to the composite and the readback work (2: 100% blue); no scene draw writes a
  colour or a depth (3: 100% red): the world, its depth pass, the models, showtris alike; every buffer, the UBO/SSBO
  layouts and bindings, the state and the programs' validation are as on the PC; a minimal program with the same data,
  transform, instance SSBO and clip distances draws (4 to 8: 100% green). The fault is inside the real scene programs
  on Adreno. Next: a constant fragment output switched in through the ES header, then the vertex shader cut down.
- PC unchanged: the probes act only while `vr_gl_probe` or `vr_gl_probe_fix` is set.

## mpN (B7b): snapshots down acknowledged and delta-coded; the entities' interpolation buffer (agent/mp, 2026-11-14; never shipped by the coordinator)

- A remote client acknowledges the newest snapshot it read in each `QVR_CLC_MOVES`; the server writes its datagram's
  player state, entity updates and the avatars it sees as records of one `QVR_SVC_SNAPSHOT` (`vr_netsnap.cpp`;
  `QVR_NET_VERSION` 18), coded against the acknowledged one: an unchanged record is not sent, a changed one goes as a
  byte mask or whole, a gone one as its key. The client rebuilds the whole set and parses each record with NetQuake's
  own parsers: the rest of the client is unchanged. B idle on e1m1: down 7 KB/s, mean 97 B (was 20 KB/s, 270 B).
  `vr_net_snapshots` 1 (Debug > Reports > Network: Delta Snapshots; 0 NetQuake's whole datagram).
- A remote client draws the others (not brush models: doors and lifts stay in step with the player riding them; not
  stepping monsters: the renderer lerps those) a delay behind the newest message, between the two around that time,
  turns slerped; the delay follows the longest recent gap (about 40 ms at 10% loss), its clock eased (never a jump);
  the other players' hands and weapons at the same time. `vr_net_interp` 1 (Network: Interpolation Buffer).
  `mp_loss`: 0 jumps of A's body and hands at 10% loss (were 1-3), hand offset roughness 0.21 (was 0.28-0.68).
- Single player, the listen host's own client and demos of them: unchanged (no snapshot, no buffer). A demo recorded
  on a remote server mid-game asks for a whole snapshot to start from.
- Tests: `mp_loss`'s jump checks, `mp_bandwidth` under 10 KB/s and the server's deltas, `vr_netsnap_selftest` 5/0;
  MP_PLAN.md "B7b results".
- In VR (two machines): another player walking and turning (smooth, no stop-and-jump), his hands on his body; the
  Interpolation Buffer row off for comparison.

## Save and load after a Test scene (agent/saveload1115)

His report (flat, 2026-11-15): TEST on the waterdrips item, quicksave, quickload: a toolgun in his off hand, the grunts'
firing poses bent (one cast the death knight's fireballs), nothing wet. Reproduced headless (flat and the VR mock). Not a
precache-order problem: the precache list's hash and every model index were the same before and after
(`vr_model_check`: 514 models, 0 wrong), and nothing in the armed rigs caches by model index.

- **Poses and the fireballs: a QC row cache across the load.** `VR_AM_Row(kind)` (vr_armedmon.qc) fills the armed
  monsters' row globals once per kind, `nosave vr_am_filled` + saved `vr_am_kind`. A load runs the map's spawn first
  (SV_SpawnServer's two frames: vrtesthall's armed death knight filled the row), then the save's globals overwrite
  `vr_am_kind` (the grunt's) and the row's floats, but not its vectors (hand vertices, anchors, shoulders) nor
  `vr_am_spell` (a save keeps floats, strings, entities). The cache then answered "filled" for the grunt with the
  knight's vectors and spell: guns 30+ units off the hand, fireballs. Any map with two armed kinds hit it on any load,
  scene or not. Fix: `VR_AM_AfterLoad` (OnLoadGame) empties the cache.
- **The off-hand toolgun: the grip's rising edge at the load.** A flatscreen player's hands always grip
  (vr_client.cpp `gripping`). The server's previous-frame VR bits started at 0 for the reconnecting client, so its first
  move was a new press; the off hand, posed by the left hip as the stance brings it to the gun, drew that holster's
  weapon (W_Frame's `startedHandGrabbing`: here the axe, his the toolgun from `vr_debug_spawn_toolgun`). Only with a
  gun in the main hand (an empty pair's pose is elsewhere). Fix: `VR_ClientLoadedBits` (SV_ConnectClient into a loaded
  game) seeds the client's previous and received bits from the loaded player's saved `.vrbits0`: a grip held across
  the load is no new press. A headset grip pressed after the load is still a press.
- **Wetness: client-only state, never saved.** vr_drips.cpp's wet list was cleared by the load's new map. Now the save
  writes `// qvrwet <what> <num> <hand> <wet> <waterline> <liquid>` lines (`VR_SaveWetLines`, SaveData_Fill, after the
  decals), `VR_ReadSaveInfo` stages them, `VR_OnLoadGame` takes them, and each is given back as the load's map first
  shows it (a model by entity number; your body, hands, held and holstered weapons by what they are; a holstered
  weapon's entry now keeps its holster as its `hand`) for 3 s, drying on from there.

**Test.** `Misc/quakevr/saveload_test.sh <agent> [flat|vr|both]` (vr_pickup_test 16, QC/vr_saveload_test.qc;
self-driven across the load by saved globals): `vr_scenario waterdrips`, once placed `vr_drips_soak`, save
`qvr_saveload`, load; checks the off hand empty, each armed grunt's gun within 18 of its hand and no spell on a grunt, and
(the script) every thing wet out of the pool before is wet after.

## classictoggle: Classic Quake on and off leaves the gloves' relief flat (agent/classictoggle, 2026-11-15)

- **His report (flat, on next):** in the hub, the Classic Quake board pressed twice (on, off): the gloves' relief
  "almost as a diffuse".
- **Cause:** the gloves' relief (`progs/hand_rig_0N_00_glove_height`) is a height map made a normal map as it loads
  (`vr_render.cpp` `gloveHeightToNormals`), but only in `gloveTexture`; the texture keeps the height file as its source.
  It is loaded `TEXPREF_MIPMAP|ALPHA|UNCOMPRESSED`, so `TexMgr_AlphaTested` counts it, and Classic's `vr_alpha_coverage`
  change (1 -> 0 -> 1) reloads every alpha-tested texture from its source (`TexMgr_ReloadAlphaTested`): the relief came
  back as raw heights (grey: a normal pointing nowhere), so the leather lost its bumps. `vid_restart` did the same.
- **Fix:** the conversion moved into the load itself: `VR_GloveReliefNormals` (vr_render.cpp), called from
  `TexMgr_LoadImage32` (as `VR_CleanSkin` is), so the first load and every reload make the normals.
- **Cvars:** a full `cvarlist` diff before on / after off in the hub showed no setting left changed (only
  `vr_gore_preset`'s display sync). But Back restored each preset's *My Settings* (kept at the first preset ever
  applied), not the state the press found: a row changed since (in the menu, say Bloom) came back as the old My
  Settings. Classic's first press now keeps the three presets' rows as found (`ClassicState::before`, in memory) and
  Back sets back exactly those; a row changed by hand while Classic was on keeps its new value; with none kept (a
  restart since) Back is My Settings as before. The line reads "Your settings back: ...".
- **Other things checked:** the round trip test hashes every texture read from a file or a lump (4,108 in the hub:
  world textures and their normal maps, weapons' and armour's skins and normal maps, the hands', the gloves' paint):
  only the gloves' relief differed before the fix, none after.
- **Test:** new `vr_classic_roundtrip_test` (Debug > Tests, "Classic Quake On and Off"): waits for the map, keeps every
  cvar and every file texture's texels hash, presses `vr_setup_option classic` twice (the hub board's command), two
  frames after each, compares: `classicroundtrip: 5 passed, 0 failed` in vrstart (4,114 settings, 4,108 textures); with
  the old code (the conversion back in `gloveTexture` only) 4/1, `progs/hand_rig_00_00_glove_height` differing. Run:
  `map vrstart;vr_classic_roundtrip_test`, `-QuitOn "classicroundtrip: \d+ passed"`. `vr_gameplay_preset_test` 31/0
  (2 new: Back is the press's state, a hand change kept), `vr_gore_preset_test` 15/0, `vr_gameplay_classic_check` 4/0.
  menu_paths.txt regenerated (the new Debug row).

## Quest C4d: the black world fixed; the program binary cache (branch `agent/quest`, 2026-11-14)

QUEST_PLAN.md section 6k has the numbers. On the Quest 3 over adb, the headset unworn, e1m1's start:
- **Cause:** Adreno (0837.0.9) reads a struct copied whole out of a buffer wrong (`Instance instance =
  instance_data[i];`): the copy's matrix drops every vertex, in every world and model program. Found with
  `-glesdefine` (macros in the ES header switching the shaders' `QVR_PROBE_*` cuts: a constant fragment colour, the
  plain transform, no invariance, draw 0, no clipping).
- **Fix (ES form only):** `vr_glsafe.cpp` rewrites each such copy member by member; `-glesstructcopy` turns it off.
  The world and the models draw (99.5% of the eye not black, was 0%). The PC's GLSL is untouched.
- **Program binary cache:** `vr_program_cache` (1: on under OpenGL ES, 2: also on the PC, 0: off; read before the
  window opens) keeps each program's driver binary in `<cache>/programs/<driver hash>.bin`, keyed by the exact text
  compiled. Quest, process start to e1m1's first frame: 65.1 s cold, 8.3 s warm (shaders 51.1 s to 0.18 s). The
  driver's EGL blob cache keeps nothing for the app.
- **Checks:** gles_render_test 21/0, scenario_check 150/0, load_models_test 4/0; Release and ReleaseLTO 0 warnings.

## rangerhead2: the detailed head's wounds where struck; his head place as defaults; the recoil test's 2H time (agent/rangerhead2, 2026-11-15)

- **Why the detailed head's wounds were in the wrong spots:** three causes. (1) Its texture coordinates were his own skin's
  (s 88..252, t 61..142 of 256) while the wound mask is the body's (its layout the body's skin's): the head read the
  body's mask at texels that belong to the body's back, arms and legs, so their wounds showed on the head (and the
  body's skin mask, read there too, tinted it from other parts). (2) `R_PaintAliasWounds` painted the body's first
  surface only: a blow on the head never painted the head's own mesh. (3) Your body is painted as the eye views pose
  it, the neck and head collapsed: even the old head's (in the first surface) wounds were painted onto a collapsed head.
- **Fix:** `packDetailed` (vr_rangerhead.cpp) puts his two islands side by side in the body's head block (the
  placeholder's head-only texels, u 0.008..0.492, v 0.447..0.496: unused once his head is drawn), stretched to fill it;
  his vertices' coordinates are there (the md5 text and `VR_RangerHeadMesh`), and his skin is laid out to match
  (`progs/vrrangerhead_00_00`, 256 x 2048, no texel of his lost). `VR_RangerHeadImage` now paints the body's skin mask
  there for him too (skin where his texels are skin colours, normals flat). `R_PaintAliasWounds` draws the head's mesh
  as well (`VR_RangerHeadPaints`) and takes your body's bones with its head (`VR_AliasWoundBonePoses`, the shadow maps'
  `shadowSkin`; the classic head gains from this too). The sliders need nothing: the paint draws the mesh's own
  vertices, which they rewrite.
- **Test:** `vr_body_head_wound_test [keep]` (vr_wounds_diag.cpp; Debug > Tools > *Wound Your Head (Mirror)*): five
  small wounds (front, left, right, back, crown: the head's triangle farthest that way, posed with its head:
  `avatar::posedMesh(withHead, st)`), each painted alone into your mask and read back; the blood in the head's texels,
  mapped back onto the posed head, must have its middle within 1.5 units of the point and none farther than 5; a chest
  wound must leave the head's texels clean. Verdict `head_wound_test: N passed, M failed` (`-QuitOn` it). Detailed head
  11/0 (middles 0.12..0.90 off), with the sliders at size 1.8, sink 3, side -4, yaw 30, pitch 20: 11/0; the classic
  head (`-rangerhead_nodetail`): 11/0. `vr_body_head_check detailed` 3/0, `classic` 3/0. Shot (front and back with
  `keep`): `scratch/r2_face.png`.
- **His values (2026-11-15) as defaults:** `vr_body_head_side` 1.75 -> 0, `vr_body_head_size` 1.3 -> 1.25 (rows in
  `fullConfigChanges` for full configs; the Ranger Head page's *Reset Head Placement* now sets the shipped size and
  sink: it said sink 4.5, the default is 9).
- **vr_recoil_test's "two-handed return time" FAIL (0.0750 vs 0.0750):** the test's comparison, not the gameplay: the
  shares were right (0.075 printed both sides); the drawn time back to rest was checked against the one-handed time
  times the share, which the kick's floors (0.014 s of Return Time, 0.02 s a kick) and the rise's 35 ms cap make only
  nearly so, a weapon's Return Time deciding by how much (the burst rifle's a step past the 2% + 1 ms margin). Now
  checked against the kick as `shotKick` makes it (`backWant`: its length less its rise, within two 0.5 ms steps), and
  that two hands bring it back sooner. 127/0 (the baseline's script).
- load_models_test 4/0, scenario_check PASS. Dev build 0 warnings; ReleaseLTO (QvrReleaseVersion 1.1.0) 0 warnings.

## Quest C4e: from 2 FPS to ~39 on the Quest 3 (branch `agent/quest`, 2026-11-14)

QUEST_PLAN.md section 6l has the numbers. e1m1's start over adb, the headset unworn:
- **CPU (370 ms in "models"):** ES has no `GL_ARB_buffer_storage`, so `GL_Upload` was a `glBufferSubData` into a
  buffer in use, which Adreno copies whole. `GL_EXT_buffer_storage` (Android) now gives the persistent mapped frame
  buffers: under 1 ms.
- **GPU (the world's fragment shader, ~280 ms):** the ES struct copy of C4d copied `Light.gateinverse[3]` with a
  loop; the index into a local struct's array kept the whole `Light` in scratch memory for every pixel. Literal-size
  arrays are now copied unrolled (`vr_glsafe.cpp` `appendMemberCopies`). Found with `-glesdefine QVR_PROBE_*` cuts
  (gl_shaders.h: CUT1-5, LCOUNT, NOSHADOW, SIMPLELOOP, NOPARALLAX, NORETRO, NOCARVE; kept for the next split).
- **MSAA:** `vr_quest_preset 0` now `vid_fsaa 0` (2x cost ~100 ms: resolved through memory).
- **Frame:** 424 ms -> 25.6 ms (39 FPS); without the world 14.1 ms (72 Hz). `vr_profile_slow_ms` (Debug > Profiling,
  250 as before) keeps slow frames in the profiler's averages.
- **Checks:** gles_render_test 21/0, scenario_check 150/0, load_models_test 4/0; dev and LTO builds 0 warnings.
