## presetlate (2026-11-15)

His flat report: a Run Setup Style (Classic, then Unleashed) took effect only when the run was started a second time.

- Order of events, every way in (Levels list, Map Library, New Game, Official Campaigns, the hub's teleporter, Arena
  Mode; a Continue row is a load: the save's run): the Start (`runSetupStart`) sets every `vr_run_<id>` and applies the
  presets' rows at once (`applyStyle` / `applyGore` / `applyArmed` / `applySmartAi`: `Cvar_SetQuick`, no Cbuf), then
  queues the launch (`M_LevelStart`: `disconnect`, `skill`, `map`; New Game `map start`; a campaign `map start`
  after its folders; the arena `vr_campaign_hub vrarena`). `Host_Map_f` -> `newGame` (kept: `runSet`) ->
  `SV_SpawnServer` -> `VR_OnSpawnServerBeforeLoad` -> `beforeMapLoad` -> the entities. QC reads the settings as each
  monster spawns (`cvar_hget`: the cvar itself, no cached copy). Nothing in that chain defers or latches a preset row.
- Not reproduced headless: `vr_runlaunch_test` now picks a different Style and Gore (and Armed Humanoids over Light) on
  every way in and checks the first start; all passed on next before the fix too. Whatever set the last run's values
  back in his game ran between the Start and the spawn (a queued command, a config) or is outside these paths.
- Fix (a guarantee, whatever the cause): a Start whose map comes at once (`runsetup::start(mapNow)`; not the hub's
  teleporter, the screen without a launch, `vr_run start`) keeps every Gameplay and Gore preset row's value; that `map`'s
  spawn (`beforeMapLoad`, before any entity) sets back any changed since, printing `Run setup: <cvar> is "x", the run's
  Start set "y": set again before <map> spawns` (the line to look for in his console if it ever shows).
- Test `vr_runlaunch_test` (80/0): per step its Style/Gore/Armed picks (each other than the run before: Light, Classic,
  Unleashed, Classic, Unleashed, Light + Armed On, Unleashed, a load of Classic, Unleashed, the arena's, Classic); checks
  the presets' settings (`matchingLevel`, the Gore choice, `vr_agrunt_repl`, `vr_reload_mode`) and the map (QC
  `VR_Run_PresetLaunchCheck`: every grunt and enforcer armed or none; the guns' reloading modes); step 9 queues
  `vr_agrunt_repl 0; vr_reload_mode 0` after its Start, ahead of its `map`: both set back (2), every other step 0.
- Found on the way (not fixed): Classic + 3x Enemy Count on e1m1 leaves two grunt copies in solid
  (`vr_run_enemies_check`: "2 copies in solid"; Classic's full-size hulls, `vr_mhull 0`); the test keeps Classic off
  that pick row.
- Cause (the coordinator, from his log 2026-11-14_22-40-06): a checklist test scene was running (classic_drops), then
  Levels > E1M1 with Classic. The Start set the run's settings; the map change then ended the scene
  (`scenario::worldReset`), whose put-back ("5 settings put back") set its saved old values over the run's before the
  map spawned. The second start had no scene left. Fix: `scenario::endBeforeRun()` (vr_scenario.cpp) ends a running
  scene, its settings put back, before a run sets its own: at a Start (`startWith`), a new game's mutators
  (`newGame`) and a save's run (`onLoadGame`); not a scene loading its own map. The `beforeMapLoad` guard above stays
  (it runs after the scene's put-back, prints only when it sets something back; it set nothing back here).
- `vr_runlaunch_test` (86/0): the classic_drops scene run (waited for until `scenario::active()`), then the Levels list
  with Unleashed: the scene ended at the Start, the map spawned Unleashed (armed grunts, reloading), nothing for the
  guard to set back.

## gibthrow: the hand stays on a gib pulled off the blade; thrown blades settle point first (branch agent/gibthrow, 2026-11-15)

His notes (vrtesthall_2026-11-15_00-03-02, _00-03-51): pulled off the sword with the hand that held it, the gib was drawn off
the hand ("it seems like the gib is floating"); thrown swords and daggers should steady towards their point in the air, "not
instantly turning straight like an arrow ... not perfect or unbelievable".

**The gib.** On the blade the hand is drawn at its hold (`.vr_skewer_gripd`, the carried props' fit, turning with the gib:
skewerDrawnHand's pin). At the take (`VR_Skewer_Take`) the gib was moved by that world offset as taken (stale once the gib had
turned with the blade), then fitted twice more as any prop taken: `carryfit` (VR_Carry_FitToHand) and the grip fit
(vr_gripfit.hpp), whose Box3D hulls are wider than a gib as drawn and pushed it 2 units off the fist. Now the hold is also kept
in the gib's own frame as it takes hold (`.vr_skewer_gripl`, `.vr_skewer_gript`: new builtin `skewerhold`), and the take turns
and places the gib so that the hand has it there, its turn on it as then (`skewerplace`), with neither fit after it
(`vr_carry_asheld` round VR_Carry_Start; `carrygrip`'s optional 7th argument `asheld`, grip::serverTake's `fit`). Measured
(`vr_embed_test 34`, a new step: the other hand slides the gib off the tip): off the blade the hand was 4.46 cm from its hold,
2.30 units off the surface (the fit's gap) and turned 27.7 degrees on it; now 0.03 cm, 0.01 units, 0.0 degrees. 15 of 15.
(The test's own gib, made seconds before, fades about 0.15 s after it is taken: its old think restored; the step reads at once.)

**Point first.** `pointAlign` (vr_box3d_step.cpp, after spinAlign while the throw is in the air): a pointed blade (weapons.txt
`embed` 1: the swords and the dagger; `axestick::pointLine` gives its line, whatever vr_embed is) gets a damped turn of its
line towards its flight: an angular acceleration of 150 rad/s^2 per radian off, damping 14/s of the tumble across the blade
(its spiral about its length kept), at most 90 rad/s^2, all times a share: Point-First Settling (`vr_throw_point_align`, 1)
x how near point first it flies (1 at 0, 0 at `vr_throw_point_angle`, 45 degrees) x how calm (0 from `vr_throw_point_spin`,
1.5 turns/s, across the blade) x speed (0 under 3 m/s, 1 from 8) x a fade over `vr_throw_point_time` (0.3 s) after the
throw. VR and flat throws alike (any thrown weapon's Box3D flight). Tunables rows after Spin Alignment (Debug > Tunables);
menu_paths.txt regenerated.
Test `vr_embed_test 47` (QC/vr_throwpoint_test.qc; `map vrtesthall;wait30;god;notarget;vr_embed_test 47`): 22 throws at

## flipgrip: the blade's grip flip seamless everywhere (agent/flipgrip, 2026-11-15)

His notes (VR, 2026-11-14/15): flipped (reversed) dagger loses its two-handed hotspot; the re-grab from the other hand keeps the
old grip; a reversed dagger dropped or thrown leaves the hand flipped; taken off a table reversed it was mostly a prop; grabbed
in a body the other way round the drawn hand on the handle was twisted.

**One root.** The reverse grip lived only as the holding hand's turn (`reverseTurn` between the hand and the weapon, the flag a
hand state): everything that takes the weapon's pose from the hand (the prop's angles on a drop or throw: the hand's; the other
hand's carry: drawn upright from the holder's pose; the 2H aim and blade line; the helping hand on a hotspot; the "at its handle"
of a grab: the origin, where only the upright hand stands) lost it or applied the upright grip. Now the blade's own pose goes
through every transition, and every grab chooses by the blade's way:
- **Out of the hand** (notes 3, 5): `view::leavingTurn` (QC `weapondrawnpose` 49 angles, 50 the origin's move;
  `DropWeaponInHandScaled`): a reversed weapon leaves at `rot Rev` (`uprightTurnOf`) and the reverse grip's shift: the prop lies
  and flies as it was drawn (blade cos 0.999 to the held line). The hand-off: `drawnAs[hand].rot` is the upright-equivalent turn
  while reversed, so the other hand's carry (and a hand holding it anywhere) keeps the blade's way (cos 1.00).
- **Into the hand** (notes 2, 4): `VR_RevGrip_TakeCarried` (QC; `weapondrawnpose` 47, `view::carriedGripChoice`) chooses as the
  hand takes the carried weapon back (`VRTakeCarriedWeapon`); the choice uses the hand's own turn (`rot`, not the drawn one: an
  empty hand on the carried weapon is drawn on it). The reversed hand point (`reversedHandPoint`: the hand holding it reversed,
  the weapon's origin less the reverse shift; QC `weapondrawnpose` 48 for tests) counts as its handle in the server's grab
  (`vr_physics.cpp weaponHandleDistance`: the handle leniency, not "anywhere"), the view's ground spots and the carried
  weapon's take-back (`setCarriedHandle`'s reversed point, HS_CARRIED_GRIP; the free-grip candidate). The dagger's reversed
  hand point is 4.3 units off its origin, inside `vr_weapon_grab_anywhere_min` only just: a hand a little further was a prop.
  Force grab: `vr_revgrip_forcegrab` 0 (his note 1, upright; test 42 case 3 unchanged), 1 by the blade (Debug > Tunables >
  Weapons > Reverse Grip > Force Grab Catch).
- **Two-handed while reversed** (note 1; choice: the automatic one): the hotspots stay (`placeHotspots`, on the drawn frame:
  turned with the blade); the helping hand turned with the weapon (`attachedTurn`'s `flip`, `helpingTurn`, the held hotspot's
  offset); a fixed (gun-style) 2H hold worked out for the upright-equivalent hand and turned back (`applyHotspots` ->
  `applyFixed` in that frame); the sword-style hold's blade line flips (`bladeDirection` with `view::heldReverseTurn`). Optional
  tweak only while reversed: Weapon Offsets > Hand > Reversed 2H Hand X/Y/Z, Pitch/Yaw/Roll (`rev_2h_vx`.. `rev_2h_vroll`, 0:
  added to the held hotspot's Held Hand offset).
- **The embedded handle** (note 6): the grip was right, but the hand's roll about the handle was the blade's as it went in,
  up to half a turn from the real hand's (palm up/down): `embedHandleRoll` draws the hand half round the handle's line when
  that is nearer its controller (swords and the dagger: two edges alike), chosen once per hold. Probe `vr_embed_probe_hctl`
  (degrees, the hand on a handle against its controller).
- **Decision:** his dagger 2H hotspot promoted to the defaults (weapons.txt slot 51: `2h_mode` 1, `hs1` his place and turn;
  was one-handed, no hotspots): he holds it two-handed and asked for it to keep working flipped.

Test `vr_embed_test 44` (QC/vr_flipgrip_test.qc, `flipgrip: 21 passed, 0 failed`): the hotspot upright and reversed (moved with
the blade), 2H held both ways (reversed: blade still down, cos -0.96); handed off upright (carried, cos 1.00), taken back by the
hand turned for the other grip: reversed, blade where it was (cos 0.96); reversed and let go of: the prop's line cos 0.999; off a
table reversed (4.3 units from the origin) and upright: by the handle, the right grip; stuck upright, taken reversed: held in the
body, reversed, the drawn hand 17-55 degrees from the mock hand (under 95: the mock's roll is free; never twisted past a quarter
turn; case 6: the grunt held still and unharmed after the stick, the blade checked still stuck, the take tried at three points; when the mock hand is kept out of the grunt's body short of the handle (about 1 run in 5, 6-10 units) the case reports SKIP, not FAIL: never a fall-out, the sword stays stuck; 5 runs in a row clean). ## torchgrab: the torso's torch taken whatever the other hand holds (agent/torchgrab, 2026-11-15)

His notes (start_2026-11-14_23-38-09, _23-38-55, vrtesthall_2026-11-15_00-09-43, _00-10-19, _00-11-08): with the torch
on the torso and the dagger in the right hand, the left hand could not take the torch at all (fine once he gave the
dagger a two-handed hotspot); with the super shotgun held one-handed, sometimes not even 30 cm from the gun.

Two rules in `gameGripWins` (vr_flashlight.cpp: whether the game's grip wins over the torch for a hand at it):
- **The two-handed hotspot alone won.** `body::hotspot` says HS_OFFHAND_2H_GRAB whenever the hands are 5-25 units
  apart, whatever the other hand holds. For a weapon with no fitted grip (`!s.grip2HValid`) the game's grip won there,
  even for one that may never be held in two hands: the dagger (slot 52, Two-Handed: Not Allowed) won anywhere 5-25
  units from the right hand, which is where the chest torch is.
- **The weapon's line ran from 30 cm behind the hand** (`otherWeaponNear`, for a sword's pommel): any gun held
  one-handed at the chest or low at the belt, pointing away from the torch, covered it (within 12 cm of that line).
  Not the holsters or the clip-on zone (the "cap"): those were already nearest-wins.

Now `otherWeaponNear` asks the game's own rules (vr_twohand.cpp), and the nearest wins: the fist on the weapon's surface
where gripping holds it anywhere (`twohand::onOtherWeapon`, the view's free-grip candidate); its fitted grip
(`s.grip2H`, within 8 units less its bias, and nearer than the torch's axis); a weapon with no fitted grip, or a sword
(`twohand::swordHeld`: its blade), within 12 cm of its line from the hand to the muzzle or tip and nearer than the
torch's axis. A weapon the other hand may not hold (`twohand::forbidden`) wins by its surface only. The 2H hotspot case
itself never wins any more.

His dagger tuning promoted (weapons.txt slot 52, `weapons_data.py promote`): `2h_mode` 2 -> 1 and its hs1 grip
(type 1, x -1.785095, y -2.161255, z -11.23747, pitch -6.90695, yaw 8.52477, roll -3.05592). Not promoted (not
asked): his `bl_from/near/org_x/org_y/org_z/spine/width_52` and `muzzle_x/y/z_52`, none of them defaults yet.

Test aid: `vr_test_give_flags` (impulse 149's weapon flags; 3072 with id 13 gives the dagger). The probe prints
`helping` per hand and the main weapon's grip and muzzle. Test: `flash_grab_test.py <agent> otherweapon` (verdict line
`otherweapon: N passed, M failed`): the dagger without its grip (the old defaults) and with it, the super shotgun
one-handed at the chest, the shotgun low at the belt; the off hand at the torch takes it, at the weapon's grip (or 60%
along it) holds the weapon, the torch left on. Before 4/3 (the dagger, the chest and the belt cases at the torch);
after 7/0. `mounted:9-10` (the two gun torso turns) 312 lit, 312 taken. Scenario `torch_otherweapon`.

## flipgrip2: the flip's pivot is the fist; the reversed two-handed hold mirrored (agent/flipgrip2, 2026-11-15)

His note (vrtesthall_2026-11-15_03-14-49): the flip "much better", but the dagger needed tweaks (his config: `rev_x_52` -0.15,
`rev_z_52` 1.1, `rev_thumb_top_52` 0, `rev_thumb_bias_52` -1; his `hs1_*_52` equal the shipped ones); and the flipped two-handed
hold was wrong: the hotspot below the main hand (expected above), the other hand's knuckles towards him, the wrist bent past 180.

**On paper.** Frames in the holding (main) hand: `a` the handle's line (pommel to blade, upright), `n` the palm's normal made square
to it, `R` the hand's turn, `O` the weapon's angle offsets. Reversed, the hand stays on its controller and only the weapon turns:
`G`, half round about `n` through a pivot `c` on the handle (`reverseTurn`), so the weapon is `R G O` and the handle is the same
line through the fist. Two-handed upright: the main fist on the handle, the other fist below it at `-d a` from it, both thumbs
towards the blade, knuckles out; the other hand's turn relative to the main hand is `h0`. Flipped in a real hand: the main hand
is unchanged and the blade leaves it on the little finger's side; the pommel is up; the other hand holds the same handle the way
the main hand does: thumb up (now towards the pommel), knuckles out, so its turn relative to the main hand is still `h0`, and its
fist is at `+d a`: the positions swap along the handle (a reflection along `a` about the main fist), nothing across it. What the
code did (flipgrip): the other hand carried rigidly with the weapon, `R G h0` and its point `c + G (p - c)`: `G` sends `a` to
`-a` and the knuckle direction (across the handle, square to `n`) to its opposite: thumb down, knuckles in (his "towards the
player", the wrist past a half turn), and the point's offset across the handle flipped too: the dagger's hotspot point is 2 units
off the handle (it is the hand's point, not its fist), so it went 4 units across, to below and in front (measured: 3.9 below,
3.7 along the blade's side). Pitch 180 on the hand (his guess) is `G` again (about `n`); the wrist-to-knuckle axis would keep the
thumb up but put the knuckles in. The right answer is neither: no turn at all relative to the main hand, a move along the handle.
- **The other hand** (`flipSpot`, vr_view_hands.cpp; `vr_revgrip_2h_mirror` 1): turned `R h0` (`helpingTurn` without the flip; its
  Held Hand move in the main hand's frame, its part along the handle mirrored: `flipVisualPos`); its point `q_up + delta` in the main
  hand's frame, `delta = -2 ((palm_up - c) . a) a` (the fist's middle is its palm's, `palmAt`; the point moves with the fist), plus
  the weapon's Reversed X/Y/Z. The hotspot (`placeHotspots`), the grab (the same world hotspot) and the fitted fingers
  (`canonicalHotspotGrip` with the flip: the reversed weapon against the mirrored hand) all use it.
- **The aim** (`view::twoHandTurn`): the 2H solves (the fixed hold's `applyHotspots`, the sword hold's `bladeDirection` for its grip
  below the hand; the half-sword blade grip keeps `G`) worked out for the hand turned by `Q = (least turn from G q_up to q_now) G`
  instead of `G`: the upright hold's line onto the mirrored grip's, so taking hold turns the blade exactly as upright does
  (test: cos to the one-handed line 1.00 both ways).
- **The pivot** (`reverseLearn`; `vr_revgrip_pivot` 1, `vr_revgrip_pivot_shift` 0.35): why the dagger felt off. The half turn was about
  the handle's middle (butt to an estimated guard); a fist off that middle by `e` along the handle slid `2e` along it when flipped
  (the guard's estimate, Blade From or 0.15 of the length, is a guess for the swords too). Now about the fist's own middle: the point
  of the handle's line abreast of the drawn hand's palm (`palmOnWeapon`: the main hand posed as `canonicalOwnGrip`), 0.35 units towards
  the blade (the palm's centre sits a little below the fist's middle; one constant of the hand, the same for every weapon). Dagger:
  the reversed weapon moves (-0.03 0.01 1.09) in the hand's frame against before: his (-0.15 0 1.1) made by the model (the 0.15
  forward, 3 mm, left out). Knight's sword: (-0.05 0 -0.22). Learnt again once the jointed hand is there.
- **His tweaks:** `rev_x`/`rev_z` unnecessary (he must set his dagger's back to 0, else they add on top: the checklist line says so);
  the thumb is a hand-pose preference, not geometry: `rev_thumb_top` 0 (wrapped) and `rev_thumb_bias` -1 promoted to the defaults

## throwfix: thrown blades really come round point first; a thrown gib skewered in the air (agent/throwfix, 2026-11-15)

His notes (vrtesthall_2026-11-15_03-19-26, _03-21-03): the point-first throw "doesn't seem to work at all ... it always seems to
immediately start spinning a lot"; tweakables "that can go to extreme levels". A gib pulled off the blade and thrown can be hit
and shot but not skewered again in the air.

**Why nothing happened.** Replaying his take (`vr_motion_play` of the _03-21-03 replay, `vr_debug_box3d 1`: pointAlign now prints
each pointed blade's flight every 0.05 s) the sword left the hand 136 degrees off its flight (its point up and back, as any
overhand release has it) tumbling at 12.5 rad/s across the blade; his recorded releases show the controller at 10-22 rad/s. The
gates (45 degrees, none past 1.5 turns/s = 9.4 rad/s) shut pointAlign out of every real throw; only near point-first, calm,
synthetic throws were helped.

**Now** (vr_box3d_step.cpp `pointAlign`): the gates are the release's (Slot `flightOff`, `flightTumble`) and wide: any angle
(`vr_throw_point_angle` 180), the whole help up to half of `vr_throw_point_spin` (3 turns/s; none from it: a throw spun on purpose
near Max Spin stays a spin). A damped spring turns the line to its flight: 400/s^2 per radian times Point-First Settling (about
0.15 s to come round), damped critically (`vr_throw_point_damp` 1, new: the release's tumble across the blade taken out as it
comes round; less swings past and back, more kills the spin first), at most 600 rad/s^2 times the strength, times speed (3-8 m/s)
and a fade over `vr_throw_point_time` (0.5, was 0.3: the residual tumble gone before it lets go). spinAlign waits while it acts.
Ranges to extremes: strength 0-5 (50), Time to 2 s (10), Angle to 180, Tumble to 10 turns/s (50), Spin Damping 0-3 (20).
His replayed throw: 95 deg off at 0.04 s, 25 at 0.14, 10 at 0.19, 2 from 0.29 s on (tumble 0.4 rad/s left); before: 8 deg only
in passing at 0.19 s, 55 at 0.29 and tumbling on at 11.4 rad/s.

Test `vr_embed_test 47` (extended; `gibthrow: 6 passed, 0 failed`): thrown from higher (0 0 64) the most open of eight ways, read
at 3 m and again at 5 m (point first at both: steadied, not passing through it as it turns over), three passes: off, default,
extreme (strength 5, Tumble 20, Time 1). Point first (within vr_embed_sword_angle 35), off / default / extreme:
- good (10-40 deg off, 1-5 rad/s): before 1 / 9 / 11 of 12, now 1 / 12 / 12;
- VR-style overhand (100-150 deg off, point up and back, 8-16 rad/s towards the flight, a little roll, 10-15 m/s): before
  1 / 1 / 11 of 12, now 1 / 12 / 12 (mean 79 -> 10 deg);
- spun on purpose (19-24 rad/s): 0 / 0 / 6 of 6 (tumble kept 17.6 of 17.6 rad/s at default; 1.4 at extreme);
- axes: identical in every pass (11.28 rad/s).

**The gib in the air** (vr_skewer.qc `VR_Skewer_AirTarget`): a gib thrown hard is the thrower's for its throw (VR_Carry_Throw:
owner), and VR_Blow_Strikable passes it, so the sweep never dealt the sword's blow on it (a blade-thrust touch defers to the
blow: VR_Gib_Struck). Now the sweep also takes such a gib when the blade is driven along its line at it (VR_Skewer_Thrust,
VR_Skewer_Can), and VR_Melee_Deal skewers it by the loose gib's rules (a stab, its line within vr_embed_stab_angle, by its tip,
through it); a blow that doesn't skewer it leaves it be (no burst: as before). Skewered, its throw is over (owner, carry_thrown,
vr_throw_self cleared). Test `vr_embed_test 48` (QC/vr_airskewer_test.qc, `airskewer: 4 passed, 0 failed`): the sword in the
mock hand, a gib thrown hard (his) met near the top of its rise: a 5 m/s thrust puts it on, a 0.6 m/s push or a 5 m/s swing
across doesn't, a hanging gib the same. Open: the test passes on the old code too (the gib's ownership seems to end before the
thrust in the mock: its touch of the hand or its throw's grace); the case he hit is not reproduced headless, the fix covers the
owned window. Case 3 (the hanging gib) failed once in five runs (the mock's thrust; seen on the old code too).
## pdisarm: the player disarmed by the armed humanoids' own rules (agent/pdisarm, 2026-11-15)

His voice note (e1m1 2026-11-15 03:28): players get disarmed by precise shots and melee hits on their gun or hand, "using
the same exact rules" as enemies; an option, on by default, single player and multiplayer.

- One rule (`QC/vr_armedgrunt_shot.qc`): `VR_Disarm_Add` (the adding up over `vr_agrunt_shotdisarm_window`, the threshold
  `_damage`, the cooldown), `VR_Disarm_Roll` (`_chance` + `_chance_scale` per threshold past, at most 0.95, times a
  scale) and `VR_Disarm_ProjChance` (a projectile's one roll: `_proj_*`), on any holder entity. The armed humanoids'
  `VR_AGS_Add`, `VR_AGS_Frame` and `VR_AGS_ProjRoll` now call them (same random() order: agshot unchanged).
- The player's side (`QC/vr_playerdisarm.qc`): each hand of each player a holder (`vr_pd_hand` entity, spawned at its
  first hit). Volumes: the held weapon's line as the melee and parry lay it out (`VR_Parry_WeaponLine`, so fists and
  empty hands never count) with `VR_AGS_W_RADIUS` + `vr_agrunt_vol_shot_weapon`, the hand as a sphere with
  `VR_AGS_H_RADIUS` + `vr_agrunt_vol_shot_hand`; `vr_agrunt_shotdisarm_parts`, `_near`, `_weapon_w`, `_hand_w` as for
  them. Hooks: `FireBulletsImpl` and `LightningDamage` (`VR_PD_Shot`: anyone's shot but the player's own, so agent/mp gets
  PvP as is), `PlayerPostThink` (`VR_PD_Frame`: projectiles within a frame back/ahead: nails, rockets, grenades,
  enforcer lasers, ogre grenades, vore balls, zombie gibs; then the rolls due), `VR_Parry` (`VR_PD_Blow`: a blow with a
  line that lands, i.e. no directional parry, guard or crossed arms, meeting the weapon within the parry contact distance
  + `vr_agrunt_vol_blow` with at least `vr_agrunt_disarm_damage`: the armed humanoids' blow rule, certain at chance 1).
  The shot itself is not stopped by your weapon (no blocking added): your body takes it as before.
- Knocked out: `DropWeaponInHandScaled` at `vr_weight_drop_velocity` (the grip-lost drop: a `thrown_weapon` with its
  record, clip and ammo kept, pickable), pushed along the shots' way (`vr_wpn_dropped`, new global); sparks, a ricochet,
  a buzz on that hand, `bf` flash, a line.
- Cvars: `vr_player_disarm` 1, `vr_player_disarm_chance` 1 (times the chance, at most certain; 0 never): Advanced VR
  Options > Combat > Armed Grunts > Disarming: Your Weapon. Debug: `vr_agrunt_shotdisarm_debug 1` prints `playerdisarm:`.
- Test `vr_pd_test 1` (Debug > Tests > Player Disarm): 10/10 (blast across the gun knocks it out at forced chance, lies
  on the floor with clip 5; blast across the body: no hit; enforcer laser: out; option off: nothing). agshot (vr_agrunt_test
  50) 10/0, vr_agrunt_test 200 33/0. Scene `player_disarm`. The melee path has no headless test (dirparry's held blows).

## throwfix2: the dagger settles point first; thrown blades never gib; no floating blade (agent/throwfix2, 2026-11-15)

His note (vrtesthall_2026-11-15_17-58-33): the sword's point-first throw is right, the dagger "much harder to throw point
first ... still tumbles"; thrown swords and daggers gib what they hit; a javelin-thrown sword stayed floating in the air,
embedded, over the body it killed.

- **The dagger.** A light blade leaves the hand spinning faster: the throw's spin limit is by weight (vr_throw_table: the
  knight's sword, 4 kg, 12.5 rad/s at most; the dagger, light, Max Spin's 20), and pointAlign's Tumble gate (3 turns/s:
  full help up to 9.4 rad/s, none from 18.8) shut most dagger releases out. New weapons.txt key `throw_point` (this
  pointed blade's leniency: times the Tumble limit and the spring's strength and its most; 1 by default, the swords
  unchanged bit for bit; the dagger, slot 51, 2: full help up to 18.8 rad/s, about 0.1 s to come round). Per weapon, so
  `vr_wofs_throw_point_NN` in the config. pointalign's debug line prints it (`x2.00`).
- **No gibs** (combat.qc `VR_Gib_Overkill`): a thrown sword or dagger (weapons.txt `embed` 1) counts
  `vr_gib_overkill_blade` (0) of its overkill whichever way it struck, not only blade first (`vr_throw_bladein`; a thrown
  blade counted as "blades", all its overkill). Quad counts all as before; no Gore preset or run mutator touches overkill.
  Blade first still counts in `vr_throw_bladein_count` (test 41). Damage unchanged. Measured (the old rule from the overkill
  lines): at 28 m/s, the not-blade-first sword and dagger left a grunt at -157/-50 and a knight at -112 (gibbed: under -35,
  -40): 5 of 12 such throws gibbed; now 0 of 18.
- **The floating blade** (vr_axestick.cpp serverFrame, QC VR_AxeStick_Think): headless at 28 m/s the point-first sword
  went into a grunt's gun; as it died its death frames squash the gun's triangles to a point (hitmodel::anchorFrame: no
  frame), the engine stopped placing the blade and QC kept it stuck: it stayed where it struck while the body flew 3 m
  back. Now the engine marks the blade (`.vr_stick_lost`, new field, the time it could not place it; 0 again once it can)
  and QC lets it fall (VR_AxeStick_Fall: with the body's motion) after `VR_STICK_LOST_GRACE` (0.04 s). A blade in the
  body's flesh stays with the corpse as before (knight, ogre: off the body at most 6.7 units over 2 s).
- **Test** `vr_embed_test 47` (extended; `gibthrow: 12 passed, 0 failed`): a new "any way" set (16 throws, the point 60-170
  degrees off, the dagger tumbling 14-20 rad/s at 12-20 m/s, the sword as its weight lets: 12.5 rad/s, 10-12 m/s), daggers
  point first (35 degrees, at 3 and 5 m) off / on / extreme: with `throw_point` 1 0 / 5 / 8 of 8, now 0 / 8 / 8; swords
  8 / 8 / 8 both; the spun daggers 0 -> 3 of 3 (spun swords stay a spin: 0, tumble 17.4 of 17.4 rad/s); the old sets
  unchanged. Then QC/vr_throwdmg_test.qc: a grunt, a knight and an ogre (stock health) each hit by the sword and the dagger
  at vr_throw_max_speed (28 m/s) point first, flat and handle first (pointAlign off for these): 0 gibbed, 12 of 18 killed,
  most damage 122; point first 6 of 6 in the body; flat and handle first 12 blunt blows, none stuck; floating (the tip
  over 24 units off the body as drawn, `modelanchor`, 4+ frames, or stuck in a body gone or gibbed): 0 (2 before the fix).
  Tests 41 19/0, 34 15/0, 48 4/0, 40 24/0, 21 43/1 (the known slow-swing burst).
- Scene `throw_hard` (a grunt, a knight, an ogre; the sword and the dagger). Builds: dev and ReleaseLTO
  `-p:QvrReleaseVersion=1.1.0` 0 warnings (after merging next; test 47 12/0 again).
- Open: a blade in a body the engine models only by its box (`MonsterBox`: no Quake .mdl) still follows the box as the body
  dies; a blade striking a gun sticks in it (a clang and a bounce would be truer). Not changed.

## flat1116: Burst Rifle name, toolgun gun+blade, gun-and-axe melee, flat B = next ammo, disarm sounds (agent/flat1116, 2026-11-16)

His flat-screen notes (2026-11-16) and the coordinator's disarm-sound item.

- **Burst Rifle.** The holster menu names weapons from `vr_notectx.cpp` `weaponNames` ("grunt's shotgun"): now
  "Burst Rifle", as are the QC weapon table (pickups, `WeaponIdToWeaponName`), `VR_EnemyGun_Name` (console), the toolgun's
  and Debug's spawn entries, Weapon Holds and the armed grunts' weights. With `vr_grunt_burst 0` the grunts still fire
  pellets, but the gun in your hands always bursts, so the name holds.
- **Toolgun gun + axe.** The game supports it (`vr_ag_gunaxe`: the replacements' `vr_agrunt_repl_gunaxe`, a gun and an axe
  or a dagger; the ranged knights' crossbow and sword), but only a replacement's roll set the flag, and the toolgun's
  Left Hand list paired melee with melee and guns with guns only. Now `armedPairs` / QC `VR_AM_UiPairs` also offer a
  one-handed blade beside a dual-wieldable gun in the right hand (never a blade then a gun, nor a big gun), and
  `VR_AM_ArmAll` sets `vr_ag_gunaxe` for such keys (map `weapon2` too; FGD regenerated). Test
  `vr_toolgun_armed_pair_test` (Debug > Tests): 7/7 (shotgun/Burst Rifle + axe, shotgun + dagger: gun and axe; two guns;
  two blades; axe + shotgun and rocket launcher + axe not offered).
- **No damage from gun-and-axe grunts.** Cause: the axe swings in its left hand (`vr_ag_left`) while the gun is the
  pose's right-hand prop, so `VR_AGP` only ran `VR_DRP_Frame` when the right prop was melee: a blow held back for your
  weapon near its way (`VR_DRP_Blow`, `vr_dirparry_window`) was never let go, parried or dropped, and every later blow
  was folded into it: no damage, no `VR_PD_Blow` roll, ever (pre-fix: 29 blows, 1 held, 0 ended). The axe-only grunt was
  fine. Fix: the left blade of a gun-and-axe grunt runs `VR_DRP_Frame` when it is the swinging prop. Rules unchanged: a
  parry across the blow blocks, a landed blow hurts and may disarm (`vr_player_disarm_chance`). Counters
  `vr_drp_held_n` / `_done`. Test `vr_pd_test 2` (`Misc/quakevr/pd_melee_test.sh <agent> [flat]`): 8/8 VR mock
  (gun+axe 44 damage, 4 rolls 4 disarms; axe-only the same), 8/8 flat (gun+axe 2 parried, 2 landed). Scene
  `agrunt_gunaxe_melee`.
- **Flat B = Next Ammo Type.** `vr_flat_key_ammo` "b" (Flat Keys page; in the flat key list so its bind is left off):

## MP B13: the join through reordering (selective acks); deathmatch with bots (agent/mp, 2026-11-16)

- **A join through 30 ms jitter and 5% loss stalled in its signon** (keepalives only): NetQuake's receiver acked the
  chunks it dropped (one that overtook a late one); with the acks reordered too, the dropped chunk's ack came after the
  late one's and read as the next in order, so the server took serverinfo as delivered while the client still lacked
  a chunk. Fixed with selective acks (`net_dgrm.c`): the receiver holds early chunks and acks only what it has; the
  sender resends only the chunks not acked. Non-Quake VR peers keep a one-chunk window; the accept reply carries the
  server's network version (`QVR_NET_VERSION` 34). A stale unreliable datagram no longer ends the frame's read.
  `mp_retransmit` stages the stall deterministically (the old code: never delivered); `mp_voice_lossy` now joins under
  its loss. Multiplayer only (the loopback is another driver). Details: MP_PLAN.md, "B13 results".
- **Deathmatch with bots** (`mp_dm`, new): dm4, two FrikBot bots (impulse 100), a real death respawned by the trigger,
  the fraglimit's intermission at both clients with the same scoreboard: it all worked unchanged. New client watch
  lines `mp_frags`, `mp_event: intermission= / died / respawned` (`vr_mptest.cpp`).

**Wet shine.** Not the wetglint change itself: the drips (vr_drips.cpp `scan`) take a model's box from its frames' bounds,
and its bottom (`lo.z + 1`) was tested against the world's leaves only. e1m1's bridge over the slime (the grunts by the
four buttons' door, entities 113 and 118) and e1m2's lifts and bridges over water: the box's bottom lies under the floor,
inside the bridge's brush, in the slime leaf below it, so the grunts were "in slime up to 16" for ever (soaked every
scan, never drying; the corpse kept it). Now `groundBox`: over a liquid by the leaves, the bottom is brought up to the floor
a line from the box's middle meets (`worldtrace::world`: the world and the moving brush models); only things over a liquid
pay for the trace. Keyed values checked: drips' records are keyed by the cl_entities slot and were forgotten only when the
slot went unsent (a slot freed and reused within a scan kept them): now also forgotten on the server's removal (wounds'
KindClear, as the wound masks and dents already were: `drips::forget`). The save's "// qvrwet" lines are matched by edict
number at the load, which a load restores as saved: right. The wound masks' `wetLeft` decays and is freed with the mask.

113 and 118 were wet standing; now 1 passed + 1 passed. e1m2 by the ogre's spot: nothing wet.

**Looping sounds.** A loop (a sample with a cue point) plays on its entity's channel until another sound replaces it. The
server now keeps which entity channels play a loop (vr_server.cpp `VR_SoundLoopNote`, the loop flag read once a map from
the wav's cue chunk, GetWavinfo): a sound that replaces a loop (misc/null.wav, the stall) goes with the reliable messages
(a broadcast's sounds are dropped when it is full, as in a big fight: then the knight's idle played on with nothing to
end it), and an edict freed with a loop still on it has the loop stopped, reliably (`VR_SoundLoopsFreed` from ED_Free:

whatever removes it). QC: the freed-holder path silenced its chainsaw too, and a drop resets the knight's saw sound state
(taken up again, its idle plays afresh). `vr_snd_loops` lists the loops playing. Test `vr_v1116_test 1` (vrtesthall;

## One-way teleporter exits: hands stay, no self view (agent/vr1116b, 2026-11-16)

Note start_2026-11-16_00-54-53: at start's exit by the start (the hub's teleporter back, side 3: its exit plane y 280,
normal +y, no gate there), crossing that plane hid his hands and showed him himself in a teleporter.
- Cause: an unpaired side's exit (`reverseSide`, a plane in the open) was still an aperture for two client-side things.
  `eyeThrough`'s "back" case (body in front of an exit, eye behind it: meant for the frame after a carry, eye still
  behind a paired gate's face) drew the eye from the entrance in the hub: looking through that gate he saw the start
  room and his own body, his hands not drawn there. And `VR_PortalAlias` let the player's own models (hands, guns, held
  things) be cut by an unpaired exit (the 10-07 change exempted `own` from its "only what moves out" rule): the part
  behind the plane was drawn back at the hub.
- Fix (vr_portals.cpp): `eyeThrough` takes the back case only for a paired side; `VR_PortalAlias` never cuts own models
  at an unpaired exit; `VR_PortalAddPVS` sends the entrance's room for an exit straddle only for a paired side. Paired
  gates (vrteleporters, two-way custom maps) are unchanged; entrances unchanged.
- `vr_portals_selfview_test start | end | sides` (Debug > Teleporters, "Check Teleporter Exits (Test)" runs `sides`):
  each side's exit with a body 6 units in front and an eye 6 behind (carried only if paired and open); `end` also checks
  the live set-up (eye straddles a one-way exit) and, since `start`, eyes drawn / from another room, own models drawn /
  cut. `Misc/quakevr/teleporters/selfview_test.sh <agent>`: start, body 8 in front of the exit, head 0.35 m back tilted
  up (eye 3.0 behind the plane, body 4.8 in front), hands on the plane: 11 passed, 0 failed; without the fix 3/8 (120 of
  120 eyes drawn from the hub, 4320 own-model draws cut).
- Sweep (`sides`): start, e1m2, e1m3, e1m5, e1m7, e2m3, e2m6, e3m2, e3m6, e4m3, e4m7, dm2, dm5 all pass (all unpaired);
  vrteleporters 32/0 (35 paired sides carried as before); AD: ad_azad 3/0, AD's start, ad_tears, ad_magna no recognised
  sides. turned_exit_test 2/0; teleporter_cross_test cases as its header expects.

## Quest Pro: hissy sound (a 1.1.0-rc.1 regression for everyone); eye-tracked foveation (agent/questpro, 2026-11-16)

- **Sound: the cause.** nohunk (6a634cdf0, 2026-11-13: the hunk and cache became the heap) stopped setting
  `host_parms->memsize`; `parms` is static, so it read 0, and S_Init's old "less than 8 MB of heap" rule set
  `loadas8bit 1` on every start: every sound loaded as 8-bit and the SDL device opened as 8-bit unsigned (snd_sdl.c),
  a -37 dB quantization hiss and crackle under every sound, flat and VR, every device. His logs (all five kept, 11-15
  and 11-16) print "loading all sounds as 8bit". In 1.1.0-rc.1, not in beta4 (nohunk came after it); the player's
  GitHub issue #83 (flat, Realtek + a Logitech USB headset) is the same bug. Not specific to Virtual Desktop.
- **The fix (on, a bug fix):** the rule removed (snd_dma.c), `membase`/`memsize` removed from `quakeparms_t` so nothing
  reads them again. `loadas8bit` is still there for anyone who asks for it.
- **The log** now names the system's default output device and its own rate/channels (SDL_GetDefaultAudioInfo):
  "SDL audio device: 48000 Hz, 2 channels (the mix's 44100 Hz 16-bit converted by SDL)". It used to name device 0.
- **Test:** `vr_snd_outtest` (vr_audiotest_out.cpp, through snd_mix.c's S_TransferTest: the real output stage into a
  test buffer): a -6 dBFS 1 kHz sine at 44.1 and 48 kHz: 16-bit THD+N -86 dB (its truncation, under one step), 8-bit
  -37 dB (the regression's), plus the live device's format (16-bit) and loadas8bit 0. 6 passed, 0 failed (run with
  `-Sound`: live 16-bit stereo 44100 Hz on a 48 kHz default device).
- **If anything still sounds off on the Quest Pro:** start with `-mixspeed 48000` (mix at Virtual Desktop's device rate:
  no SDL resampling); `_snd_mixahead 0.15` if it crackles under load (underruns). Neither changed by default.

- **Foveation: what his runtime offers.** VDXR 1.1.0 (his qvr_openxr.txt, 34 extensions): XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction
  and XR_FB_eye_tracking_social; no runtime foveation (no XR_FB_foveation, XR_META_foveation_eye_tracked or
  XR_VARJO_foveated_rendering; those are for Vulkan/D3D swapchains anyway, the game is OpenGL). His GPU has
  GL_NV_shading_rate_image (vr_foveated, 16x16 tiles), so the eye tracking drives our own foveation.
- **Built: `vr_foveated_gaze`** (0, archived; VR Settings > Graphics, advanced: "Eye-Tracked Foveation"; needs a VR
  restart). On, the OpenXR backend enables XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction (only then: some runtimes start the tracker or
  ask permission), checks the system's supportsEyeGazeInteraction, binds an "eye_gaze" pose action to
  /interaction_profiles/ext/eye_gaze_interaction, and locates it each frame (valid only while ORIENTATION_TRACKED: a
  blink falls back to the lens centre). FrameState::gaze carries it; vr_foveated.cpp moves the full-rate centre to
  where the gaze meets each eye's image, snapped to a tile (the rate image is remade only when it moves a tile, ~30k
  tiles of CPU then), the rates from the angle between the tile's direction and the gaze's. Off or untracked: the
  rates as before, bit for bit (the lens-centre path is unchanged). The log line "OpenXR: eye tracking
  (XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction): ..." says on / offered not used / no tracker / not offered.
- **Test:** `vr_foveated_gaze_test` (rates around a gaze 30 degrees right: full there, 2x2 in the middle, 4x4
  opposite; the mock's gaze, `vr_mock_gaze "right up"` degrees, followed within a tile): 9 passed, 0 failed.
- **For him:** Virtual Desktop must forward eye tracking to the PC (its Streamer setting; the headset's eye tracking on
  and calibrated). Then `vr_foveated_gaze 1`, restart VR, check the log line, and `vr_foveated_debug 1` shows the
  yellow/red rates following the eyes. With gaze on, Aggressive (or `vr_foveated_inner 15`, `_outer 30`) should still
  look sharp where he looks.

## arenafix: the audit's arena_6 and arena_10 (agent/arenafix, 2026-11-16)

The 1.1 readiness audit's baseline regressions. Both were the tests, not the game; both already failed in the
2026-11-14 and 11-15 baselines (so older than the RC). Only `QC/vr_arena_test.qc` changed.

- **arena_10 (timeout).** `VR_AT10_Tables` ran 36 cells of 400 armour rolls and 120 plans in one QC call; past 16
  million statements that is a runaway loop error (Host_Error). The test never printed a verdict and the run waited
  for its timeout. The armed-humanoid and mutator work of 11-13 made the rolls and plans slightly more expensive,
  which was enough. In real play a plan runs once per wave and stays far below the limit. Fix: the tables run in
  parts, one per frame (`vr_at10_part`: the gates, then one part per skill with its rolls and plans, then the rest),
  and the live wave-5 check follows. Result: 160 passed, 0 failed, the same as the 10-30 baseline.
- **arena_6 (6/2), "no broken guns".** The audit's runner runs it undrawn (`vr_mock_fast 2`). That run plays out
  differently, and one of the axes a foe dropped stuck in a wall (`vr_embed`, on since 11-08). A stuck blade has no
  rigid body while it is stuck, and the scan counted that as "no rigid body". Stuck blades (`VR_AxeStick_IsStuck`)
  are now skipped in that check.
- **arena_6, "the map grows no faster than a wave clear's drops".** Test 6 is the only arena test besides 42 that
  follows the run's director, so since 11-11 it soaks the budget director. Its later waves are bigger, so more gibs,
  limbs, debris and live foes are in the count at each wave's start. The mock player's hands also swap guns that land
  at its feet, and each swap leaves its own gun on the floor. The arena's gun cap never counts a gun a player dropped
  (`vr_monster_drop` 0). That is by design, and so is keeping stuck blades. The floor went 191 -> 214 (limit 13). The
  per-class counts at each window's wave starts showed no class growing steadily except these guns. Fix:
  `VR_AT6_Passing` leaves out of the count the things that go away by themselves, the live foes, the player's own
  guns and stuck blades (with their records). Each wave in the windows prints its count. Result: undrawn 119 -> 123,
  drawn 119 -> 121; 8 passed, 0 failed both ways (the soak's longest wave was 224-233 s, under AR_STALL 300).
- **ragdoll_stagger 54/3** (was 52/5): this is the known open item (BACKLOG section 1, "ragdoll_stagger: what is
  left"), and it is slightly better than before. Not touched.
- **teleporters_chase 5/1**: the same case fails the same way in the 11-14 baseline ("chase dog at framed_sill32:
  never reached the north room", seed 3), which is older than the one-way teleporter change (vr1116b). It is not
  related to that change. Not touched.

  tools are nearly all of it (feature: the four Custom tools 0.20 of 0.30; BloodRelief alone 0.135, as it lit the whole
  blood crop), intro: every Custom tool 0.1-0.5, the full-frame RevealRamp Custom 0.3 (a static ramp). Blurs and noise
  are minor (GPU).
- **Lossless speed-ups** (the Custom tool's `if` is lazy): each lighting tool works only where its colour tool shows it
  (feature MetalRelief / BloodRelief, intro L1Relief / L2Relief: a gate on the colour tool's coverage input, now
  their Image2; the sweeping light's term only while it is on), each colour tool only where its coverage is above 0
  (MetalColor, BloodColor, L1Color, L2Color, intermediates included), L1Tail, SplatCov and RuleCol likewise; the
  intro's RevealRamp is now GPU gradients (two Horizontal and two Vertical Backgrounds, Darken merges, an additive merge
  with Gain 0). L2Cov's lossless gates measured slower (0.43 -> 0.64 s): left as it was (noted in the generator).
- **After**: feature 0.13 at 1080p (-45%), 0.21 at 4K (3.2x); intro 0.48 at 1080p (1.7x), 1.9 at 4K (2.6x). Final
  frames: the feature's 6 stills (in, sweep, hold, out) pixel-identical to before; the intro's 7 stills identical
  except frame 90 (line 3's reveal edge: 0.004% of pixels, at most 11 levels: the gradients sample half a pixel apart).
- **Draft (fast preview)** checkbox published on both (Ctl.Draft): the lighting tools return a flat key light and do
  no lighting work, the feature's HeightBlur and the intro's L1Height off. Flat metal and blood; text, layout, timing,
  reveal, blood shapes and drips as in the final. A small saving now that the lighting is cheap (4K feature 0.21 ->
  0.17, intro 1.93 -> 1.90; 1080p about the same). Fusion's HiQ/proxy flags don't help: an Edit-page title's comp
  reports HiQ true, Proxy false, and nothing tells a preview from a Deliver render, so Draft stays the user's switch
  (`apply_titles --draft on|off`), and a bake always renders with it off.
- **`apply_titles.py --bake`**: each title (after the usual update) is rendered once from its section timeline to
  ProRes 4444 with alpha, "<QVR - section> [<digest>].mov" in "QVR Titles (baked)" next to the trailer's first media
  file (`--bake-dir`; with no media file, Videos/QVR Titles (baked)/<timeline>), imported into the section's bin (the
  section's settings in its Comments) and placed on the QVR Titles track in place of the nested timeline. The digest
  hashes the title comp's tools (node positions and the Draft toggle left out), frame size, rate and length: unchanged
  titles reuse their clip. A plain run keeps a baked title while its digest matches, else puts it back live and says
  so; `--unbake` and `--rebuild` put the live titles back. Only the bake's own render job is removed from the queue.
- **Checked**: `ts_bake_test.py` on a test trailer (10 Step generator, an intro of 2 s and a 2.5 s title at a
  marker): bake placed both clips (ap4h, 2.000 s and 2.500 s); stills of the trailer live vs baked: titles over the
  grey steps match (feature frames at most 2 levels; intro 1.5% of pixels 5-18 levels, ProRes). Found: the first
  digest took the whole exported comp, whose header (CurrentTime, CurrentID, Prefs) changes by itself, so the rerun
  saw "changed"; now only the tools block is hashed (not re-run: see below). **Resolve closed** during the second
  `--bake`'s render (the retest of the reuse path); not reopened (GUI), so the reuse path and `--unbake` are unchecked.
  A bake of both titles took 271 s of wall time (the renders alone should take about 80 s: not explained).

## Flat-screen hip fire through teleporters (agent/flatportalaim, 2026-11-16)

His report: hip-firing through a teleporter in flat-screen aimed off; ADS seemed fine.
- Cause: the aim's convergence trace (flatsight `lineStop`, used by `crosshairPoint` and the blocked check) did not go
  through gates: it stopped at the gate's face, so each gun pointed from its muzzle at a point on the gate. The shot
  (QC pellets, `MOVE_PORTALS`) crossed there and the gate turned the muzzle-to-face way, not the crosshair's: off by the
  muzzle's angle to the ray times the distance past the exit. ADS has the muzzle nearly on the ray (2 units off).
- Fix: `worldtrace::shotLine` (vr_trace.hpp; in vr_portals.cpp) traces a line as the shots go, through the gates, with
  the crossing loop of `VR_PortalTrace` moved into `crossGates` (one function for QC's tracelines and this; QC's
  `portal_entry`/`portal_exit`/`portal_turn` state untouched by the client's lines, no "from an image" rule for a
  camera far from the body). It gives `seen` (the stop unfolded onto the line: where the gate's view shows it) and `at`
  (the far room's place). `lineStop` takes `seen`: the guns aim at the image, their lines cross the gate and come out
  on the target. With no gate crossed `seen` is SV_Move's endpos as before (non-portal aiming identical). The visor
  crosshair's shot line (flatxhair `shotHit`) goes through too, so the gun's crosshair sits on what it will hit there.
  `vr_flat_xhair_probe` adds a line per hand: `gates shot N centre N lands x y z apart U` (the shot as sent and the
  screen's middle, both traced through the gates, real places).
- VR: no convergence (the gun shoots where the hand points; the shots already cross gates); VR's laser
  (`vr_crosshair.cpp aimEnd`) still stops at a gate's face: unchanged, not part of the aim.
- Test `Misc/quakevr/teleporters/flat_gate_aim_test.sh <agent>` (vrteleporters, flat, shotgun): 6 passed, 0 failed.
  Apart (units), before / after: hip 160 back from flush_player's gate 11.37 / 0.01; 24 back 35.07 / 0.01; ADS 2.00 /
  0.00; turn90 gate - / 0.00; no gate 0.00 / 0.00; loop (the real shotgun at your own back through T's loop) 223 apart,
  health 100 / 100 before, 100 / 70 after.
- Checklist Test scene `flat_gate_hipfire` (vrteleporters -256 440, yaw 90, two grunts beyond the gate).
## Sliding in VR (branch agent/vrslide, 2026-11-16)

His request: an experimental option to slide in VR too, off by default, the turning stick pulled down precisely.

**One slide.** The slide's server side moved out of `vr_flatmove.cpp` into `Quake/vr/vr_slide.cpp` / `vr_slide.hpp`
(namespace `qvr::slide`): its state per client, the start (speed over `vr_flat_slide_min`, the boost), the step
(`slideStep`: friction, slope, steer, top speed, end), the step up, the stamina parts, the cooldown, the jump/ledge/prone/
water exits, `.vr_sliding` (the charge), the prop push (`slide::onServer`, `vr_box3d_standing.cpp`). The C hooks are
renamed `VR_SlideMove` / `VR_SlideStepUp`. Flatscreen and headset run the same code with the same `vr_flat_slide_*`
tunables; only the input differs: flat, the crouch key (`hull::flatCrouchHeld`, gated by `vr_flat_slide`); a headset, the
move's bit 14 (`protocol::moveSlideBit`, the same bit as the flat crouch's: a headset client never set it), sent only with
`vr_slide` on and its stick gesture held (`vr_client.cpp`), read by `slide::setHeadsetInput` (`vr_server.cpp`). The flat
client side (view drop, pose, tests) stays in `vr_flatmove.cpp`, which takes the slide through using-declarations.

**The gesture** (`slide::stickGesture`, from `vr_input.cpp`'s walking branch): the turning stick pulled at least
`vr_slide_stick_threshold` (0.85) down, within `vr_slide_stick_angle` (20) degrees of straight down, armed only from the
middle (a pull out past 0.5 off that cone disarms it until the stick is back under 0.3: a snap or smooth turn swept round
the rim to straight down never slides). Held while still pulled under -0.5 and within the angle plus 15. While held the
turning stick's down is no `+movedown` (DPAD_DOWN) and no turn. Only on foot out of the water (swimming or flying the
stick's down is `+movedown` as before), not while the Smooth + Teleport aim has the stick, and released when a menu or a
tool takes the sticks. Today the turning stick's down was `+movedown` only (no crouch toggle or menu on it); `vr_slide 0`
leaves it so to the bit.

**A headset's slide:** his box is the flat slide's crouched one while it is on (`vr_hull.cpp` updateCrouchBox: his eyes
taken as `slide::slideEye()`, 46 less `vr_flat_crouch_drop` and `vr_flat_slide_drop`, 22: the lowest crouched box),
his head as it is; after it he stands as his head asks (flat ends into a crouch because the key is still held). No view
drop and no FOV bonus (flat-only code: `flatmove::slideDrop`, `vr_flatspeedfov.cpp`). The comfort vignette counts a

## titlebake: trailer title bakes verified and fixed, longer holds (agent/titlebake, 2026-11-16)

In "QVR Titles Preview" (Resolve Studio 21.1.0.17, restarted by him; his open project was the empty "Untitled
Project", so nothing to save), on test timelines of my own (removed afterwards).
- **Why the first bake took 271 s**: the test's intro section was "QVR - Intro", a timeline left by an older test
  (ti_apply) holding the **pre-titlespeed intro macro with Dark Backdrop on**: section timelines are found by name, and
  timeline names are unique in a project, so a second trailer timeline with the same marker shares the section. That
  title renders at 0.73 s/frame vs 0.45 for a fresh one (60-frame renders), and its frames are 4x bigger. With fresh
  titles a bake of a 2 s intro + 2.5 s title took 85-104 s (73 + 27 s of render, the rest import/placing).
  apply_titles now says when a baked title was made with an older template (`--rebuild` first) and makes a shared
  section follow the current trailer's frame size.
- **The digest was still unstable**: Fusion saves each expression input's last evaluated value next to the
  expression (they follow the comp's current time and whether it was rendered), and reflows short blocks onto one line
  or several. A plain rerun after `--bake` went back live, and a second `--bake` re-rendered. Now those values and the
  whitespace are left out: plain reruns keep baked titles baked, `--bake` reuses them (0.6 s, nothing rendered),
  `--bake` with Draft on reuses the full-quality bake; a changed subtitle goes back live on a plain run
  ("unbaked(changed)") and `--bake` re-renders only that title (23 s).
- **Edits lost after a render, and the crash**: one render per title, each started right after the last, then editing
  the trailer timeline at once: in one run a baked clip was "placed" but not on the track, in another AppendToTimeline
  failed, and a render job could not be deleted (left in the queue); the previous worker's Resolve closed in the second
  render of such a sequence. Now every title to render goes into one batch (one Deliver visit, one StartRendering), the
  jobs are deleted once Resolve lets go of them (retried up to 30 s), the page and timeline switch back is awaited,
  and only then are the clips imported and placed; afterwards the track is checked. No crash or lost edit since
  (6 bakes, back-to-back runs included).
- `--unbake` put both live nested timelines back; `--draft on` / `off` set both titles' Draft (checked on the
  comps), and a bake leaves it as it was.
- Seen, not changed: the same title baked in different Resolve states came out 3.6x bigger at the same picture (PSNR
  59 dB; low-bit noise in the alpha and colour): first renders after the restart ~0.7 MB/frame, later 2.5 MB/frame.

His timing notes (extra scope):
- **Title clips are 10 s now**: a title inserted between a timeline's In/Out marks takes their length
  (Timeline.SetMarkInOut, counted from the timeline's start), so make_section_timeline no longer depends on Resolve's
  standard generator duration (5 s). Titles made before need `--rebuild` for more than 5 s (apply_titles says so).
- **Intro**: new published **Hold** (frames, 180 = 3 s at 60 fps) counted from when every line is in (frame 118,
  1.97 s); the out (0.6 s) follows: 5.57 s in all (was 5 s, with 2.4 s of hold). The out always ends by the clip's
  end (a hand-inserted 5 s title shortens the hold, as before). titles.txt `[Intro]` `hold:` (3); `seconds:` now
  defaults to in + hold + out; given, it still sets the out's end.
- **Feature titles**: **Subtitle Delay** now counts from the end of the title's in, 60 frames (1 s) by default:
  title in over 0.67 s, alone 1 s, subtitle in over 0.67 s (in by 2.33 s), hold to 5.57 s, out 0.43 s: 6 s by
  default (was 4.5), so the subtitle keeps its 3.2 s fully on screen. titles.txt `subdelay:` (1); a given `seconds:`
  shortens the hold, and apply_titles warns when the subtitle would be fully on screen for less than 1.5 s. The rule
  under the title keeps its own start (frame 5).
- **Checked** (test trailer: intro + a default 6 s title + a 4.5 s one over a 10 Step generator): `--rebuild` made
  10 s clips (placed 334, 360, 270 frames); preview mp4 and contact sheet (intro: all in at 1.97 s, full hold to
  4.97 s, out; feature: title alone at 1.5 s, subtitle in at 2.0 s, hold, out) in
  qvr-kit/scratch/titletiming_shots/; `--bake` of the three: 293 s, ap4h yuva444p12le 334 / 360 / 270 frames; a plain
  rerun kept all three baked. Test timelines, bins and jobs (mine and ts_* / QVR - Stab Test) removed from the
  preview project, which is closed again (Resolve left on its untitled project, as found).

## Quest C4v: the world split by surface where lights reach it; the rig's small lights' switch (branch `agent/quest`, 2026-11-16)

- Under the ES profile (the Quest) `vr_gl_world_unlit 2` (new default): where dynamic lights reach the walls, only the
  surfaces a light's sphere touches are drawn with the world's lights' loop; the rest with the loop-free program, in one
  flush. The GPU cull sends the lit surfaces to a second command per texture and now runs after the lights are known.
  e1m2's start (0.55): GPU 5.76 -> 5.17 ms, world 4.08 -> 3.41. The picture the same (PC `-glescompat`: max 4 of 765).
  The PC's own path unchanged.
- `vr_rig_lights_world` (cvar, default 1, Quest preset row 1 at every level: his look call): 0 keeps the guns' screen
  lights and the wrist gadget's lights off the walls (they still light the hands and gear) under the Quest's plain
  lights' loop: ~0.34 ms more at e1m2's start, and most of e1m1's walk unlit. Debug > Profiling has both settings.
- e1m1's frozen fight: 9 monsters cost ~2.7 ms of GPU and 71 draws at 0.55; the models' plain form saves 3.1 ms.
- The perf recorder has a `split` column. PC: scenario_check PASS, load_models_test 4/0, gles_render_test 21/0.
  Details: QUEST_PLAN.md 6zb.

## Quest C4w: the monsters' draws batched, the world models' pre-pass off on the Quest, the split's empty lit draws (branch `agent/quest`, 2026-11-16)

- **Alias sort key (PC bug, from Ironwail)**: every alias model's key was the name's hash masked to 4 bits (16 keys),
  so models sharing one drew in entity order, a batch each (an armed grunt and its gun interleaved); the models made in
  memory ("#rig2", "#armor", "#bridge") had no key of their own. `Mod_AliasSortKey` (gl_model.c): 15 bits, both.
- `vr_alias_batch_posed` (default 1, Debug > Profiling): the world's posed models of one model and skin (armed grunts on
  the authored rig, their armour, ragdolls; not your own) batch, their bones in one buffer (r_alias.c `R_AliasPosedJoin`).
- `vr_alias_prepass_world` (default 1: the PC as before; **the Quest preset 0**): the world's models without the depth
  pre-pass (the Quest draws the eyes apart, so each model batch was two draws).
- `vr_gl_world_lit_skip` (default 1; ES only): the split by surface draws only the lit commands of textures a reaching
  light can fill (a CPU walk of the view's PVS leaves, r_world.c `R_WorldLitTextures`).
- `vr_gl_passes` also lists the frame's alias batches. `vr_rig_lights_world` left at 1 (his call).
- Headset, e1m1's frozen fight lifted into the unworn headset's downward view (0.55): GPU 4.81 -> 4.00 ms, draws 219 ->
  149 (the models' share 2.2 -> 1.4 ms); e1m2's start 192 -> 180 draws. PC eyes 0.000% over 8 for each switch.
- PC: dev build 0 warnings; gles_render_test 21/0; load_models_test 4/0; scenario_check PASS (138 run; a first run failed bench_crowd_ad's placement once, the rerun passed). Details: QUEST_PLAN.md 6zc.

## Quest C4x: the gore form of the models' shader; the live fight measured (branch `agent/quest`, 2026-11-16)

- `vr_gl_alias_gore` (tunable, default 1; ES only, Debug > Tunables): a solid model batch that needs only wounds (or
  the wet coat) and dents among the plain form's features is drawn by the plain form keeping those

- `vr_gl_alias_skin` (tunable, default 1; ES only, Debug > Tunables): your body, which kept the whole models' shader for

  clients in and each one's next move read, one move of each a step by number; `vr_mp_lockstep_until S` holds it after
  step S; its clients' `vr_mp_lockstep_ahead K` keeps them at most K moves ahead (a waiting frame passes no time).
  With `vr_fixed_frames 1` and `sv_random_seed 1` two runs are the same bit for bit.

  was the load's wall-clock time: the melee history went apart by an ulp).

  steps, with walking, strafing and a rottweiler hunting. Details: MP_PLAN.md, "B14b results".
## introfix: the titles under a proxy, the intro's cost (agent/introfix, 2026-11-16)

His report: previewing the QVR Intro Title lags and never shows the whole picture (Smart cache, Timeline Proxy
Resolution Half/Quarter, proxies on); a full render works but takes over a minute for 5.6 s.
- **The proxy bug (both titles).** The macros measure the text image (its Width and DataWindow: real pixels, so half
  of them under a Half proxy) and fed those numbers to built-in tools whose pixel inputs are full-resolution pixels
  that Fusion scales by the proxy itself: Crop offsets/sizes, the crops' canvas Backgrounds, the grime and splatter
  FastNoise sizes, the rule's canvas, and every blur (`G.Res*...`). Under a proxy of scale K they were scaled by K
  twice: at Half the crops were a quarter of the text from the wrong origin (the letters cut off, the metal, blood and
  rule misplaced) and the glows, shadows and relief blurs half size. Fix: a `ProxyProbe` Background 1024 wide measures
  K (`G1.K`, the feature title's `Lgt.K`); the built-in tools get measured pixels divided by K (`/G.K`, blurs
  `G.FR = Res/K`); the Custom tools keep real pixels (`w1`, `G.Res`). K is 1 without a proxy, also at a lower frame
  size, so the final picture is unchanged: the intro's 7 stills (frames 20-280) at 1080p and 2 at 960x540, and the
  feature title's 3 at 1080p, are pixel-identical before/after.
- **Not reproduced in Resolve itself**: no scripting reaches Playback > Timeline Proxy Resolution or a proxied
  render (Edit-page title comps report `COMPB_Proxy` false and ignore SetAttrs; the Fusion page takes it but its
  viewer can't be read back; `comp.Render` with a Saver on an Edit-page title comp **crashed Resolve 21.1**: never
  again), and GUI control was declined. The fix follows Fusion's proxy rule; **he should check it**: the intro at
  Half and Quarter vs Full, paused on a hold frame. The lag with Smart cache is Resolve showing what it has while it
  renders in the background (the cost below).
- **Cost** (Deliver renders, s/frame, frames 40-99; this session's numbers, ~10% noise): intro 0.46-0.48 at 1080p,
  0.46 at 960x540, 0.42 at 480x270, 0.69 at 4K (60-89; titlespeed measured 1.9 there in another session); feature 0.145
  at 1080p. **The cost is per frame, not per pixel** below 4K: passing all 8 Custom tools through drops 0.46 to 0.16,
  yet a quarter of the pixels saves nothing. So a proxy won't make the titles real-time, and neither did two lossless
  per-pixel cuts I measured and dropped: L2Cov's per-column hashes, waves and pool width moved into a one-row
  lookup (24 sines a pixel to none; stills within 7 levels) 0.59 s, L2Cov's unread green channel zeroed 0.52 s, and
  a Draft switch skipping the relief tools (Dissolve to a flat key light) 0.475 vs 0.467. Untested lead: the per-frame
  cost may be the ~30 `G1`/`G2` expressions reading `L1Text.Output[0]` / `L2Text.Output[0]` (each a request of the
  text at frame 0) that every Custom tool's inputs pull in; freezing them would tell.
- Regenerated (`make_intro_title.py`: 92 tools), installed, and in "QVR Titles Preview" on a test trailer: apply
  (`--rebuild`) placed both (334 and 360 frames), `--bake` rendered both in 219 s (ap4h, 1920x1080, yuva444p12le);
  that run left the intro at the timeline's start unplaced ("could not be placed at 216000", apply_titles said so),
  the next `--bake` reused it and placed it (0.2 s). Test timelines, bin and clips removed; his "v1_1trailer" saved
  before and reopened after.
- After it ships: run `install_titles.py`, restart Resolve, `apply_titles.py --rebuild`.

  sample at its clock, with the lightmap's cached spot): compared now. The ammo pouch stays set apart (its body's pose
  eased over the frames since the load: 1/64 unit in z at step 72 while B starts walking, equal again by step 360).

  hold where they differ). Test `mp_test.py lockstep_dm` (in the suite): two lockstep runs on dm4, A adds two bots at

## MP B14d: the bots out of dm4's lava, vr_dm_test 3's flaky parry (agent/mp, 2026-11-16)

- **The bots' lava deaths were vr_pmove_bots'**: a dedicated dm4 server, A and two bots, counted from A's obituaries
  (`scratch/b14d_lava.py <pmove_bots> <seconds>`): 21 in 150 s with the bots' walk through the players' moves, 0-2 per
  45-150 s with FrikBot's own physics. Three causes, all fixed:
  - the walk's "held by a wall" report to FrikBot (vr_predict.cpp botWalk) took the speed before as a length and the way
    across the wish: a turn or a stop read as a wall every frame, and `frik_obstructed` with no danger *clears* a held
    AI_OBSTRUCTED, so the ledge obstruction `frik_obstacles` had just set was gone before `frik_dodge_obstruction`
    read it (the flags went 1/0/1/0 at the pit's edge). Now measured along the wish only, from the speed along it.
  - FrikBot's look ahead is one line 32 units ahead: a stair's or narrow ledge's side lets the box walk off, and dm4's
    route down beside the pit is a blind one (AI_BLIND: no obstacle checks at all). `frik_obstacles` now reads lava,
    slime or the sky below the drop ahead (past its 256-unit trace) as a danger on any route (a blind one given up).
  - and botWalk holds a bot at the edge (as walkmove holds a monster) when its walk, not a jump, takes it off its floor
    over lava or slime (its box traced down 1024), told to its AI as a wall.
  Now 3 in 120 s (one a straight drop after a death, one from a shot); mp_dm's own run: 0.
- **vr_dm_test 3's flake** (2 of 9 in B14c: "neither read nor landed", "parried 0, damage 20"): the other bot's shots at
  A (a shot knocks his crowbar out, or him off his place) and A's body moving a little as his pose changes. The test now
  holds every other bot's attacks off while it runs and the bot's spot follows A until he has stood still through the
  whole hold (restarts bounded by its give-up).
- **New**: a bot's walk prints its `pmtrace:` line too (vr_pmove_trace 1; bots walk from QuakeC's frame, not

- Checks (his game running: low-impact mode): the MP suite 35 of 37 (mp_dm 17/0, mp_lockstep_dm 20/0); mp_climb 10/1

## MP B11 part 4: bots punch and grab as players do (agent/mp, 2026-11-16)

- **A bot's off hand is a player's.** Its AI decides (`bot_offhand_ai`); the hand, its grip and its velocity go
  through the players' code. It punches an enemy within 60 units: its fist is thrust at 6 m/s and struck by the
  melee's sweep, a player's punch. It takes a dropped gun or a backpack within its reach: the open hand goes there,
  closes on it, and the hand's touch takes it. With "You Can Be Disarmed by Players" on, it closes its hand on a
  player's held weapon and pulls it away (the players' grab disarm).
- **What changed underneath:** bots' walks run the client premove (the hand touches). Their grips go through
  `VR_HandGrabUtil_UpdateState`. The melee takes hands that move themselves (`VR_HandLinesKept`). A bot's sword swing
  keeps its traced blow, and its sweep is off during the swing (one blow).

  Hand / Grabs Your Gun".

  - SP: Melee Only bots (`vr_pickup_test 15`) 13/0, scenario_check PASS (138/0), load_models 4/0, vr_run_check 9/0.

## installerfix: AD "ready (experimental)", the relight's speed (agent/installerfix, 2026-11-16)

- **AD label**: `ExpansionDetector.Campaign` has `Experimental` (AD's row; the engine's `qvr::ad::campaignIndex`): a
  found, intact AD is `Ready`, "ready (experimental)" (GUI expansion rows, the CLI and the detection report). A copy that
  isn't 1.80 patch 1 is the new `ExpansionState.OtherVersion` (a warning row): "another release (its pak2.pak isn't
  1.80 patch 1's): only 1.80 patch 1 is played" or "1.80 or older (no pak2.pak): ...". The self-test "readiness
  matches the engine" also checks the experimental row against `static_assert(qvr::ad::campaignIndex == N)` and the
  engine's "experimental" label, and both AD wrong-version labels. The engine's `vr_campaign_status` said "installed;
  native support in progress" for AD: now "ready (experimental)".
- **Relight**: the installer's relight is the game's own (`-preparerelight`: `vr_relight_batch everything`), already
  parallel (2 maps at once from 8 cores, the cores shared out) and already skipping maps relit with the same settings.
  Measured on 32 cores (light 2.0.0-alpha11, the default look: -extra4, bounce, dirt), six of id's maps: one at a time
  at 31 threads 28 s of light; six at once at 6 threads each 27 s (each map 2-4x slower); two at once ~23 s. light
  keeps the cores busy by itself, so more maps at once was not taken (memory: hundreds of MB a light). Changes: the
  batch lights the biggest maps first (after the map in play: LPT, so it never ends with one big map in one slot while
  the other idles), and the threads are rounded up (2 x 16, was 2 x 15). Where the time goes: "everything" includes
  the Library's and AD's maps; AD's are 1-2 minutes each (ad_mountain 104 s at 15 threads): with AD there, 111 maps
  took over 20 minutes here before the run was stopped. Not changed (his call): leaving the Library's/AD's maps out of
  the installer's relight.
- **Output**: light is not byte-deterministic even run to run at the same settings (the faces' lightmaps are packed
  in its threads' finishing order: 95% of e3m2.lit's bytes move between two sequential runs), so "byte-identical" was
  checked as the lightmaps' sorted byte values: sequential vs sequential and sequential vs parallel are identical (0
  of 401,100 differ).
- Checks: installer 0 warnings, self-tests 41/41; engine dev and ReleaseLTO built.

## Relighting about twice as fast: Quake VR's ericw-tools fork (branch agent/ericwfork, 2026-11-17)

His decision (2026-11-17, after the kit's `work\ericw\FINDINGS.md`): ship a fork of ericw-tools' `light`,
2.0.0-alpha11-qvr1. It is the shipped light, behind nothing.

- **The fork** (`Tools/ericw-tools/`: light.exe, the stock release's embree4.dll / tbb12.dll / tbbmalloc.dll, the
  licence texts, `patches/0001-0003`, README.md in Tools/fteqcc's style; source branch `qvr-fast` of
  https://github.com/vittorioromeo/ericw-tools, tag `2.0.0-alpha11-qvr1`, not yet pushed): deterministic lightmap
  packing (two runs byte-identical), `-bounceextra N` (bounce traced from N x N of -extra4's 4 x 4 samples per luxel,
  shared with the block), a version label patch (0003, `CMakeLists.txt`: the source zip builds the same label).
  Without `-bounceextra` it lights as stock: face-by-face 0 bytes different (e1m1, e3m5 with bounce 1.2), same light
  grid. With `-bounceextra 2`: mean |d| 0.25-0.31 per lightmap byte, 0.3-0.7% > 2, max 12-17; .lux and grid unchanged.
- **Game:** `vr_relight_bounceextra` (2, CVAR_NONE; 0 = stock) adds `-bounceextra N` to each light run when bounce > 0
  and the light.exe has the option's name in its bytes (`bounceExtraFor`, vr_relight.cpp; stock light: a console line,
  full cost). Not in the batch's lookKey: maps relit before stay "done". The in-game download (`vr_relight_tool.cpp`)
  pins the fork zip (13,277,988 bytes, sha256 afbd29bf...39d8e7) on the support release `assets-2026-11-17` (its only
  URL: ericwa's release does not have it); the NOTICE texts name the fork and its source. The page's button is
  "Download ericw-tools (13.3 MB)" (menu_paths.txt updated by hand: the row has no cvar, no board names it).
- **Scripts:** `relight_maps.py --bounceextra` (2) the same rule; `package-quakevr.ps1` and `make_release.ps1` take
  light from the repo's `Tools/ericw-tools` (QVR_ERICW_TOOLS still wins) and warn if it is not the fork;
  `support_assets.json` files may carry their own `tag` (ericw_source / ericw_win64 -> `assets-2026-11-17`; the HD pack
  stays on `assets-2026-10-08`); make_release.py/.ps1 build URLs and the online check per file's tag.
- **Release artefacts** (kit `work\ericw\release\`, SHA256SUMS.txt): `ericw-tools-2.0.0-alpha11-qvr1-win64.zip`
  (13,277,988, afbd29bf...), `ericw-tools-2.0.0-alpha11-qvr1-src.zip` (86,728,577, d56d651e...: the stock source zip,
  .git included, `git am` of the patches, `patches\`, README-qvr.md). The binary was built from that source tree.

## MP B19: the server-side move buffer; broken packets; the suite's flakes (agent/mp, 2026-11-17)

- **A lift meets your moves where your game predicted** (vr_netmove.cpp; `vr_net_movebuffer`, 2, Debug's network rows
  "Move Buffer"): a remote player's moves are kept as they come and run one a server tick in order (at most 2 left
  waiting; 0 off). Packets bunched on the way no longer run two moves in one tick, so a mover is no longer a step off
  where his replay met it: on e1m1's rising lift the lift's own predicted-place error went from ~2.1 units every run to
  0.05-0.14 (8 runs), the move contact error 0 throughout. Cost: about 10 ms average (28 ms at most) before the server
  runs a move; nothing felt by the player himself. The lockstep and the lag compensation are unchanged.
- **A broken server packet can no longer crash or strand the client** (SP-relevant: damaged demos too): a model
  number past the precache list (entity update, baseline, weapon stat) is a Host_Error, and a Host_Error inside a
  snapshot's records puts the network buffer back (it stayed pointed at the record: the next connect overflowed).
  Found by mp_fuzz.
- **Test flakes fixed:** mp_armed's rate-priority check (now on the server's own pose waits by weight,
  `vr_net_posewaits`: the entries a client read depend on how often each pose changed); mp_dm (B's list read before
  the second bot's name came); mp_disarm's toss (a real-time release's high lob slid
  to a wall: within 96 units, A put further back if the spot is in the wall); mp_lockstep_throw's "8 moves differ" (the
  hands' throw history held the joining frames' samples: a lockstep client clears it at its first move); mp_predictclimb
  (a climb's transition flag lost when two states came in one frame: kept until a replay takes it, vr_predict.cpp).
- Checks: MP suite 3 runs of 3 clean (52 each); mp_fuzz 14/0 in 5 runs alone; SP: scenario_check PASS (136/0),
  load_models 4/0, vr_run_check 12/0, autosavenow 4/0; dev and ThinLTO builds 0 warnings. MP_PLAN.md, "B19".
- **In VR:** nothing new to feel in single player; in multiplayer, riding lifts and doors as a remote player should
  show no small jolt when you land on a moving one.

  `vr_arena_test 6` prints it every 4 waves; the MP soak each minute (`mp_box3dmem`).
- **The prop hulls' cache** (`propHulls`, `vr_box3d_mesh.cpp`): keyed by model, frame and the thing's drawn box, so
  gibs, heads and dropped things of every size added hulls all map long (3940 over the arena's 32 waves, Box3D
  5.3 -> 10.5 MB; ~0.2 MB a minute on a 16-player server). `trimPropHulls` (`vr_box3d_props.cpp`, each sync) lets
  the non-actor hulls go once it holds more than 1024 (the actors' frame -1 hulls stay: `Slot::hull` keeps them; the
  others are read only as a body is made, the world copying the hull); `vr_physics_hull_stats` counts them. The
  arena soak now holds at ~5.7 MB.

  512 arrays for every count up to the longest a mesh contact ever had, kept until the world goes; quadratic). The
  longest measured: 6 in the arena, 8 on dm3 with 16 players: a guard (Box3D README).
