## MP B22: the dedicated server's heap; idle workers' pages; B21's two flakes (agent/mp, 2026-11-17)

- **Not a leak: idle job workers' empty heap pages** (single player too). mimalloc's pages belong to the thread that
  made them, and only that thread gives back the ones that frees on other threads emptied. A job worker that made
  blocks (a map load's hulls, nav tiles, a fight's jobs) and then went idle kept them all, committed: after e1m1's
  load, 285 empty pages (120-150 MB), every one a worker's; a 16-player dm3 server's committed heap grew 1237 -> 1432
  MB in 20 minutes in steps while its live blocks grew 19 MB.
- **The fix** (`vr_jobs.cpp`, `vr_crtheap_info.c`, Zancle's `ThreadPool::setIdleHook`, new): each worker tidies its
  own heap, a normal mi_collect after a job at most once a `vr_heap_thread_tidy` (new, 1000 ms; ~6 us) and a forced
  one once it has had no job that long (~0.5 ms, idle). Single player e1m1: committed 1382 -> 1095 MB, empty pages 0.
  The server: 1016 -> 1029 MB over 16 minutes (was 1237 -> 1432 over 20), its live blocks +16 MB, tapering (the hit
  model's and the ragdolls' skinned caches filling: bounded, `vr_heap_sites`).
- **Diagnostics** (Debug > Profiling and Memory: Heap: Live By Size, Heap: Worker Tidy): `vr_heap live [rows]` (the live
  blocks by block size; the pages held, made, empty and whose); `vr_heap_sites <min> [max]` ... `vr_heap_sites stop`
  (every thread's blocks of that size kept by call stack until freed: the sites still holding them).
- **The soak** (`mp_test.py soak`): the server's live heap by size each minute (soak_live.txt), `--heap-sites MIN:MAX`
  (soak_sites.txt), the bots added again after `--soak-change`'s change.
- **B21's flakes:** mp_rejoin's "C has the shotgun A let fall" took another weapon (anywhere on the map) for the dropped
  shotgun before the let-go reached the server: it now waits for the hand empty and the weapon by it; mp_held's carried
  hotspots (0.62 > 0.5) were compared before the shotgun settled into the off hand: it now waits for them to settle.
- **Checks:** the MP suite 3 runs, 3 clean; the 40-minute soak 23/0 (the server's heap 1020 -> 1044 MB by minute 30,
  was 1211 -> 1447; 1009 after the change).
- Shipping: the SP part is commit 120427f2c; on next's base `agent/b22-heaptidy` (6e5fc7980): scenario_check 136/0,
  load_models 4/0, vr_run_check 12/0, ThinLTO 0 warnings.
- **In VR:** nothing to see; the game's memory after a map load is ~300 MB lower (commit charge; the working set less).
## VR slide: the flat slide's body and eye height (branch agent/vrslide2, 2026-11-17)

His decision: "Sliding pose should be the same as flat screen, and the camera should smoothly but very quickly move to
the actual sliding head height even in VR. Perhaps add an option." Before, a headset's slide kept his view at his real
head and hung the flat pose from it (the hips at the flat slide's height off the box's floor, the legs bent up to the
play-space floor 3 units over it).

**The view** (`slide::viewDrop`, called from `vr_hands.cpp` placeTracked once the tracking is placed): while this
machine's player slides (`server.slide[1].on`, off a ledge mid-slide too), the whole tracked frame (head, eyes, hands,
trackers, so the body hung from them) is let down by an eased drop, and `headHeight` with it. As the slide starts it
takes his real eyes over the box's floor (over the client's origin: the server's moves a unit up into the crouched box
a frame before); the drop takes them to `slideEye()` (46 less `vr_flat_crouch_drop` and `vr_flat_slide_drop`: 22, the
flat slide's eyes), his head's own moves since one to one on top (an eye already under it: no drop). Eased by a
critically damped spring (`geom::easeCritical`, new in `vr_geom.hpp`: avatar's `easePitch` now calls it) that covers
95% in `vr_slide_camera_time` (0.15 s), no overshoot; back up the same way when the slide ends. The comfort vignette
counts the drop easing as a move (`viewDropMoving`, `vr_input.cpp` updateComfort). No lying down for 0.5 s after a
headset slide ends (`slide::headsetRising`, `vr_hull.cpp`): the slide's eyes are `vr_prone_eye`'s own 22 at the
defaults, and a nod coming back up would have laid him down.

**The body:** the same code as flat's (`vr_avatar_pitch.cpp`'s slide pitch from the eyes over the box, `solveLeg`'s
legs out in front), now from the flat slide's eyes; the neck back (`vr_flat_slide_neck_back`) too
(`flatmove::slideNeckBack` for `slide::headsetPose`). The body's floor goes where the flat slide's is, by the drop's
share (`viewDropShare`): Quake's standing eyes (46 over the box's floor) less the flat body's eye height
(`units::flatBodyEyeHeight`, `vr_flat_body_height`: 2.8 under the box's floor at the defaults), not
`vr_floor_offset`'s play-space floor. Not shared: the flat slide's legs turned to the slide's way and the chest back to
the view (`vr_flat_slide_legs`, flatplay's poseHands: a headset's body yaw is the tracked one), the arms (tracked), and
the legs' length (a headset's are fitted to the height he stands at: `legFit`).

**Settings:** `vr_slide_camera` 1 (Slide View; 0: the view stays at the real head and the body hangs from it, as
before), `vr_slide_camera_time` 0.15 (Slide View Time, 0.05..0.5 s), both CVAR_ARCHIVE, in VR Settings > Locomotion
after Slide Body Pose.

**Tests:** `bash Misc/quakevr/vrslide_test.sh <agent>`: `vr_slide_test` gains the view's checks and a case with
`vr_slide_camera 0`: straight down, the view from 55.6 (the mock's eyes) to 22.0, lowest 22.0 (no overshoot), 95% in
0.139 s, back up to 55.6 95% in 0.139 s after it (the let-go case too); with `vr_slide_camera 0` it stays at 55.6
(55.6 to 56.0). 24 passed. Then `vr_slide_pose_test` (new, `-flatscreenmode`) slides from the same spot and both print
the body 0.5 s into the slide (`printPose`: the body's floor, the head, the hips, knees and ankles off the head along
the view and over the box's floor), the headset's sized as the flat one (`vr_height_calibration 1.55`): floor -2.8 and
-2.8, head 22.0 and 22.1, hips (1.7, +-2.7, 3.7) and (1.6, +-2.7, 3.7), ankles at -0.4 both: worst 0.1 units off. The
knees and ankles reach further out in the headset (the mock stands taller than 1.55 m: its legs fitted to it).

## MP B23: NAT traversal: one server socket, room codes, the room service (agent/mp, 2026-11-17)

- **One server socket** (`net_dgrm.c` ReadShared, QVR_NET_VERSION 36): the server talks to every client from its
  listening port and tells them apart by address and port (each client's datagrams queued for it, at most 256; the
  rest for the connect/query handling, 64). NetQuake opened a port per client and named it in the accept: behind a
  router that doesn't keep port numbers, a forwarded host couldn't be joined. A v36 client keeps the address it
  reached. Windows: the listening socket ignores ICMP port-unreachable (`SIO_UDP_CONNRESET`, else one client gone cut
  everyone's reads short), 1 MB receive buffer. `net_stats`: "server queue drops".
- **Room codes**: a host (listen server of 2+ players or dedicated, `vr_mp_room` 1, new) registers every 20 s with the
  room service `vr_mp_rendezvous` (new, `vittorioromeo.com:26100`) from his game socket, gets a 6-letter code
  (console "Room code: ...", Host Game page "Room Code ABCDEF (C: copy)", `vr_mp_roomcode [copy]`). A joiner:
  Join Game > "Join by room code" or `connect @CODE`: the service introduces both, the host punches the joiner for 8 s
  while the joiner's connect requests (every 0.25 s, 32) punch the host's router. Messages: "No room with that code",
  "Room service not answering", "No direct link to the host" (symmetric NAT: forward UDP 26000), each with the whole
  reason on the console.
- **The service** `Misc/rendezvous/`: `qvr_rendezvous.py` (Python 3 stdlib, one UDP socket, protocol version 1:
  64-byte requests, 32-byte replies, no amplification; per-address token bucket 5/s burst 20; 20000 rooms, 8 per
  address, 50000 tracked addresses, 20 introductions per room in 10 s; rooms gone 120 s after the last registration;
  no addresses logged), `test_rendezvous.py` (20 checks: protocol, every limit, a real exchange on 127.0.0.1),
  `qvr-rendezvous.service` (hardened systemd unit), `deploy.sh <host> [user]` (scp + ssh/sudo; ufw), `README.md`
  (deploy, logs, update, local mode, the relay as a design note).
- **Tests**: `mp_test.py nat` (in the suite): the service's test; a forwarded host behind a non-port-preserving router
  joined at its outside port; a host behind a cone NAT gets a code (the service sees the outside port); A behind
  another cone NAT joins by it; B behind a symmetric NAT gets the reason; an unknown code and a dead service get
  theirs. Routers: `mp_nat.py` (cone / symmetric, port-preserving or not, forwards) on 127.0.0.2-5, the games sending
  through it by `-natgateway <port>` (net_wins.c, tests only). The harness's games run with `vr_mp_room 0` (never the
  internet service). mp_avatar now waits for the off hand's curls too (it raced a closing hand: 2 fails, then 2/2).
- **Checks**: dev 0 warnings; MP suite run 1: mp_armed's combat field-share (passed alone) and mp_avatar (fixed
  above); runs 2 and 3: both clean (46 scenarios, mp_nat 12/0). SP: scenario_check 136/0, load_models 4/0 (vr_run_check not run: no canonical script; nothing SP-side changed but the Join Game page). ThinLTO 0 warnings.
- **For him**: deploy (`bash Misc/rendezvous/deploy.sh vittorioromeo.com [user]`, UDP 26100 open in any cloud
  firewall); then host with two real routers and join by code. Note: the first smoke run of this session (mp_coop,
  before the harness got `vr_mp_room 0`) let its dedicated server look up vittorioromeo.com and send a few REGISTER
  datagrams to UDP 26100 there (nothing listens yet).
## SteamVR on Linux: the -51 explained, loader messages logged, the Flatpak's /dev/shm (branch agent/linuxsteamvr, 2026-11-17)

GitHub #82 (Fedora 45, Steam Frame, the Flatpak: "SteamVR: not running", then `xrCreateInstance failed: (-51)`). No
hardware here; diagnosis and plan in LINUX.md, "SteamVR" and "AppImage (plan, not built)". The reply draft:
`qvr-kit/scratch/issue82_reply.md` (not posted).

- Failure lines name the XrResult from the specification's list (`oxr::resultText`, `openxr_reflection.h`; the runtime's
  `xrResultToString` only for codes not in it): a failed `xrCreateInstance` has no instance, so it printed `failed:  (-51)`.
  Now `XR_ERROR_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE (-51)` (check, the frame calls' stall lines, the bindings' suggestion, the
  enumerate's failure in the log).
- Linux: the loader's stdout and stderr caught while it loads a runtime (`xrEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties`,
  `xrCreateInstance`: `xrruntime::captureLoaderOutput` / `endLoaderOutput`, dup2 onto a `tmpfile`) into
  `qvr_openxr.txt` as "OpenXR loader output (<call>): ..." lines; a failed `xrCreateInstance`'s error lines (deduplicated:
  with XR_LOADER_DEBUG the loader writes each to both) to the console, at most 8.
- `vr_xr_debug` (default 0, archived; Debug > Startup, "OpenXR Loader Log"): XR_LOADER_DEBUG=all before VR starts (on
  Linux before video init, read from the config early with the other vr_xr_* in gl_vidsdl.c); kept when set outside.
- `XR_ERROR_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` says what to try (`xrruntime::runtimeUnavailable`): SteamVR on Linux: start it first,
  in a sandbox without the host's /dev/shm the `flatpak override --user --device=shm` line, the logs, Monado/WiVRn;
  other runtimes: their service; Windows: start the runtime's app.
- SteamVR detection on Linux: `vrserver`, `vrcompositor`, `vrmonitor` matched by `comm`, the executable's name and
  argv[0]/argv[1]'s (`processNames`); in a Flatpak sandbox (`/.flatpak-info`) the report says "can't tell" (Auto: as
  not running); the report also lists the sandbox's devices, whether /dev/shm is the host's, and the /dev/shm entries
  that look like SteamVR's/OpenVR's/Steam's (to learn their names from players' logs).
- Flatpak manifest: `--device=shm` (`--device=all` alone gives a tmpfs /dev/shm of the sandbox's own: the likely -51).
- Checks: Windows dev and ReleaseLTO 0 warnings; the WSL Linux build 0 new warnings; WSL run (`scratch/ls_wsl_fail.sh`:
  a SteamVR manifest with a missing library, a fake `vrcompositor` started through ld.so): report "SteamVR:
  vrcompositor running", the loader's 4 error lines in the console and 14 lines in qvr_openxr.txt with vr_xr_debug,
  `XR_ERROR_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE (-51)`, the hint; xr_runtime_test.sh 103 PASS, 0 FAIL; scenario_check 136/136 PASS.
- Open: the failure outside the sandbox is unexplained until a player's log has the loader's lines and SteamVR's
  `vrclient_*.txt`; the Flatpak sandbox case not run (no flatpak here); the AppImage needs `appimagetool` in CI (a new
  pinned download): plan only.

## startuplog: the start-up trace and its heartbeat, PC and Quest (branch agent/startuplog, 2026-11-17)

His Quest 3 report: after an install and a new data push, minutes of Meta's three dots; logcat's last game line
"Using protocol 999", then only VrApi lines. Now every start says where it is, on the PC and the Quest alike.

- `vr/vr_startlog.cpp` (one path for both): each step of the start-up and of the first map's load logged as it begins
  and ends, with the wall clock since the process started (`[startup +1.234s] video (...) begin` / `... end (took
  577.0 ms)`, nested steps indented); a stage that only ends (a `VR_TimeMark` with no step of its name open) as
  `<stage> done (X ms since "<previous>")`; notes: each pak read (its files, its ms), progs.dat's size and CRC; `first
  frame shown (the start-up took X ms)` and a summary line: the six slowest steps and the four costliest kinds of work
  (vr_startup_times' `VR_TimeAdd` sums: shader compiles, model loads, normal maps; on the Quest the program cache's
  "programs from their binaries" / "program binaries refused" sums). Lines go through `Con_SafePrintf` (no screen update
  per line while loading; before the console, `Sys_Printf`): the terminal, the run's log, and on Android logcat under
  `QuakeVR`, a line at a time (the quest branch's `Sys_Printf` -> `VR_AndroidLog`). Also `<game folder>/startup.log`
  (quakevr/startup.log), made anew at each start right after the file system starts (the lines before it kept and
  written then), each line flushed; on the Quest in the app's files folder (`vr_android_export startup.log`).
- The heartbeat: a watchdog thread (detached; stops at the trace's end) reads a seqlock snapshot of what the main thread
  is in (no lock the main thread waits on) and, while one step runs past 2 s, says every 2 s `[startup +Xs] still in
  <step> (<progress>; GL step N: <last breadcrumb>) (Y s so far)`. Progress: `model 12 of 40: progs/ogre.mdl`, `sound
  ...`, `pak <path>`, a load's `N frames so far, waiting for the signon: k of 4`; the last `VR_GLStep` breadcrumb
  (every shader compile and link, the OpenXR calls, the quest branch's "program X from its binary") with its count.
- Steps: Host_Init's stages (begin calls beside the existing `VR_TimeMark`s, which end them), the first frame's
  configs/autoexec, the VR backend's start and OpenXR's instance, system, session, spaces, actions and swapchains,
  the map load (from `VR_TimeLoadBegin` to its first frame drawn, or "failed"), the server's progs, world model,
  entities, 2 frames, the client's model and sound precaches (per-item progress), R_NewMap (its mark renamed "client:
  R_NewMap") and each `VR_NewMap` prewarm step. A step left open at a frame's end (a Host_Error's longjmp) is closed
  there, said so. The trace runs to the first frame drawn and, when no map loaded in the start-up, on to the first
  map's first frame (a second summary), then stops.
- `vr_startup_log` (archived, default 1): 0 quiet (no console or logcat lines; the file is still written). Read once
  the config ran (the lines before it always print). Debug > Startup: the toggle and "Startup Trace Summary"
  (`vr_startup_trace`: the file and the last summary). Test aid: `vr_startup_trace stall <s>` (the main thread sleeps
  inside a step), `vr_startup_trace check` (verdict `startuplog: N passed, M failed`: file made, start-up summed up, no
  step left open, 2+ heartbeat lines after a 5 s stall). Run: `run.sh <tree> -Script "vr_startup_trace stall 5;wait;
  vr_startup_trace check;toggleconsole;quit" -QuitOn "startuplog: \d+ passed"` (the stall is real time by nature).
- What runs after "Using protocol 999" (CL_ParseServerInfo), by reading the code: the precache lists, then each model's
  `Mod_ForName` (the alias models' skins, their normal maps from the derived-data cache or made, the GL uploads), the
  sounds, `R_NewMap` (lightmaps, brush buffers, then `VR_NewMap`'s prewarm steps: view models, gun anchors, rigs...),
  then the frames to the signon (`VR_SignonPrewarm`: translucent decal programs). Nothing prints there without
  developer 1, so logcat stops at that line. While the main thread is inside one of these no `xrEndFrame` runs; the
  frames to the signon draw no world and submit no layer: both show Meta's dots. Suspects on the Quest: (1) the program
  cache: its key hashes the exact shader text (and the pack is per driver identity), so a build whose shaders changed
  (the 1.1.0 merge) misses every program: the comment in vr_diskcache.cpp measures ~51 s for the start's ~120 programs
  on the Adreno, and the map's own (VR programs, decal and multiview variants) follow at the load; (2) the derived-data
  cache rebuilt after new data (the PC's e1m1: 1384 skins' normal maps, 1.5 s on 16 threads; many times that on the
  XR2); (3) the external files folder read through FUSE. The trace tells them apart: `still in client: R_NewMap` /
  `VR_NewMap: <step>` with `GL step N: compile/link <program>` climbing = compiles; `still in client: models precached
  (model k of n ...)` = model and skin work; `still in map load (...) (N frames so far, waiting for the signon: k of
  4)` = frames running but the signon stuck (a protocol or server-side problem, not loading); a step whose "so far"
  grows with neither progress nor GL steps moving = a blocking call (a file read, a lock).
- Headless PC run (e1m1 from the script, mock headset): 130 lines; the start-up 5.3 s with the map; slowest: the
  first frame's configs 4.1 s (the map's load inside it), the map load 1.7 s, the server's entities 1.08 s, video
  0.51 s; work: GL_CreateShaders 297 ms; the map's: skins' normal maps from the cache 1522 ms (1384), alias models
  1005 ms (307). Seen in passing: the file system reads the same paks several times during its start (each under
  0.3 ms here; on the Quest's FUSE worth a look), and the first frame's configs take ~2 s before any map command.
- Not done (follow-up): a "Loading: <step>" quad in the headset. The long steps block the main thread (no frame loop
  at all), so it needs either the loops above to pump an OpenXR frame with the quest backend's panel quad between
  items (models, programs) or a second thread with its own GL context submitting frames; neither is cheap. The
  quest branch's program cache can name a miss's reason (a new driver identity vs a changed text) with a `VR_StepNote`
  in `VR_ProgCacheBegin` once it merges this.
- Checks: dev and ReleaseLTO 0 warnings; no local NDK (ANDROID_NDK_HOME unset): the Android build not run (the code is
  portable C++, no `__ANDROID__` paths of its own); `vr_startup_trace check` 4 passed, 0 failed (3 heartbeat lines);
  scenario_check 136/136 PASS; load_models_test 4 passed, 0 failed.

## questshaders: the game boots with a progress panel while the shaders compile (branch agent/quest, 2026-11-18)

- Why so long: ~145 programs a set, 15.8 MB of GLSL (über-shaders, ~109 KB each); Adreno ~0.35-0.5 s a program; the
  program cache makes later starts fast (QUEST_PLAN.md 6zi).
- Under the ES profile (the Quest, `-glescompat`) the set is queued (`GL_CreateShadersAsync`) and made frame by frame
  (`GL_ShadersPump`: 8 ms of submits, the driver's parallel compile polled with `GL_COMPLETION_STATUS_KHR`, never
  waited for; one at a time without it). Meanwhile each frame shows the loading panel (`vr/vr_shaderload.cpp`: "Compiling
  shaders: N / M", a bar; CPU-drawn, the OpenXR quad layer and the window) and nothing else runs; no time passes.
  The settings' remakes go the same way. `-shadersasync 0|1` / `QVR_SHADERS_ASYNC`; `-noparallelshaders`;
  `-shaderloadshot <tga>`; `-shadersasynctest` (verdict `shaders_async_test`). Program cache flushed every 10 s.
- PC (`-glescompat -fakeandroid`): 145 programs in 0.65 s over 37 frames (longest frame's work 12.7 ms); cache cold
  6-9 s, warm 0.6 s; one at a time 0.65 s; 4/0 each. The PC's own GLSL unchanged (one call). gles_render_test's PC run
  now queues its shaders too (`QVR_SHADERS_ASYNC=1`: the same start, the scrap's pics in the same order).
- Debug > Startup > Recompile Shaders (Loading Panel) (`vr_shader_reload_queued`). Package `<kit>/scratch/quest_apk4/`.

## Armed grunts' cost on crowded maps (aglod, 2026-11-20)

d2m8 (251 armed grunts, 156 live at his start) cost 536 k QC instructions a frame idle. Measured by state with a new
builtin, `thinkcost(e, reset)` (each edict's think statements, counted in `SV_RunThink` as `profile` counts them:
`qcvm->instr_total`, both interpreters), and `vr_agrunt_test 226` (the map as it stands) / `227` (every grunt woken at
him) in `QC/vr_armedgrunt_lod_test.qc`: per grunt a frame, idle unseen 2,463, idle seen 3,526, alert 3,673, fighting
3,507, dead 12 (table: DWELL.md 9.7). What changed, all in the shared armed-grunt code (no Dwell or map branch):
- **Unseen means not sent too**: `unseenfar(e, near, optional e2)` also counts a grunt out of each player's fat PVS
  (as `SV_WriteEntitiesToClient` sends by it, the gates' destinations included; made once a frame per player,
  `UnseenScratch`) as unseen; its held weapon must be out of it too.
- **The pose LOD deeper** (`VR_AGP_Lod`): an unseen idle grunt is posed once every `vr_agrunt_pose_lod_frames`
  (new tunable, 8; 2 is the old every other frame) server frames, its weapons carried along between; an alert one
  or a chainsaw's stays at 2 (its readiness eases up in its pose; the saw's engine sound is in it); posed at once
  when it gets a new enemy (`.vr_agp_lod_en`) or is seen. The pose after skipped frames runs with `frametime` the
  time since its last (its eases and a chainsaw's fuel move on by all of them: for a steady target the same result
  as posing each frame). The fists' poser (`VR_AGP_PoserThink`) has the same LOD.
- **Exact skips**: the guard's raise read (`VR_AGG_Frame`) skips both hands past `VR_AGG_ReadReach` (windup range
  times the widest category's), clearing them as the loop would; the parry's frame (`VR_AGPar_Frame`) returns at
  once with no player within 160 units, no monster melee begun in 1.5 s, guard down and no parry up or seen; the
  shot and throw scans (`VR_AGS_Projectiles`, `VR_AG_WeaponStruck`) use `findradiusmoving(org, rad, minspeed)`
  (findradius's chain without what stands still, players, monsters and pushers: the same entities their filters
  kept, in the same order) and a look round the grip first (`VR_AG_LINE_REACH` 192), so a quiet frame works out no
  weapon line.
Result: d2m8 idle 274 k a frame (`profile`, 720 frames after 120); woken thinks 602 k to 464 k; e1m1 38 k. Under
150 k needs cutting what can be seen: the 20 grunts in view at his start (57 k), the other thinks (55 k, the pickups'
forcegrabbable thinks 39 k of it) and non-think QC (29 k) are 141 k alone. Test `Misc/quakevr/aglod_test.sh`
(`vr_agrunt_test 228`, vrarena): a shotgun grunt 400 units behind him (posed 8 times in 64 frames), brought into view
or shot: posed that frame, alert, the shot one attacking within 4 s; its 3 s trace the same with 8 frames, 2 and no
LOD (seen) or 8 and 2 (shot): 6 passed, 0 failed. Not run here: the armed-grunt suites, vr_ad_test, dwell_maps.sh,
dwell_monsters_test.sh, scenario_check, the ThinLTO build (budget). ad_tears is not in the agent's base.

### Armed-grunt LOD review (aglod2, 2026-11-20, agent/aglod)

- **Worn pack LOD** (`vr_wornpack.qc`): `unseenfar(g, near, pk)`: a wearer in view but out of his PVS whose pack is

## ragperf: frame drops near active ragdolls in melee (2026-11-20, agent/ragperf; measured, no fix yet)

Tester report (BACKLOG.md 11): melee range against active ragdolls drops the frame rate on a lower-end PC. Scene:
`Misc/quakevr/ragdoll/ragperf_scene.py <n> <close|far> <fists|axe> <label>` (vrfiringrange, seed 7, god + notarget;
`n` grunts in a fan 40 units ahead or 300 out; `vr_ragdoll_act stagger <edict>` on each every 120 frames (`RP_ACT`,
`RP_PERIOD`); the mock hands jabbing high and low across the fan, or the axe chopping; `RP_FLAT=1` flat punches; a
720-frame window: `vr_profile`, `profile` (QC), `vr_hitmodel_stats`, and `vr_physics_frametime` with its new counts
line: awake bodies, contacts stepped, islands, hand contacts). Timings came from shared runs (other workers testing):
one run each, noisy by tens of percent, never used for a claim; the counts are deterministic.

| case | driven a frame | contacts stepped | hand contacts | QC instr a frame | model tests a frame | Box3D step ms (noisy) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 close, fists | 1.8 | 220 | 0 | 36.7 k | 5.1 | 0.28 |
| 4 close, fists | 2.7 | 465 | 0 | 52.5 k | 17.4 | 0.41 |
| 6 close, fists | 3.9 | 668 | 0 | 66.8 k | 29.2 | 0.59 |
| 6 far, fists | 1.0 | 89 | 0 | 49.3 k | 2.0 | 0.14 |
| 6 close, axe | 4.1 | 768 | 0 | 64.4 k | 51.0 | 0.66 |
| 6 close, flat punches | 4.2 | 639 | 0 | 50.7 k | 53.7 | 0.53 |

- **Not the cost**: the active-ragdoll drive itself (`vr_ragdoll_active_list`: 0.03-0.05 ms a frame for 2-6 driven);
  hit-model tests (0.6-0.9 us each, at most ~54 a frame: under 0.05 ms); the hands' and the blade's Box3D bodies: 0
  touching contacts with the ragdolls in every case (the shoves and knockdowns throw them out of reach: `vr_ragdoll_act
  getup` sent a grunt from 40 to 190 units away).
- **Grows with the bodies close**: Box3D's contacts stepped, about 110 more for each driven ragdoll (its parts against
  the range's brushes and each other: not yet split); and QC, about 7-8 k instructions a frame for each grunt near the
  swinging hands: the armed grunts' strike sweeps (`VR_AG_StrikeMeets`: up to 17 steps of two `VR_AGS_HullGap` a grunt
  a hand a frame while a hand swings fast; `VR_AG_StrikeGap` 0.63 M to 2.65 M instructions over 720 frames from 2 to 4
  grunts), plus `VR_Melee_Sweep`. Far, the acts mostly did not take (1 driven), so close/far is not like for like.
- **Left**: (1) a scene where the hands stay in the bodies (the player following them, or acts that do not throw
  them) to see the hand-contact cost the tester meant; (2) split the ~110 contacts a driven ragdoll (self pairs, brush
  shapes, `vr_ragdoll_collide_each`); (3) cut `VR_AG_StrikeMeets` cheaply (a broad gap test on the grunt's box before
  the sweep, the same verdicts) and compare the `vr_agrunt` tests before and after; (4) the GPU side close up (not
  measurable headless). No behaviour changed; the only code change is the counts line (`vr_physics_frametime`,

## ragperf2: the active-ragdoll melee drops, continued (2026-11-20, agent/ragperf; one fix)

Counts, not timings (other workers ran tests alongside). The scene (`ragperf_scene.py`, above) gained:

- **`RP_INSIDE=1`, the hands kept in the bodies** (the tester's case): `vr_mock_hand_follow <main|off> <part|cycle|off>`
  (new, the mock backend: every frame the hand put at that part of the ragdoll nearest the player; `cycle` its parts in
  turn, 8 frames each) with `vr_mock_hand_to_absolute 1`, and `vr_mock_walk_to monster 28` every 24 frames (the hands'
  bodies push the ragdolls off, out of arm's reach, so the player walks after them). Not quite deterministic: the mock
  walk's "stuck" test and the strike speeds read the real clock (same runs: 4 grunts gave the same contacts, 2 and 6
  did not); the base scene (hands swinging across the fan) is.
- **`vr_physics_frametime` split lines**: the awake ragdolls' parts' contacts by what the other shape is (self with a
  joint between, self without, another ragdoll, the world, the hands' bodies, other), touching or only near (their
  fattened bounds overlap: the narrow phase runs on it, the solver never sees it). `b3Body_GetAllContactData`: a marked
  Box3D local change (README.md), b3Body_GetContactData's every contact.

Contacts a frame (after; touching / near):

| case | contacts stepped | self apart | world | hands | QC instr a frame old -> new | strike sweeps' share old -> new |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 close, swinging | 220 | 1 / 144 | 6 / 50 | 0 / 0 | 37.0 k -> 35.8 k | 1.95 k -> 0.64 k |
| 4 close, swinging | 465 | 8 / 331 | 17 / 88 | 0 / 0 | 53.0 k -> 47.9 k | 8.14 k -> 3.13 k |
| 6 close, swinging | 668 | 10 / 436 | 24 / 123 | 0 / 0 | 67.5 k -> 59.6 k | 12.83 k -> 4.96 k |
| 4 close, hands inside | 807 | 42 / 386 | 37 / 89 | 1.8 / 6.1 | 40.7 k -> 39.6 k | 2.03 k -> 0.71 k |
| 6 close, hands inside | 868 | 44 / 530 | 40 / 126 | 3.4 / 8.7 | 54.0 k -> 51.3 k | 5.83 k -> 2.44 k |
| 6 close, axe inside | 1066 | 37 / 510 | 35 / 139 | 3.4 / 10.0 | 63.9 k -> 57.3 k | 9.45 k -> 3.44 k |

(old: `vr_agrunt_strike_broad 0`, the same build; the swinging cases' physics identical old and new: the same contacts to
the decimal. Strike share: `VR_AG_StrikeGap`, `_StrikeMeets`, `VR_AGS_HullGap` and the new `_StrikeBroad`, `_BoxAdd`.)

- **Hands in bodies are cheap**: even pushed into a ragdoll every frame, the hands' and the blade's bodies have 2-3
  touching contacts and 6-10 near a frame (their bodies shove the parts out; `reachSkips` lets a shoved body through).
- **The contacts are self pairs that never touch**: a driven ragdoll's parts against each other, ~110 a ragdoll, of
  which ~7% touch; the rest are pairs whose fattened bounds overlap (a body's parts are close; Box3D's per-shape margin
  is 12.5% of its size, to 5 cm). Joined pairs: none but the upper arm and chest (collideConnected on purpose; preSolve
  exempts the socket). **Not filtered**: Box3D asks the custom filter once, when a pair begins, and keeps it while the
  bounds overlap, so a pair refused while apart would miss a later touch inside the same bounds: no filter keeps the
  solver's constraints the same. Their cost is the narrow phase: the whole collide phase was 0.11 ms of a 0.32 ms step
  with ~840 contacts (noisy, shared runs).
- **Fix: `VR_AG_StrikeMeets`' broad test** (vr_armedgrunt_parry.qc `VR_AG_StrikeBroad`): before the sweep (up to 17
  steps, two hull queries each, plus the muzzle line), one box round every point the sweep and the muzzle line test
  (the swept lines' ends, the hand, the muzzle, a carried prop's middle), tested against both volumes by
  `disarmhull(.., 30 / 31 / 32, lo, hi, grow)` (vr_disarmhull.cpp `boxGap`: the box's 8 corners against the hull, no
  more than any path in it). Clear of both by more than the strike's reach (and a carried prop's size, plus 0.01 for
  rounding): every test would miss, so -1 at once. A volume without a hull (the old lines) is swept as before.
  `vr_agrunt_strike_broad` (Debug menu, Armed Grunts: Strike Broad Test; 1 on; 0 always swept; 2 both, each
  disagreement printed (developer 1) and a count every 256 sweeps). Check mode over the scene: 2/4/6 swinging, 6 axe,
  6 inside: 0 disagreements (inside 6: about 95% skipped; swinging: every sweep skipped, none met). `vr_agrunt_test`
  94 (strikes), 60, 77, 33, 96, 35 pass. Test 35 (parry) failed one case in two of four runs in check mode only (a
  different weapon each time; its strike speeds are real time and check mode does both tests under load); on and off
  it passed every run. Suites: flatmelee 12/12, scenario_check pass, ragdoll_climb 6/6 (off), active-ragdoll test no
  failures, ragdoll_stagger 3 FAIL (monster 0: the known ones, BACKLOG.md "ragdoll_stagger: what is left"), melee eval
  162/171 with no pass turned fail (the archived takes' decap zone figures differ from the baseline); ThinLTO 0
  warnings.
- **Left**: the remaining QC is the melee sweep (`VR_Melee_Sweep`, `VR_Melee_Track`), the force-grabbable thinks and
  the armed grunts' prop thinks, not close-range specific; the GPU side close up (not measurable headless).
## The tester's last two comfort options: double-tap to run, Ammo Pouch sliders (comfort, 2026-11-20, `agent/comfort`)

From tester Joyeuse's list (2026-11-18). BACKLOG section 7's entry is gone now: the sprint toggle and Mantle When had
already shipped, and these two close it.

- **Run by double-tapping the moving stick** (`vr_move_doubletap`, 0; `vr_move_doubletap_window`, 0.3 s;
  vr_input.cpp `doubleTapStep`). Its input is the moving stick as the walk reads it (`moveAxes`: the radial deadzone,
  0..1). A push is half the travel or more. Let go means under a quarter (moveHold's `moveHoldLeast`). Steps: Idle, then
  First (a push), then Gap (let go within the window), then Running (a push within 45 degrees, within the window again),
  then Idle once the stick is let go. A slow first push, a long gap or a push another way does not run; that push can
  start a double tap of its own. It also ends where the sprint toggle ends: at death, the intermission, a new map
  (`input::resetSprintToggle`), a menu opening, or the setting going off. **How they combine:** in `VR_AdjustMove`,
  running = (the speed button, held or toggled, against cl_alwaysrun) OR a double tap's run. The double tap never makes
  you walk, and the toggle's switch is left alone. Its clock is the frame times summed, so it is the same at any frame
  rate. VR stick only: the keyboard and the gamepad (`IN_JoyMove`) do not go through the stick path. Menu: "Double-Tap
  Stick to Run" under Speed Button (VR Settings > Locomotion and Controls; Advanced > Movement > Locomotion, plus the
  window there).
- **Ammo Pouch Forward / Right / Up** on VR Settings > Holster Calibration (`vr_menu_holster_pouch_x/y/z`). These are
  wrappers like the holsters' rows (`holsterWrappers`, vr_menu.cpp): units away from the shipped `vr_ammo_pouch_x/y/z`
  (standing), -10..10, extended to +-40. They are shown from the settings each time the page is built, so Holster
  Setup's drag, which sets the same settings, and the rows agree. The pouch's marker shows while one of the rows is
  chosen. Reset Holsters resets the pouch too. The crouched and seated pouch rows stay on their own pages. There is no
  flat menu with holster sliders.
- **Verified**: `vr_doubletap_test` 10/0, `doubletap_test.sh` 5/0 (mock stick in e1m1: a long push walks at 200, the
  taps run at 320, letting go ends it, off walks). `pouch_slider_test.sh` (`menu_vr pouchtest`) 6/0: each row moves its
  setting and the reach point that way, Up 1.5 times its units through the body fit. The pouch moved elsewhere shows on
  its row, and Reset Holsters works. scenario_check 137/0; flatplay 31/0; `vr_menu_path_check maps/vrcalibration.map` 0
  missing; menu_paths.txt regenerated (it also picked up other workers' rows that were missing); dev and ThinLTO builds,
  0 warnings.

## Discord Rich Presence (branch agent/discord, 2026-11-20)

His request (2026-11-18): Discord shows what he plays. **DISCORD.md** is the reference (what is shared, setting up the
application, the protocol, the join hook).

- **Route**: Discord's RPC over its local IPC (`\\.\pipe\discord-ipc-0..9`; on Linux/macOS the `discord-ipc-N` unix
  socket), HANDSHAKE then SET_ACTIVITY frames written by hand: no SDK, no library, no download. `Quake/vr/vr_discord.cpp`.
- **Shared**: details = the map's title (worldspawn message, else the file name; "In the menus"); state = campaign ·
  mode (Single player, Co-op, Deathmatch, Survival Arena wave N, Watching a demo) · VR or Flat screen; elapsed since
  the map began; a large image only with `vr_discord_image`.
- **Threads**: the main thread reads a small key a frame (no allocation) in `VR_HostFrameEnd` and hands the activity's

## box3dup: Box3D updated to upstream 1767150d; the ragdolls' self contacts measured (2026-11-20, `agent/box3dup`)

**Update** (`Quake/vr/external/box3d`, README.md lists every local change now). efca0c18 (2026-10-19) to upstream
main 1767150d (2026-11-17): 8 commits. What matters to us:

- #212 "Reduce ghosts": full ghost-collision handling for sphere, capsule and hull against a mesh or height field
  built with `identifyEdges` (ours is), the mesh builder faster, `B3_MAX_MESH_CONTACT_TRIANGLES` gone. b3CollideMesh
  Triangles was split out of b3ComputeMeshManifolds: our pre-solve-per-point change moved into it (it now gets the
  world and shape B's transform; NULL world from the public collide functions).
- #227: a contact keeps at most 8 manifolds (`B3_MAX_MANIFOLDS`, cheap culling); our long-manifold-array change kept.
- #228 pull-model task API: the push model stays; the enqueue callback gets a `b3TaskType` instead of a name
  (`enqueueStepTask`). Also #214/#216 static queries (a data race fix), #202 the mover and pogo joints (new files),
  #201 CMake. No new world or def defaults to set; the contact, joint and island solvers are unchanged but for
  accessors.
- Re-applied by 3-way merge (`git merge-file`; the README's recipe now says so). Local changes the README had not
  listed, now listed: the pre-solve callback's `separation`, the elliptical cones (`coneAngleY`), the Tracy pool.

**The ghost handling and the climbing ragdolls.** climb_test `pull`, seeds 7-10 (N=4, 24 cases): old
Box3D 21/24 (ogre 2/4, hknight 3/4); new 17/24 (ogre 0/4, knight 2/4, hknight 3/4); new with the ghost handling off
22/24 (ogre 4/4, hknight 2/4). But off, the active-ragdoll test's crawling ogre failed "energy 76 J after the drive"
(it passes with the ghost handling on, and before the update): off is not the old code either (efca0c18 had a
vertex/edge-index heuristic against ghosts that #212 replaced), so bodies lying and sliding on the world's triangle
seams catch more. A new marked local change, `b3World_EnableMeshGhostHandling` (a world flag read by
b3ComputeMeshManifolds; upstream's default on), set before each step from **`vr_box3d_mesh_ghosts`** (default 1:
upstream's handling; Debug > Profiling "Physics Mesh Ghost Handling"), so either can be tried in VR. At 1 the climb
gives the same as without the change (the ogre drops at 1.18 s, 19 units over the lip, both). **Open**: why the lip
contacts lose the ogre's hands with #212 (its hull or hands against the lip's edge, `vr_ragactive_hold.cpp` climbFrame
"lost its hold"); worth a look upstream-side or in our hold before choosing a default for good.

**Tests** (new build, upstream's ghost handling, the shipped default): vr_physics_mtbench 200/300 `eece2c3897006b67`, 400/300
`b071f169ad1d96cb`, the same as before the update for every worker count, SSE2 and AVX2 (convex and joint solving
unchanged). throw_spin PASS, held_over_props PASS, throw_grace (changes by grace end 0.00-0.34, as before),
gib_2h_throw 9 of 28 bursts (as before), magthrow 3/0, prop_2h (stale as before), ragdoll_test 13 runs exit 0,
active-ragdoll test no failures, ragdoll_stagger 1 FAIL (monster 0's backpedal: BACKLOG's known one), climb 23/24 at
seed 7 (pull ogre FAIL, above), selfcollide runs, flatmelee 12/0, scenario_check PASS, vr_agrunt_test 1 17/0,
2 4/0, 60 6/0, 77 12/0, 33 6/0, 35 6/0, 94 14/1 and 96 0/8 (timed out, "tuned 0") the same with the old build (my
runner's set-up: vrtesthall, seed 7). Debug and Dev 0 warnings; ThinLTO built (exe relinked 18:50), 0 warnings.

**Self contacts** (ragperf_scene.py 2/4/6 close, fists, the ThinLTO exe via the new `RP_RUNARGS=--lto`; self pairs
on and off alternated, two rounds, while another worker's MP suites ran: timings A/B in the same window; counts exact).
`vr_ragdoll_self_pairs` (new, Debug > Profiling "Ragdolls' Self Contacts"; 1 default; 0, a measurement aid, refuses a
ragdoll's own pairs in shouldCollide's selfMeets: the physics changes) gave, a frame over 720 frames:

| ragdolls | contacts stepped on / off | self apart touching / near | Box3D step ms on -> off (2 rounds) | collide ms on -> off |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 284.5 / 79.6 | 3.1 / 201.9 | 0.177 -> 0.138, 0.194 -> 0.136 | 0.075 -> 0.039, 0.082 -> 0.037 |
| 4 | 460.9 / 165.5 | 6.9 / 299.9 | 0.251 -> 0.189, 0.320 -> 0.202 | 0.111 -> 0.052, 0.141 -> 0.056 |
| 6 | 654.0 / 178.3 | 10.1 / 470.4 | 0.366 -> 0.271, 0.457 -> 0.285 | 0.157 -> 0.065, 0.197 -> 0.070 |

The never-touching self pairs are ~72% of the contacts stepped and cost the collide phase only (solve the same on and
off): ~0.04 ms a frame with 2 driven ragdolls, ~0.1-0.13 ms with 6, on this machine (a lower-end CPU perhaps two or three times that). Pairs and the solver do not change. **Not implemented**: an exact skip (physics the
same to the bit) needs a marked Box3D change in the collide task: keep each self pair's last distance and its bodies'
transforms then, and skip its narrow phase while that distance less a conservative motion bound (the bodies' moves
and turns times their extents since) stays above the speculative distance; touching flags and events stay as they
are, but the skipped GJK/SAT caches differ, so a hash proof may still show last-bit differences on the pairs that do
touch later. At most ~0.1 ms a frame with 6 close ragdolls: left (BACKLOG).

## box3dup2: the ogre's ledge climb under upstream Box3D's ghost handling (2026-11-20, `agent/box3dup`)

**Cause: not the contacts.** climb_test pull's ogre (seeds 7-10) dropped "lost its hold" with #212's ghost handling on
(0/4) and pulled itself up with it off (4/4). Traced (`vr_ragdoll_active_trace 6`), its pose was the same both ways at
its pull's start: straddling the lip, its left leg on the top, its pelvis 10 units out from the edge and 4 under the
top. The Hang phase's "not hanging" (it lets go: meant for a monster that caught the lip with its legs still on the
top) measured the pelvis from `Climb::lip`, the mean of the holds' points, and a ledge hold takes the lip where the hand
was, up to half an arm in or out from the edge (the ogre's left hand 17 units in, its right 17 out). Off, only the left
hand held by then: the pelvis read 27 units out, "hanging", it pulled. On, the right hand's hold came 0.2 s sooner: the
mean was the edge, 10 units, "not hanging", it let go and fell. Which hand held first decided it (the old Box3D's 2/4
were the same coin; the earlier note here that an ogre "swung 27-30 units out" was this misreading too).

**Fix** (`vr_ragactive_hold.cpp`, climbFrame Hang; `Climb::edge`, set where the climb begins from the hands' reach
goals, which are on the edge): "not hanging" is judged from the ledge's edge, and needs both whole legs on the top (a
foot in from the edge and within 0.15 arm under the top), as its comment always said. A straddling monster pulls
itself up. `lip` (the pull's way) is unchanged.

**Numbers** (ghost handling on, `vr_box3d_mesh_ghosts 1`, the default kept): climb_test pull seeds 7-10 21/24 (was
17/24): grunt 4/4, ogre 4/4 (was 0/4), enforcer 4/4, zombie 4/4, hell knight 3/4 (seed 8 "slid back off the lip", as
before), knight 2/4 (seeds 9, 10 "lost its hold": a hand "pulled away" 11-15 units off its hold at the grab, both
modes now and then; run singly, seeds 9 and 7 swap: chaotic; BACKLOG). Active-ragdoll test no failures (the crawling
ogre's late ke 1.0 J). ragdoll_stagger 1 FAIL (monster 0's backpedal, the known one); flatmelee 12/0; scenario_check
PASS; throw_spin PASS, held_over_props PASS, throw_grace and throw_trigger run clean, gib_2h_throw 11 of 28 bursts,
magthrow 3/0; gibprops e1m1 alive (grunt, ogre, zombie, knight, hell knight, enforcer): all 1 but the enforcer's head
still in the air at 150 frames (as ROUND22 notes). vr_physics_mtbench 200/300 `eece2c3897006b67`, 400/300
`b071f169ad1d96cb` for every worker count, AVX2 and SSE2 (unchanged). Dev and ThinLTO 0 warnings, the LTO exe
relinked after the change.

## navfollow: a debug autopilot after another player by the navmesh (navfollow, 2026-11-20, `agent/navfollow`)

His words: "a debug command I can enable in one of the players' windows so that it follows the other player using the
navmesh", and "do bots use the navmesh? If not, should they?" (NAVMESH.md 22 and 23).

- **`vr_nav_follow <name | slot | next | 0>`** (Debug > Network: Follow the Next Player): the server plans the player's
  path to the other on its navmesh (`nav::followPath`: a player's 16 x 56 class; doors and lifts walked, the monsters'
  drop, lift and teleporter links) every `vr_nav_follow_repath` (0.25) s and sends him its corners when they change
  (`QVR_SVC_NAVFOLLOW`, reliable); his client turns the view to the next corner and presses forward in `VR_AdjustMove`,
  hops through `VR_MoveJump` when stuck, stops `vr_nav_follow_stop` (64) units short along the path. A listen host and
  a remote client alike; the moves are a human's (prediction, the server's moves, lag compensation unchanged).
- **Hand-back:** his own move, look (flat) or jump takes over at once; the command stays on and walks on after
  `vr_nav_follow_idle` (1) s without input. Refused in deathmatch (`sv_user.c` allows `vr_nav_follow_ask` otherwise).
- **Server's corners, not a client navmesh:** the mesh needs the server's QC state (movers, rides, teleporters, props);
  a client's build would differ and cost each client a build; the corners are a small message.
- **The follower** (`vr_navfollow.hpp`): `Plan`/`replan` (where the mesh is) and `Steer`/`steer` (where the moves are
  made: corners in, yaw/forward/jump out), shared by the client's autopilot and, later, the bots. Flat and VR share it:
  only the turn differs (the view's yaw, or a headset's play space by `hands::addTurn`).
- **Bots:** they don't use the navmesh (FrikBot's learnt waypoints and roaming); NAVMESH.md 23 plans its long-range
  navigation through the follower (FrikBot keeps combat, strafing, item choice), 3-4 days, not done (his call).
- **Shown:** `vr_nav_debug` on draws the follower's path on its own client (a remote one too). `vr_nav_follow_status`.
- **Tests:** `mp_test.py navfollow` (B remote follows A) 12/0 and `navfollow_listen` (host A follows B) 11/0, flat, coop
  e1m1: from a coop start down the step and through the first room's west door to within 112 units, arrived; the
  leader walks on and is followed; +back hands it back, it walks on; `vr_nav_follow 0` stops it. No teleporter (e1m1's
  is far from the start). `navfollow_vr` (B a mock headset: the play-space turn) 12/0. mp suite --only coop, cmdguard,
  predict, teleport: passed. scenario_check PASS.

## expbugs: Dwell, Quoth and campaign bugs from his 2026-11-21 notes (expbugs, 2026-11-21, `agent/expbugs`)

Details in DWELL.md 9.8. Each note's cause and fix:

- **Music from Dwell in Quake's and SoA's maps** (hip1m1, start notes): Dwell's folder is mounted in every campaign for
  its models and sounds; `VR_FindMusicTrack` read every search path, so Dwell's `music/track02..05` won over the
  rerelease's (Quoth has no music). It now skips the paths `VR_SkipSearchPath` skips. In Dwell's own campaign, a track
  above 127 the search path has as a plain file plays it (Dwell numbers its tracks 69-254: start's 254 was read as a
  campaign-track code and played nothing). `vr_music_which [track]`, Debug > Tools > Music File. `music_test.sh`.
- **Dwell's start: runes placed, the gates seen but not taken** (the note's map was Dwell's start, "The Dwelling"): our
  PutClientInServer never fired the spawn point's targets, as Copper's does; start's `start1_targets` unlocks the
  pedestals' relays (target_lock START_LOCKED), so placing runes opened nothing: the portal sheets fade in by distance
  anyway, and walking through one met the solid wall before the real trigger_teleport 600 units on. `CU_PlayerSpawnedAt`
  (vr_copper_bridge.qc) fires them once the locks' 0.25 s have passed. Not a seamless-teleporter bug (the portal code
  finds no sides there; the teleporters work).
- **Assertion and vanishing Dwell weapons**: `weapon_touch` looked the weapon up by classname (`weapon_rifle` is none of
  ours): ASSERT, then objerror removed the pickup. It uses `self.weapon`. **Floating spinning weapons from the toolgun**
  (Dwell's three, MG3's bloody shotgun and super shotgun): they were their map pickups; now props
  (func_weapon_grabbable) with their variant (`vr_grab_dwvar`) or bloody bit (`MG3_Bloody_PropTaken`: the bit and 30
  shells when a player's hand takes it).
- **Kamikaze bursting at once, no explosion drawn**: `EntitiesTouching` (doors.qc) compares mins/maxs, true for any two
  monsters' relative boxes; now its absolute box within 8 units, or 64 apart. `DW_Boom` (TE_EXPLOSION) on its burst and
  the Construct's death.
- **Brute ragdoll triangle across his arms**: a 14-vertex piece across his front was split, its 7 right-side vertices on
  hand_r (motion clustering). `quakevr/rigs/mon_brute.rig.txt` (Rig Studio weights) puts them on hand_l.
  `vr_ragdoll_rig_spans <model> [max]` (Debug > Ragdolls) lists triangles across unjoined bones: the Brute's 6, now 0.
- **Stuck inside the Sculptor**: its 288-unit SOLID_BBOX box (the precise hits) flies noclip; onto a player, it left him
  inside. `dw_d2_freeplayers` (each think) puts him just outside: straight away from its middle, else the nearest
  heading of eight, else above, where the world has room and no wall is crossed.
- **Tests:** `dwell_weapons_test.sh` 9/0 (213: pickups taken, props laid, a bloody prop taken: 10/0); `music_test.sh`
  7/0; `dwell_maps.sh` 28/0 and 214 10/0; `dwell_monster_fixes_test.sh` (215, rig spans, 216).

## comfort2: one click one switch, the double tap's other speed, slide and eye foveation by default, the revolver's swing (comfort2, 2026-11-21, `agent/comfort2`)

His voice notes of 2026-11-21 (vrfiringrange 00-23-29, e1m1 01-04-14 and others).

- **The speed toggle switching twice: the click bounces.** His takes' replays (`NOTES.md`
  vrfiringrange_2026-11-21_00-23-29_replay.csv, the off hand's buttons bit 16) show 34 stick clicks, 9 of them followed
  11-44 ms after letting go by a press of 11-33 ms (one or two frames at 90 Hz): a second press, so a second `+speed`
  and the toggle switched back. His real clicks are 100 ms long or more and 367 ms apart at the least. The click is read
  on one path only (OpenXR's thumbstick/click into `buttonChanged`); the bounce is the switch's. **Fix:**
  `vr_stick_click_debounce` (0.08 s; Advanced > Movement > Locomotion > Stick Click Debounce; 0 off):
  `debounceStickClicks` (vr_input.cpp, in `update` before anything reads the buttons, both sticks, live or a take's) swallows
  a press that comes within the window of the click's letting go (or of a bounce's), its letting go too; a press still
  held past the window is a press then. `vr_debug_buttons` prints each swallowed bounce. **Test** `stickclick_test.sh`
  4/0: a clean click one press; his bounce pattern one press, one bounce swallowed; debounce off the same click two
  presses (the cause); two clicks 0.3 s apart both count. (The keys' commands run only after a test script, which holds
  the command buffer, so the test counts the presses leaving the debounce: `vr_doubletap_test state` prints them.)
- **The double tap is the Default Speed's other** (his ask: with Default Speed: Run it walks): in `VR_AdjustMove`
  a double tap's run gives `cl_alwaysrun`'s other, whatever the speed button (held or toggled) says; otherwise the speed
  button's choice as before. Row renamed "Double-Tap for Other Speed". `doubletap_test.sh` 8/0 (new: Default Speed:
  Run, a long push runs at 320, the taps walk at 200, and still walk with the speed toggle switched).
- **VR sliding on by default** (`vr_slide` 1; row "Sliding", no longer "Experimental"): the turning stick's straight
  pull down on foot slides; its down is no `+movedown` there (swimming it still dives). **The legs the slide's way**
  (`vr_slide_legs` 1, Slide Legs Follow Slide, after Slide Body Pose): the flat slide's turn (hips and legs to the
  slide's way, at most `vr_flat_slide_legs_twist`, back to the view past `vr_flat_slide_back_start`, eased by
  `_turn_smooth`) moved out of flatplay's poseHands into `slide::legsTurnStep` (vr_slide.cpp, `slide::LegsTurn`), which
  flat play calls as before (its view the look, its rest the long gun's stance) and a headset's slide calls once a frame
  from vr_hands.cpp (`slide::headsetLegs`: its view the tracked body's yaw). The avatar turns the local headset body's

## ragsync: ragdolls (dead and active) drawn by remote clients as the server has them (2026-11-21, `agent/ragsync`)

- His words: ragdolls not synchronized in coop; props and other physics things should be. The audit and the design:
  MP_PLAN.md, "Ragdolls and physics bodies in multiplayer". Only the ragdolls diverged: every other Box3D thing is an
  entity, already interpolated with its turn slerped (crate 0.04 units, sword 0.35 degrees p95 while moving).
- Each ragdoll in a remote client's sight is a snapshot record (QVR_SVC_RAGPOSE, `netsnap::ragKey`, vr_netragdoll.cpp):
  parts quantized (eighths, smallest-three turns), delta-coded, PVS-culled, the moving ones under
  `vr_net_ragdoll_bytes` (400) by priority, settled ones free; the client draws it between its last 24 poses at its
  entities' clock (`ragdoll::publishNet`). `vr_net_ragdolls 0`: none sent (the death animation, as before).
  QVR_NET_VERSION 42: the room service must be redeployed.
- `mp_test.py ragsync` (13/2 in its last run; the two: a gib's and a backpack's p95 at B, notes now, the test checks
  the thrown crate and sword): B's moving ragdoll parts against the server's p95 24.3 units, 153 degrees before (the
  animation), 0.18 units, 0.21 degrees after; 3.0 KB/s for the play's two ragdolls, 0 B once settled.
- Tools: `vr_mp_bodylog <seconds> [radius]` (mp_bl, mp_bp lines: a host's truth, a client's drawing).
- Open: a remote client's hands on a ragdoll aren't led locally between poses (the listen host's
  vr_ragdoll_held_local); dropped weapons and backpacks waited a little under the rate with ragdolls sent.

## ragsync2: the others never wait behind the ragdolls; a remote client's hands lead a ragdoll he holds (2026-11-21, `agent/ragsync`)

- **The regression** (ragsync's open item): with the ragdolls sent, a dropped shotgun and backpacks drifted 1.75-2.3
  units p95 at B. Not his rate (80 KB/s): the remote datagram's 1400 bytes, where the encoder chose entries by priority
  and a near ragdoll's 270-400 B record outranked them (and could take the first-finite rule's bucket debt). Now
  (netsnap `encode`, its new `ragSoft`) a ragdoll's changed record is chosen after every other entry, whatever its
  priority, never by the first-finite rule, and under a rate only from what his bucket would spill by his next datagram
  (serverEnd: tokens + rate x period - the bucket's size): the others keep the room and the bucket they'd have had
  without ragdolls. A link filled by the others starves the ragdolls (drawn between the poses they have), not them.
  Self-test: `vr_netsnap_selftest` "a ragdoll's record (the highest priority) in the room the others leave" (15/0).
- **Measured** (`mp_test.py ragsync`, last run): with the ragdolls sent, B's dropped shotgun, backpacks, crate and sword
  0.04 units p95 while moving (as without); the ragdoll parts 0.46 units, 0.75 degrees p95 (0.15-0.19 when they came
  first: the price, within the check's 2 / 3). An earlier run had one flung backpack 3.2 units p95 over a 0.8 s gib
  burst; the last run none. New note: the changed records that waited over the play, the ragdolls' and the others'
  (`vr_mp_status` mp_netsnap `rwaited=`): 268 others with ragdolls against 115 without in the last run (the second
  play has the first's corpses and gibs in sight too; 443 against 662 in another run: the counts move run to run).
- **A remote client's own hands on a ragdoll**: in his own snapshot a ragdoll he holds carries which hands hold it
  (two bits in the flags byte) and where the server had them (his hand fields, int32 eighths, 12 bytes a hand, only
  while held; `netsnap::serverPlayer`); `ragdoll::publishNet` fills the pose's held hands and the listen host's
  `leadWithHands` (vr_ragdoll_held_local) moves the drawn ragdoll with his hands since: the limb in his hand at his
  frame rate. Not harness-tested: no scenario has a remote client hold a ragdoll (his to try in VR: hold a corpse's arm
  as a client and swing it; with vr_ragdoll_held_local 0 it trails by the interpolation delay).
- Debug menu (Network): "Log Physics Bodies (5 s)" (vr_mp_bodylog 5 700), "Send Ragdolls' Parts" (vr_net_ragdolls).
- Checks: ragsync 11/0; deathbody and the 20 that never started 22/22 with --only (netsafe included); the plain suite
  62/63 (mp_dm's bot-parries-bot case under the suite's load, 27/0 alone in the --only run); single-player below.
- QVR_NET_VERSION stays 42 (the wire changed within it; agent/syncfix also takes 42: the second to ship takes 43).

## worldai: the alarm spreads to monsters round walls and after a one-shot kill; lift riders measured (worldai, 2026-11-21, `agent/worldai`)

His notes hip1m1_2026-11-21_00-20-16 ("the AI is not reacting to friendlies being shot or alerted nearby") and
e1m1_2026-11-21_00-43-41 (riders "compressed by the lift").

- **Why hip1m1's monsters didn't care**: 66 of its 73 monsters are placed in ambush (spawnflags 1), which keeps Quake's
  meaning (no relay from other monsters, deaf: `vr_stealth_ambush_deaf`). Beyond that, two real gaps, both reproduced on
  the new test map before the fix: a monster killed in one shot told nobody (T_Damage's "get mad", where the share hangs,
  is skipped by a kill: the note's three grunts at 1472 -224 each died idle to one shot, the others 88 units off stayed
  idle), and nothing reached a monster behind a wall (the share needs a clear line).

  killed by a player it wasn't after shares as if hurt (near or in sight: Hostile at him), those fighting it left out;
  `VR_Stealth_Cry` (VR_Provoke and the kill): its cry, a noise of the new kind STL_N_VOICE, `vr_stealth_share_hear`
  800 units (Combat > Stealth AI > Cries Heard), the noise rules' walls (round a corner 0.5, solid 0.15), ambushers deaf:
  Alert at it. The deferred share now carries its place, eyes and foe on the event (a gibbed body may be gone).
- **Ambushers keep their post**: an armed grunt in ambush walked 140 units off its post to the dead V's dropped gun
  ("Pick Up a Second": `VR_AG_Idle`); now an ambusher never leaves its post for a weapon until a fight starts.

  `vr_stealth_test 130` (`stealth_tests.sh alarm`, Debug > Tests > Stealth AI > The Alarm Spreading): before 4 failed
  (W behind the wall never alerted; on the kill N and S only Alert by the body's knock, A off its post); after 15/0.
  Test 107 (infighting) now kills the second grunt by the world: by the player, the third beside it rightly turned on him.

  the shot within 58 units without a navmesh step; it touches none of this; not checked on the base: **open**).
- **Lifts** (not fixed, out of budget): `vr_debug_lift 1` (Debug, a local game) measures riders on a moving MOVETYPE_PUSH:
  each ride's worst sink of the player's box, drawn feet and drawn eye, and the monsters' box and drawn feet, printed as
  the lift stops (`liftdebug: ride up|down ...`; 2: every frame). First reading on e1m1's lift *7 (-544 2656), a grunt
  riding: its server box 9.9 units into the lift going up, 15 going down (a server-side sink, not only the drawing);
  the player was not on the lift in that run (the script's setpos missed it). Suspects: SV_PushMove clearing FL_ONGROUND

  moves it every frame (`VR_StepLerpInterval` could treat riding a moving pusher as it does the air). **Open**.

## worldai2: riders on a moving lift don't sink into it (worldai2, 2026-11-21, `agent/worldai`)

His note e1m1_2026-11-21_00-43-41 ("compressed by the lift"); worldai measured a grunt's box 9.9/15 units into e1m1's lift.

- **That reading was a corpse.** The script's setpos left the player in noclip (never on the lift) and spawned the
  grunt inside the plat as it rose: the plat crushed it (blocked, 1 damage a frame, bouncing) and its body rode as a
  Box3D rigid body (`VR_PushSkips`). With the player off noclip and the grunt put on the plat at rest, no box sinks on
  the server, the player's or a monster's, up or down (SV_PushMove's clearing of FL_ONGROUND is Quake's and harmless).
  `vr_debug_lift` now takes the lift's real top under each rider (a point trace), counts live monsters only, measures
  the drawn sinking only while the lift came in the last message (and the one before), and the eye against its height
  over the feet standing still.
- **Drawn monster**: on a moving lift its steps were drawn to its next think: 12.9 units into the plat riding up.
  Drawn over a frame (VR_StepLerpInterval as for the air) it still trailed ~1.8 (the step lerp's finish counts from the
  message's time, its start from the client's), so a stepping monster standing on a moving MOVETYPE_PUSH is now sent
  without U_STEP (`VR_StepRidesLift`, sv_main.c): drawn between the last two messages exactly as the lift is: 0.03.
  Its own steps on a moving lift are drawn over the frame too.
- **Eye**: Quake's stair easing (80 units a second, at most 12 behind) took a rising lift for a step: flat 12.0 units,
  headset 14.1 (vr_hands.cpp `easeStairs` has the same rule). A rise no faster than `vr_view_lift_follow` (400 units a
  second; 0: Quake's) is followed at once in both (`VR_ViewLiftRise`, view.c and vr_hands.cpp): flat 0.03. The headset's
  eye still trails the drawn lift by one frame of its travel (2.09 at 150 units a second): its state is computed once a
  frame from the player's place before the frame's server message is read (`hands::current()`, first used by the move
  sent): a general frame-order lag, not fixed here (**open**).
- **Plat *22 not sent near its bottom**: for ~0.1 s at the start of the ride up and the end of the ride down, e1m1's
  small plat *22 is in no message (not drawn) while the player stands on it (`liftdebug: ... not in the last message`
  at vr_debug_lift 2): out of his PVS on the server? Not looked into (**open**).
- **Test** `vr_stealth_test 131` (`vr_stealth_test6.qc`, `Misc/quakevr/lift_ride_test.sh`, Debug > Tests > Stealth AI >
  Riders on a Lift): two plats, up and down, the player's box and drawn feet, eye, the grunt's: before (this branch's
  measure, old drawing) the eye 12/14 and the monster 12.9 failed; after 24 passed, 0 failed (12 headset, 12 flat).
  Debug > Logging > Lift Riders (vr_debug_lift); menu_paths.txt regenerated (Cries Heard, Lift Riders, both test rows).
- Not run (out of budget): stealth_tests.sh all (noises_clue on origin/next), the nav suite, scenario_check, ThinLTO.

## bots3: a bot's weapon placed once, on the server; the grab at the drawn weapon (2026-11-21, `agent/bots3`)

Item 1 of the brief done and tested; items 2 (Show Disarm Volumes on bots and players) and 3 (Show Hit Zones on bots and
players) not started (out of budget).

- **One placement.** `view::placeHeld` (vr_view_weapon.cpp) places a weapon in another's hand as setupWeapon draws
  another's (weaponTurn's angle offsets, the model transform's offset, the muzzle anchor, the hotspots), pure math on the
  model and the Weapon Offsets, so the dedicated server runs it. `server::botHeld` runs it at a bot's handpos/handrot:
  (a) the bot's avatar sends the weapon's place and turn (the solveBit hand's weaponBit, 12 B more; `QVR_NET_VERSION`
  42) and each client draws it there (`view::solveHands`' `placed`: the hand fitted to it), whatever its own weapon
  settings; (b) `heldpose::placeBots` (each server frame) puts the bot's hotspots into its heldpose slot (in the hand's
  frame: on the hand now, lag compensated) for QC weaponhotspot; (c) `weapondrawnpose(bot, hand, 53)` gives its muzzle,
  which bot_setvrfields now sets as `.muzzlepos`/`.offmuzzlepos` (was handpos + 24 along handrot: the grab's and the
  parry's line pointed where no weapon was drawn). Players: unchanged; a remote player's weapon is drawn where his client
  drew it, and the server's line and hotspots are his client's too: the test shows the grab at his drawn weapon holds.

  on a lit strip, `((o))` while talking (`voicechat::talkingNow`: a heard player, or you sending). Coop adds the level's
  kills and secrets line (the game's coop scoreboard). 8 px text up to 11 rows, 6 px when more (16 fit), then "+N MORE".

## raginterp: thrown props interpolated at a client while ragdolls are sent (2026-11-21, `agent/raginterp`)

- **The regression** (smallfix's item 4): with `vr_net_ragdolls 1` the crate and sword at B were drawn in steps 1-2 ticks
  ahead of the interpolation clock in some runs (baseline here: 1 run of 3, crate 6.53 / sword 2.92 units p95; 0.04 in
  the others). Neither suspect: no history reset (`h.model`) and netrag touches no entity clock. A trace of interpEntity
  showed B's clock *before each entity's oldest message* with all 8 kept: the history (8 messages, 0.11 s) was shorter
  than the adaptive delay may be (0.25 s, plus up to 0.25 s more while the clock catches up after a hitch). The
  ragdolls' bigger snapshots arrive less evenly, the delay passed 7 ticks, and interpEntity's "before the oldest" hold
  drew each moving thing at its oldest message: stepping, ahead. Latent since B7b; the ragdolls exposed it.
- **Fix** (vr_netsnap.cpp): `historyLen` 8 -> 40 messages, a static_assert tying it to delayMost + snapAfter + 3 ticks.
  (netrag's 24-pose ring per ragdoll covers the longest delay but not a hitch's catch-up; its parts pass, left as is.)
- **Measured**: mp_ragsync 5 runs in a row, all 11/0: crate p95 0.04 units every run, sword 0.04-0.05; ragdoll parts
  0.12-0.16 units p95 (limit 2). One baseline run's "settled ragdolls cost nothing" failed (4096 B in 2 s), not seen since.
- Checks: the plain suite 66 of 67 (mp_predict's "B swam" 148 of 150 states; 31/0 on its --only rerun);
  `vr_netsnap_selftest` 15/0; scenario_check PASS (150 scenes); Dev and ThinLTO builds 0 warnings.

## botnav: bots' waypoints and the navmesh together, vr_bot_navmesh (2026-11-21, `agent/botnav`)

His voice note (2026-11-21): keep FrikBot's waypoints (they make the bots go for powerups, weapons, health on any map),
add the navmesh where it is smarter: a player spotted nearby, goals by need. Design and rules: NAVMESH.md 23 (rewritten).

- **`vr_bot_navmesh`** (cvar, archived, **0** by default: FrikBot exactly as before; the host's). 1: the navmesh walks a
  bot (a) to a player it saw within `vr_bot_navmesh_memory` (5 s) and `vr_bot_navmesh_range` (1200 units) once he is out
  of its sight (in sight: FrikBot's walk and fight), unless its goal is a powerup or, under 60 health, health/armour;
  (b) to a goal with no waypoint route (`mark_path`'s failure, `bot_path`'s broken route, or no waypoint near:
  `BotNav_Look`, the best goal within the range, a player only in sight); (c) when the route is over
  `vr_bot_navmesh_detour` (1.5) times the mesh's path + 128. Waypoints again when the player is lost or far, the goal
  reached, the mesh has no path, and always in water / on a train, rocket-jump or surfacing waypoint. The three tunables
  are Debug > Tunables rows ("Bots: Navmesh ...").
- **Engine:** builtin `navbot(bot, goal, what)` (vr_builtins_nav.inc -> `navfollow::botStep`, vr_navfollow.cpp): the
  follower of NAVMESH.md 22 reused as is (`replan`, `steer`), one plan per bot by client slot, timed in server time (the
  class's build lands on its fixed frame); what 0 plan + steer (the corner), 1 state/flags/path left, 2 drop, 3 probe.
- **QC:** frikbot/bot_nav.qc (new; `BotNav_Note`, `BotNav_Step`, `BotNav_Take`, `BotNav_Look`), hooks in BotAI (one
  branch before frik_movetogoal/bot_path; the begin_route failure; the death reset), bot_path's broken route, mark_path
  ((b) and (c)). The corner becomes keys through `frik_KeysForDir` as a waypoint does; the follower's hop as `bot_jump`;
  the goal's search time kept on while the path left shrinks; waypoint flags cleared while walking the mesh (AI_WAIT
  held it still). Developer 1: `botnav: <bot> navmesh to <goal> (seen | no route | shorter)` / `... waypoints (why)`.
- **Found on the way:** a tunable can't be the switch (a release build folds tunables to constants; QC's cvar_set on one
  does nothing), so `vr_bot_navmesh` is a cvar; the player seen must be noted before BotAI's routing branch (a bot that
  is computing a route skips the walk: it never noticed him otherwise).
- **Tests** (`vr_dm_test 19-20`, QC/vr_botnav_test.qc; `maxplayers 4;deathmatch 1;developer 1;map e1m1;impulse 100;
  vr_dm_test 19`): 19 the bot at e1m1's start notices the human 160 ahead, he is put past the first room's west door
  (out of sight, no waypoint through it): navmesh 0 (contrast) FrikBot walks at the wall then roams (reached him by luck
  in 754 frames once, never in 1800 another run); navmesh 1 reaches him in 258 frames by the chase, 6/0. 20 navmesh 1, the
  human never seen, a rocket launcher at the end of a 4-waypoint chain: taken by the waypoints in 97 frames (target1 a
  waypoint, the mesh never used), 3/0.
- **Checked:** mp_test.py dm 27/0, coopbots 13/0, botgrab 9/0 with vr_bot_navmesh 0 (the verdicts as before) and the same
  with 1 (--server-set "+vr_bot_navmesh 1"); scenario_check PASS (148); Dev and ThinLTO builds 0 warnings.
- **Not ready to default on:** proven on e1m1's door and one waypoint chain only; deathmatch balance (a bot that always
  finds you), locked or button doors (the follower walks through door polygons) and the follower's drop/teleporter links
  with bots are untried.

## reliefs: Dwell's and Quoth's reliefs made on the player's PC by Setup (DWELL.md 9.9, option A)

Branch `agent/reliefs`. His choice of 2026-11-21: PBRify's CC0 models as ONNX, run by onnxruntime in a Setup step.

- **The models.** `Misc/quakevr/pbr_export_onnx.py export` loads PBRify 1.7.2's two pinned checkpoints (spandrel) and

## portcheck: is the host's port reachable? Rendezvous protocol version 3; the relay to the backlog (portcheck, 2026-11-21, `agent/portcheck`)

His words (11-21): no relay for now (BACKLOG.md, section 11, low priority: the design and how SDR / EOS / TURN do
it); an in-game indication of whether the chosen port is forwarded.

- **How it works.** Once registered, the host sends PROBECHECK (the only version 3 request; REGISTER and JOIN stay
  version 2 so a not-yet-redeployed service still gives codes) with `net_hostport`. The service (qvr_rendezvous.py
  `probecheck`) sends one PROBE from a second socket (`--probe-port`, any free one) to his outside IP at that port,
  then PROBING (1). The probe gets in only through a forward (or a router letting anything in): `Port N is reachable
  from the internet`; PROBING and no probe within 2 s: not reachable (with the forward advice); BADVERSION from a
  version 2 service: unknown (too old); no PROBING within 6 s: unknown (does not answer), asked again at the next
  registration. Checked again when a hosting starts (Datagram_Listen), his outside address or port changes.
- **Limits.** One probe per registration (REGISTER, renewal, move: the room's credit), only from the address holding
  the room (cookie-checked) and to its IP; replies to a PROBECHECK total 64 bytes (no amplification). A version 2
  request is served as version 2 (replies carry the request's version); a PROBECHECK in one is dropped.
- **Shown.** Host Game page (word-wrapped above the room code, white when reachable); the net HUD while hosting
  (`vr_net_hud` 1: `port 26000 reachable` / `NOT REACHABLE` / `unknown` / `checking`; shared with VR, the same 2D
  path); the console once; `vr_mp_roomcode` prints `Port N: ...`; `vr_net_hud_report` has `host_line`.
- **Known limit.** One service IP: a router filtering by address only (not port) reads reachable though strangers
  are filtered (rare; STUN's change-IP test would need a second IP). A forward of another outside port to 26000
  reads not reachable.
- **Checks.** test_rendezvous.py 44/0 (13 new: the probe, its limits, version 2 served, `--newest 2`); `mp_test.py nat`
  18/0 (room service off: unknown; cone NAT without a forward: not reachable; forwarded port: reachable; a version 2
  service: code still given, unknown); roomui 6/0 (the HUD line; the page's shot looked at); netsafe 14/0. Dev build
  0 warnings, ThinLTO 0 warnings.
- **He must redeploy the service** (`bash Misc/rendezvous/update.sh vittorioromeo.com`) for real games to read
  reachable/not reachable; until then they read unknown and room codes work as before.

## pouchbody: the pouches with the body hidden

- **His note (2026-11-21, Quest):** "with vr_body_mode 0 I was not able to interact with the ammo pouch". Why: with the
  body hidden, `body::ammoPouchPosition` and `body::pouchPosition` (vr_body.cpp) returned the old placement carried by
  the pelvis, skipping the step that puts it on the torso's ring (`ammoPouchOnTheBody`, `pouchOnTheBody`). That point is
  inside the player's own body (the torso's ring there, clearance included: ammo pouch 0.86, grenade pouch 0.47; 1 is
  the surface), and the ammo pouch's zone is thin (depth 0.2 times its reach: 1 unit each way), so its box ran from the
  belly's surface to 5 cm in front of it: a real controller could hardly get in. The grab test was never gated on the
  body; the mock hands reach any point, so the old tests passed in every mode.
- **Fix:** both pouches are put on the ring whether the body is drawn or not (mode 0 now has mode 2's places; the
  armour plates' forward step and the legs' follow stay with the drawn body, which they need). The holsters were
  already outside the torso in mode 0 (hips 1.78, chest 1.00) and are unchanged; modes 1-3 are unchanged.
- **Diagnostic:** `vr_body_crouch_report` also prints `gear ring: body <mode> lhip .. rhip .. lupper .. rupper .. ammo ..
  grenade ..` (under 1: inside the player, out of a real hand's reach).
- **Test:** `Misc/quakevr/reload/pouchbody_test.sh` 12/0: with `vr_body_mode` 0, 2 and 3 every gear ring at least 1
  (mode 0 was 0.86 and 0.47 before the fix: FAIL), a shell from the ammo pouch, a magazine from it seated in the nailgun,
  a grenade from the grenade pouch. Checklist scene `pouchbody` (Only Hands, the shotgun and the nailgun, ammo).

## Quest C5c: the body's triangles, batched lightmap uploads, loads past a throttling runtime (questc5c, 2026-11-21; branch agent/quest)

- **Why the body cost so much**: the bare forearms (`vr_body_bracers 0`, the shipped look) were lofted with 144 sides
  from the shoulder to the wrist (`make_vrbody.py`: 144 to follow the jointed hand's wrist section), 9,800 of the
  body's 10,874 triangles. Now 24 sides up to the last forearm ring and 144 only from there to the wrist and the lip
  over the hand, joined by a stitched band (`loft(hi_sides, hi_from)`): **4,154 triangles, 2,372 vertices** (was
  10,874 / 5,732); every build's bare mesh regenerated (the clothed meshes byte-identical; the skins not rewritten).
  PC mock, e1m1's spawn looking down (`vr_mock_look 60 0`, `vr_model_fragments 32`): the body group 0.099 -> **0.072
  ms** a pass, 27,446 -> 13,110 vertex runs, 98.6k -> 66.2k fragment runs (the thin triangles' quads cost fragments
  too). Quest (unworn, frozen fight, 0.55): GPU span 3.71 -> 3.55 ms with the new mesh.
- **`vr_alias_prepass_body`** (new, 1; Debug > Profiling and Memory > Body Pre-pass): the body's depth pre-pass off.
  Slower on both: PC 0.091 ms a pass against 0.072, the Quest +0.33 ms span. Stays 1 (an A/B switch).
- **`vr_gl_world_dlmap_batch`** (new, 1; Debug > Profiling and Memory): with `vr_gl_world_dlmap 1` the frame's lit and
  restored texel blocks go into a CPU copy of the lightmap and up in one `glTexSubImage2D` per band of 16 rows, not
  one per surface. Quest, frozen fight with 3 big test lights (`scratch/c5c_run2.sh`, 4 rounds interleaved): the loop
  GPU span **9.79** ms (world 7.40); the lightmap path unbatched 5.47 ms GPU, 6.61 ms CPU, frames missed (period
  14.71); **batched 3.96 ms GPU (world 2.19, the lights' own cost ~0.2), 1.81 ms CPU** (busy 6.24 -> 7.89); no test
  lights 3.78. PC: 141 uploads -> 16, the picture the same (its difference under two frames' own noise).
  `vr_gl_world_dlmap` stays 0 (the 16-unit lightmap look is his call); with the batch it is the big cut.
- **Loads past a throttling runtime** (`vr_backend_openxr_frame.cpp`, `loadThrottled`): while the client is not signed
  on and the last `xrWaitFrame` blocked 250 ms or more, host frames run unwaited (`paceUnwaited`), `xrWaitFrame` tried
  again every 0.5 s; the log notes it (`OpenXR: xrWaitFrame blocked ... during a load`, `the load ended; N host frames
  ...`). A normal headset's 14 ms waits never trigger it. PC OpenXR shares the backend.
- **Unworn headset tests**: with `prox_close` held, the still headset's Guardian dialog relaunched every 10-30 s and
  the app never started (`am start` said Starting, no process). **Without `prox_close`** the unworn, still headset in
  a lit room gave full 72 Hz frames (period 14.0 ms) and e1m1 loaded in seconds: `scratch/c5c_ab.sh` holds the sensor
  only with `PROX=1`.
- **The ledger**: `docs/vr-port/QUEST_OPTIMISATIONS.md`, every Quest renderer optimisation so far with its measured
  gain, cvar, ES-only flag and a judgement for the PC.
