## brushholes: invisible blockers in the gaps Quake's box never fit (branch agent/brushholes, 2026-11-21)

The author's note: grates, gates, pillars and lifts let the narrower boxes (yours at 16, narrow monsters') pass or fall
through. At map load, `Quake/vr/vr_hull_holes.cpp` finds every gap narrower than 32 between two solids facing each
other along x or y: within the world, within each solid func_* model, and between the world and a func_wall or a
door's or lift's whole travel. It adds blocker brushes there, to the compiled trees only (not hull 0: shots, sight and
the navmesh don't have them). Quake's box could never hold a point of such a gap, so nothing Quake allowed changes,
and you still stop 8 units from walls, bars and pillars. How it works, what is kept out (gaps under 8; world blockers
that hull 1 lets Quake's box reach into, from AD's non-colliding detail) and the census are in HULLS.md, "Holes".

- Setting: `vr_hull_holes` 1 (Movement > Player Hitbox > Close Gaps Quake's Box Never Fit; it takes effect at the next
  map load). `keyOf`'s buildVersion went from 2 to 3, so every map's trees are compiled once again; the blockers are kept
  for a reload and are inside the disk-cached trees.
- Aids (Debug > Tests > Player Hitbox): `vr_hull_holes_census`, `vr_hull_holes_near`, `vr_hull_holes_test`.
- Test: `vr_hull_holes_test` on the new `maps/vrbrushholes` (`Misc/quakevr/make_vrbrushholes_map.py`: a grate over a
  pit, a bar gate, a lift held up with 20-unit slots, pillars 24 apart). The player's box and a grunt's at
  `vr_mhull_army 16`: 15/0 with the setting on (stopped, and 8 units from the bars, the pillars and a wall) and 15/0 as
  `brushholes_off` with it off (they pass, so the scene really has holes). Checklist scenes: `brushholes_grate`,
  `brushholes_gate`, `brushholes_lift`, `brushholes_pillars` (runall 4 OK).
- Follow-up (the coordinator and the author): the drop test is now exact. Every centre of Quake's box that would
  reach a blocker by 2 units goes down hull 1's tree at once, for the world's blockers and the models' own, erring
  toward dropping. The search uses a 64-unit grid, and the checks and the brush models run on the pool. The debug view
  is Debug > Show Gap Blockers (`vr_hull_holes_show`, `vr_hull_holes_show_range` 1024): world cyan, with brush models
  yellow, models' own magenta, dropped red, the counts in front of you. Scene `brushholes_show`.
- Census: id1 (38 maps) 8,018 world blockers, search at most 53 ms; Quoth (6) 3,533; AD (26) 103,707, at most 0.5 s
  (ad_tears, was 1.6 s). Quake's box reaches none, on any of the 70 maps.
- Checks: `vr_hull_holes_test` 15/0 on and 15/0 off; 5 scenes OK; `vr_nav_cliptest` and `vr_nav_toptest` pass on e1m1
  and e4m7; a 60 s hull walk on e1m2 had 0 stuck; run_test_suite changelevel_signon, held_over_props, slider_step,
  slopes and turned_box pass, teleporters_chase flaky (known).
- Open: ad_tears' search time (slanted cells; coarser ones leave gaps open); func_trains' gaps with the world (only their own gaps are closed); a func_wall that is
  killtargeted is left out of the world's pairs (its blockers would stay behind).

## fixes1121: noclip flies where you look; a shove never bleeds (branch agent/fixes1121, 2026-11-21)

- **Noclip (his note: "always go towards where the camera is pointing").** The server's `SV_NoclipMove` takes a
  tracked-hands client's move (a headset's and the flatscreen mode's: `VR_NoclipAngles`) along the head's level yaw with
  upmove doubled straight up, so flat noclip never rose or sank and VR's rise came only from the stick's upmove (about
  55 degrees for a 45-degree look). Now `VR_AdjustMove` (vr_input.cpp `noclipFlies`, `flyMove`) puts the flight's pitch
  in the move: a push along the steer (pitch, yaw) becomes its level part on forward/side and its rise on upmove at half
  (the server doubles it). The keys' push follows the look (the head; the flatscreen view); the stick's follows what
  steers its walking (`vr_movement_mode`: the moving hand, the head, or the torso's yaw at the head's pitch). Strafes stay
  level; the up and down keys (jump, crouch) go straight up and down. Local games only (Quake's own
  `noclip_anglehack`, set by `noclip` and `setpos`); a remote server's noclip flies level as before.
- **Test:** `vr_noclip_fly_test` (Debug > Tests, Stick Locomotion: Noclip: Flies Where You Look): from 64 units over
  where you stand, each case's climb (degrees, the server's player over 40 frames of the push) against the look's:
  keys forward at 45 up 44.8, 45 down -44.8, level 0.0, a strafe at 45 up 0.0, the up key 90.0; with a headset the
  stick, the head 45 up 45.0, a hand (mode 0, the mock's hand turned to 30 up) 29.7. VR 7/0, `-flatscreenmode` 5/0 (the
  stick's cases skipped). `vr_stick_curve_test` 115/0 (its noclip cases set the movetype only: unchanged).
- **The shove's blood: cause.** The shove itself is bloodless (`VR_Hit_Bloodless`, QVR_HITKIND_SHOVE) and a fresh
  monster's active ragdoll never bled in any test (grunts and knights, one- and two-handed, VR `vr_knockdown_test 21`
  and the flat `vr_flat_shove_now`, staggers that recover and falls, awake or not: 0 frames of limb trails). What bled
  "from every limb" was `decals::limbTrail` on a live ragdoll whose `.vr_bloodied` was set: that flag never cleared, so
  a monster that had ever drawn blood (one pellet, minutes before) trailed blood from each limb end whenever a later
  shove flung it (measured: hurt 5, then shoved down: 220 frames bled).
- **Fix:** QC `VR_Wound_Hit` stamps `.vr_bled_at` (time) on every blood-drawing hit; the engine's `limbsBleed(ent, since)`
  (vr_box3d_ragdoll.cpp) lets a live ragdoll's limbs bleed only for blood drawn since its ragdoll was made
  (`RagdollBodies::born`; a get-up's blend keeps it in `Recovery::since`) or within `bledGrace` (1 s) before it (shot and
  shoved together). Corpses' limbs always bleed, as before; a progs without the field keeps the old `.vr_bloodied` rule.
  Fall damage and the ragdoll's own impacts still draw no blood (world inflictor), as before.
- **Test:** `Misc/quakevr/ragdoll/shove_blood_test.sh` 3/0: an unhurt grunt shoved down bled 0 frames; one shot 3 s
  before the shove 0 (was 220); one shot 2 frames before the shove 106. `stagger_test.sh steady` (grunt, 3 each) PASS.
- **Checklist scenes:** `noclip_fly`, `shove_no_blood` (`vr_scenario runall`: 2 run, 0 failed).

## Quest C5d: the body's worn cost found; a posed head for unworn GPU tests (questc5d, 2026-11-21; branch agent/quest)

- **Why the body costs ~1 ms worn**: its fragment shading, in proportion to the pixels it covers, and nothing else (no
  second pass, no world lights, not its vertices: in a level view with the body out of sight it costs nothing). Quest at
  1.0: pitch 35 (forearms, hands, holsters) +1.9 ms span; pitch 70 (the torso in the lower half) +11.9 ms. The floor
  it hides was cheap (the main pass 5.33 -> 5.16), so its pixels add up. The recorder's "world_brush" holds it (the
  tiler's timers measure the whole binned pass). PC: 0.07 ms a pass, the eyes on/off within 0.02 ms.
- **Inside its shader** (pitch 70, 0.7, `vr_gles_define` early-return probes): texture 0.6, look (skin tone, wounds,
  dents) 0.15, **light ~4 ms** (per-pixel dynamic lights on models 1.85 with his `vr_dlight_models 1`: the rig's two
  lights reach every body pixel; the own light's ambient and bumps 0.9), tail 0.85. Details: QUEST_PLAN.md 6zo.
- **`vr_debug_head_pose`** (new, 0; Debug > Profiling and Memory > Pose the Head, with `vr_debug_head_pitch` 0 and
  `vr_debug_hands_front` 0; OpenXR only): the rendered head set level at the pitch, 1.65 m high, the hands in front at
  the waist; the layers keep the runtime's poses. An unworn headset draws a worn view (`scratch/c5d_ab.sh`).
- **Worn A/B for him**: `qvr-kit/scratch/quest_worn_ab.py push`, `exec quest_worn_ab.cfg` in the game (3 min: base,
  body off, dlmap, both, 3 rounds, each marked), then `quest_worn_ab.py report`.
- **Open (C5e)**: the cut (a body-only light form), `vr_depth_float 0`, the resolution step. Unworn runs over ~11 ms
  GPU are paced at 40-55 ms by the runtime: measure at 0.7.

## humrepl2: the recolours dye only clothes and packs, keep the shading; the Texture Studio (branch agent/humrepl2, 2026-11-21)

His verdict on phase 1: "The recolors look a bit unnatural and also affect the skin/faces of the enemies." The cause: a
hue band can't separate brown uniforms from brown flesh, and a full hue turn with a saturation boost flattens the shading.

- **The rows (each skin's 8-bit histogram, `scratch/humrepl2_skins.py`):** grunt (vrgrunt = id1 soldier, 256x256)
  rows 1 30866, 10 15825, 7 9301, 6 5274, 4 1079; enforcer (576x384) 0 74933, 1 59349, 10 41345, 7 18996, 3 10256, 6 6325;
  knight (256x256) 10 32138, 1 9560, 4 6237, 7 5602, 6 3647; death knight (512x196) 1 56793, 10 25496, 7 6425, 4 4326;
  backpack.mdl (128x128) 1 14980, 7 859. Regions: uniforms and leather rows 1 and 10 (browns, tans), the enforcer's
  trousers 3, flesh 7 (peach), blood 4, the knights' plates 10, the enforcer's shoulder pads 6. Separating: flesh (7)
  from cloth (1, 10) everywhere; not separating: the grunt's arm and face highlights sit on row 10 like its uniform
  (fixed by the flesh neighbourhood), the enforcer's baked pack shares its armour's rows (fixed by painted texels), the
  knights' blood and red cloth share row 4 (left alone). AD's `mon_*.mdl` skins vary (mon_hknight row 8 23041, row 3
  5781; mon_enforcer row 3 24049): they get their key's rows; candidates for the studio's own rows.
- **Masks** (`vr_humlook.cpp`, `quakevr/humlook_masks.txt`): per skin and key, 2 bits a texel, made as it is first drawn
  from the model file's indices; painted texels, else flesh (`flesh 7`, and `fleshnear 0.35 2`: a quarter-plus of the
  5x5 neighbours flesh), else the row's class. SSBO 17 (`HumMasks`, 512 KB, rewritten when edited), bound beside the
  barrel masks (r_alias.c `VR_HumlookBind`). The instance's `Recolor` grew to four rows (the ragdoll's copy too).
- **Dye** (`HumDye`): the texel's luminance (times `light`) in the row's colour, clamped (a red stays red), or with `tint`
  its own colour times the colour; by `strength`. Table: `r g b strength light tint` (the old 13-number rows are gone).
- **Texture Studio** (Debug > Tools; `vr_humstudio.cpp`): see ARMED_MONSTERS.md "Recolours by weapon". Painting shares
  one stroke path for VR and flat: only the ray differs (a hand's aim / the view's centre); flat's attack is eaten while
  painting (cl_input.c `VR_HumStudioAttack`), VR's trigger, grip and B/Y (vr_input.cpp). The ray meets the posed model
  (its frame's first pose, not interpolated) and its triangle's ST gives the texel.
- **Tests:** `Misc/quakevr/humrepl2_test.sh` PASS (5 masks: vrgrunt 46691 clothes, vrenforcer 90875 clothes + 20075
  pack, vrknight, vrhknight 56793, backpack 14980; 0 texels on the flesh or blood rows; a stroke 113 texels, undone);
  `humrepl_test.sh` 46/0; `vr_multiview_check` 99/0; screenshots `humrepl_shots.sh` (before/after per type x category,
  and `overlay`). Not tested: the studio's sliders and row toggles by hand in the menu (the cvars and commands are).
- **Open:** AD's own skins unlooked at; the knights' red cloth (row 4, shared with blood) not dyed; flesh rule's share is
  file-only (not on the page).

  centre popup into its image). `vr_panel.cpp`: `VR_CenterPrintInView` (called by `SCR_CheckDrawCenterString` after the wrist and
  the visor) and `panel::centerShow` (the view messages, `vr_worldtext.cpp`) claim the panel for the frame; `VR_End2D` renders
  the image, `drawCenterPanel` shows it next frame on the HUD's head-following place (`hudAngles`, `vr_view_text_smooth`,
  `vr_menu_distance`), at Quake's height (line 70 of 200, 48 over 4 lines), as a textured quad with a frame line. One visor
  pixel is one menu pixel: `vr_center_panel_scale` (2) makes it larger than the HUD's own text, small at the menu's distance.

## projheadpop: heavy revolver head pops with AD's projectile slugs (agent/projheadpop, 2026-11-22)

His note (2026-11-21): where shells fly as projectiles (AD, Quoth) a heavy revolver's headshot never popped the head;
hitscan's always did.

- **Why:** AD_FirePellets (vr_ad_bridge.qc) gave each pellet its head-pop identity (`vr_ad_shotweapon`) from the gun in
  hand, and only for the shotgun, the super shotgun and the burst rifle's id shotgun: the revolver's slug flew with 0, so
  VR_AD_PelletHit's VR_Decap_Pellet / VR_Decap_BlastArm never armed it. Its big-body rule (`vr_pellet_heavy_mult`,
  applied in FireBulletsImpl) was lost too: the globals are cleared before the pellet lands (an ogre took ~30 a slug
  instead of hitscan's ~50).
- **Fix (one rule for both paths):** the pellet now takes the firing function's own `vr_decap_weapon` (what hitscan's
  VR_Decap_HeadBlastArm uses: shotgun, super shotgun, Widowmaker, Dwell's guns, the revolver), falling back to the old
  gun-in-hand rule when it's unset (direct AD_FirePellets callers: the AD shot tests). The big-body rule is one helper,
  `VR_PelletHeavy` (vr_defs.qc), used by FireBulletsImpl and, from the pellet's `vr_ad_heavymult` / `vr_ad_heavyhealth`,
  by VR_AD_PelletHit. Quoth's maps run under AD's rules, so the same path. Pops stay the player's only (BlastArm's
  FL_CLIENT test), as in hitscan: an armed grunt's revolver pops no heads either way.
- **New test** `vr_rv_test 6` (rvpop, vr_revolver_test.qc; e1m1, `-QuitOn "rvpop: [0-9]+ passed"`): a slug fired as
  W_FireRevolver fires it at a plain grunt's head and body, hitscan (vr_ad_projectiles 1) and AD's (2); AD's shotgun
  blast at a head (vr_decap_pop_roll 0); a slug into an ogre's body both ways (vr_positional_damage 0,
  vr_revolver_dmg_random 0): 7 passed (ogre 52 hitscan, 50 AD's). Without the fix: 5 passed, 2 failed (AD's head shot,
  the ogre 30). Scene `revolver_adheadpop`.
- **Checks:** ad_pop_odds_test.sh PASS (3 volleys topped up to their final chance); limbs_test.sh live on the grunt as
  before (the lightning bolt's limb case kills nothing there, untouched by this); scenario_check PASS (179 run, 0
  failed); Dev and ThinLTO built, 0 warnings.

## vrcenterprint2: VR centre messages drawn by the flat visor's own popup code (agent/vrcenterprint2, 2026-11-22)

- **His verdict (11-22):** vrcenterprint's panel (the contents image, a plain black box with a thin line) was not the flat
  visor's centre message (a dark glass pill, cut corners, a glowing bevelled frame). Now the headset draws the flat one.
- **How (vr_visor.cpp):** the flat visor's per-panel code takes its pass (`drawPanel`, `useSlot`, `drawList`,
  `packAtlas`, `buildPanels(lp, layer, ss, only)`); its per-panel uniforms (`panelUniforms`) and scanlines
  (`scanUniforms`) are shared by the window's composite and the headset's. `renderHeadsetCenter` (VR_End2D, the headset's
  frames): `update()` steps the popup's fade and pop in as the flat one does (`vr_flat_visor_center_pop`, `_center_fade`,
  Quake's `con_notifyfade`), the contents image (`gadget::renderCenterPanel(text, boot)`: its power-on scan), then the
  centre popup alone built into a second atlas (`buildPanels(..., VisorCenter)`: back plate, glass face, sheen, glows,
  bevelled frame) on a layer of its own (no lens, zoom, sway or glass: a virtual pixel 4 texels, the view's height chosen
  so layerFor's unit gives the flat edges' and glows' width against the text at `vr_flat_visor_scale`), composited by
  the flat layer program into a texture of the popup's box (`visor::headsetCenter`). vr_panel.cpp draws it premultiplied
  on the HUD's head-following place, its text where it was (Quake's height). Claims: `visor::claimCenter` (the flat
  `VR_CenterPrintOnVisor`, `VR_CenterPrintInView`, `panel::centerShow`'s view messages): one state, one fade.
- **Not in the headset:** the glass's blur of the view behind (defaults: 6 px blur, no tint or desaturation; the face
  lets the world through at `vr_flat_visor_opacity` instead: there is no view behind a world quad to frost).
- **Checks:** `vr_center_panel_info` prints the popup's fade, pop, box and contents (visor pixels). Side by side, flat
  screenshot and VR eyeshot of the same short, long and 3-line messages: the same box sizes (216x38 for the 3 lines), frame
  hue within 8%, a glow past the frame and a dark face in both (scratch/vcp2_side.ps1: 3 passed, 0 failed;
  scratch/vcp2/side.png).


## Quest C5f: why the body costs; its lights Quake's way (vr_gl_alias_body 2); dlmap pairs (questc5f, 2026-11-22; branch agent/quest)

- **Why the body is expensive**: the pixels it covers times the work per pixel. Close to the eyes it covers much of the
  view, and each of its pixels runs the models' whole shader (~3-4 ns a pixel on the Quest 3, the world ~1-2; its light
  ~4 of ~5 ms at pitch 70). Already in place, so not the cause: drawn before the world (`vr_alias_player_first`) with a
  depth pre-pass (no overdraw inside it); fixed foveation does not reach it (`vr_xr_foveation` 0 and guarded, and the
  runtime foveates only the swapchain images, not our scene targets). QUEST_PLAN.md 6zq.
- **`vr_gl_alias_body 2`** (Debug > Tunables > "Body Lighting (Quest)" > "Quake's Way"; ES only; default 0 until timed):
  the body's dynamic lights added to its light on the CPU once a frame (`r_alias.c` `R_AliasLightFinishBody`, each as
  the per-pixel loop gives its origin: `VR_DlightFlatLit`), its form with only the ambient cube at its vertices
  (`QVR_APLAIN_VFLAT`); a batch another form draws gets the light without them. PC `-glescompat` looking down with the
  flashlight: mean 4.4 levels, 16% of pixels over 8. Probes `QVR_PROBE_AMEDIUMP`, `ANOFOG`, `ANOFB`.
- **dlmap pairs** for him: `qvr-kit/scratch/dlmap_compare_*.png` (PC, 1024x1024 eyeshots): big lights much brighter and
  flatter in the lightmap (doorway mean 60 -> 105), torches alike. No `_lmscale` scene exists (no LMSHIFT support, none
  in the installed AD).
- **Not done**: the APK (vr_menu.cpp's NDK compile went past the 40-minute job limit under load), so no Quest numbers:
  the per-part table (`scratch/c5f_parts.sh`), Quake's way timed, the FFR probe, `vr_depth_float 0`, the resolution step.
## embeddual: flat dual wielding, an embedded blade keeps its hand (agent/embeddual, 2026-11-22)

His words (2026-11-21, flat): "When dual-wielding a bladed weapon and a gun, if the bladed weapon gets embedded into an
enemy, the hand that is supposed to wield it stops holding it visually and goes to hold the gun in a 2H pose ... ADS also
becomes possible in that state".

- **Why:** a held stab or swing that stays in (QC/vr_embedhold.qc) empties the hand's weapon slot (VR_HOLD_EMBED: the blade
  is a stuck thrown_weapon, the hand on it). Flat play read the hand's contents only from its weapon, carry and held
  entity, so it saw one gun and an empty hand: `flatsight` pinned that hand to the gun's two-handed grip (its drawing won
  over the embed pin's), the stance came on, RMB became the ironsight's and the ironsight came up.
- **One check, shared:** `axestick::handOnBlade(h)` / `heldStat(h)` (vr_axestick.hpp; client: STAT_QVR_EMBEDMAIN /
  _EMBEDOFF), now used by every reader of those stats (vr_avatar.cpp's arm stretch, vr_handpose.cpp's wall stop,
  vr_modelcollide.cpp, vr_gadgetlock.cpp, vr_view_hands.cpp's embed pin) and by:
  - **flat:** `flatplay::holdsThing` (a hand on a stuck blade is busy as with a prop): emptyHand is false for it, so no grip
    pin, no stance, no two-handed melee stance; routeButtons gives each button its own hand (RMB no ironsight); and
    `flatsight::adsApplies` now also asks for an empty other hand, so `vr_flat_aim 1` from the console is refused too (also
    with a prop in the other hand, which matches FLATPLAY.md's rule: "the ironsight only with one gun and an empty other
    hand"). The blade's hand keeps whatever pose flat gives an empty hand; the drawn hand is the shared embed pin
    (vr_view_hands.cpp embedPinStep, as in VR), and QC's rules let go past arm reach (`vr_embed_arm_letgo`) as before.
  - **VR and flat:** vr_twohand.cpp's helping hand (`helperFree`: held::handEmpty and not on a stuck blade) for the hotspot
    hold, the free grips and the carry grips: a hand holding a stuck blade never takes the other gun's two-handed grip (VR
    could, for the frames before QC's off-axis pull freed the blade). held::handEmpty itself is unchanged: it mirrors QC's
    VRIsHandEmpty, which flat E's force grab (the recall) relies on.
- **Probe:** `vr_flat_route_probe` gained bits 256 (a hand on the other hand's gun: twohand helping, the grip pin or the
  stance's look), 512 / 1024 (the main / off hand drawn within 16 units of the stuck blade it holds; the distances printed).
- **Test** `vr_embed_test 52` (embeddual, QC/vr_embeddual_test.qc, `Misc/quakevr/embeddual_test.sh`; -flatscreenmode,
  vrtesthall; Debug > Tests "Flat Dual Wielding: an Embedded Blade Keeps Its Hand Check"): an axe and a shotgun, the
  axe's flat swing (`vr_flat_punch`) into a grunt until it stays in (retries a miss, at most 4): case 0 axe main, case 1
  axe off. Embedded: drawn on the blade (0.0 units), no hand on the gun, VRGet2HAiming 0, the ironsight down though asked
  for, LMB main / RMB off; case 0 VR_Embed_Free: the axe back in the hand, dual again; case 1 VR_Embed_DropHand: the free
  hand on the gun and the ironsight up (ads 1.00). 16 passed, 0 failed. With the fix disabled: 5 passed, 5 failed (the
  hand drawn off the blade, on the gun, the ironsight up, RMB the ironsight's). Scene `flat_embed_dual`.
- **Checks:** Dev and ThinLTO built, 0 warnings; scenario_check PASS (183 run, 0 failed); embed tests 33 (embedgrip) 15/0, 24 (embedfeel) 22/0, 13 (embededge) 62/4: the known run-to-run four
  (the grip 64 units off, cases 8/9, standing or staggering; this file's "vr_embed_test 13" notes above). Flat:
  `vr_flatitems_test 10` (routing, ironsight with an empty hand) 63/0, 7 (a prop beside the gun) 13/0, flathands 76/0,
  flatmelee2h 16/0, flatads 6/1 (its "launchers", the outdated expectation of ROUND24.md).

## Quest C5g: dlmap as bright as the loop, its own texture; vr_menu.cpp at -Os on Android; Quake's way timed (questc5g, 2026-11-22; branch agent/quest)

- **APK build time**: the NDK's clang spent 1096 of vr_menu.cpp's 1199 s at -O3 in one pass, the *PostRA Machine
  Instruction Scheduler* (`-ftime-report`); -O1 still ran past 600 s, -Os takes 17 s. `Android/android.cmake` compiles
  that file alone at -Os (menu code). The whole native build after a merge (every file): 4 min 25 s, the APK 5 min 37 s
  (was over 18 min for vr_menu.cpp alone; c5f's 40-minute job limit killed it). 0 warnings, check_apk 20/20.
- **dlmap's brightness**: the light was added into the lightmap's bytes, so the world shader's curve on the baked light
  (vr_light_contrast 2.5 about Quake's full light, the fill light 0.1, vr_light_cap 1.75) bent it too, and the bytes
  clipped at 255; and on the PC's defaults (normal maps: the parallax program; OIT) the world never took the unlit form,
  so c5f's pairs showed the lightmap's light *on top of* the loop's (counted twice). Now the lights are summed into
  their own texture (RGB10_A2, as big as the lightmap and laid out as it: `DlightTex`, unit 15, 4x range), which
  glprogs.world_unlit adds where the loop adds its own (`dynamic_light`: after the curve, under the same cap rule); the
  lightmap itself is never written. Same falloff, angle term and colour as the loop (DarkPlaces' or Quake's); what is
  left: the 16-unit grid and the loop's sheen (vr_specular 0.2 on the Quest), which the texture has no direction for.
- **The pairs again, under the Quest preset** (PC -glescompat, the same 7 frames, 922x922 left eyes,
  `qvr-kit/scratch/dlmap_compare_*.png`; c5f's parked in `F:/QVR-Parked/2026-11-22/quest_c5f/dlmap_pairs_c5f`):
  | scene | c5f means (0 / 1) | now means (0 / 1) | now diff mean / p95 / max |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | ad_azad | 80.1 / 108.6 | 83.6 / 80.2 | 3.56 / 14 / 149 |
  | corridor_rocket | 58.5 / 45.6 | 59.1 / 55.0 | 4.24 / 36 / 203 |
  | doorway | 63.0 / 111.1 | 56.3 / 56.2 | 0.74 / 4 / 59 |
  | sweep1 | 58.9 / 66.7 | 60.0 / 57.0 | 3.06 / 18 / 113 |
  | sweep2 | 56.5 / 69.3 | 57.8 / 57.0 | 0.87 / 5 / 60 |
  | sweep3 | 69.2 / 74.1 | 69.2 / 63.6 | 5.62 / 41 / 153 |
  | torch_wall | 24.7 / 25.6 | 23.8 / 24.8 | 1.61 / 8 / 196 |
  Darker by 0-6 levels where a big light is close (the sheen and the grid's peak); no seams (the image's steps 0.98-1.00 of the loop's; torch_wall 1.07: its flicker).
- **One choice: `vr_gl_quake_dlights`** ("Quake-Style Dynamic Lights (Quest)", Debug > Profiling and Memory, archived,
  default 0): the world's light texture (as vr_gl_world_dlmap 1) and your body's flat add (as vr_gl_alias_body 2) at
  once; each light as the per-pixel loop gives it, added after the baked light's curve (`qvr::dlightmap::quakeLights`).
- **On the Quest** (posed head, 0.7 fixed, the Quest's switches, 3 rounds interleaved, gpu_span ms):
  | scene | loop | world in texture | Quake both (vr_gl_quake_dlights) | body flat only | no test lights |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | frozen fight, 3 big lights, 0.55 | 11.33 (period 41.6: 24 Hz) | **7.00** (72 Hz; CPU +1.50) | 8.24 | - | 6.10 |
  | posed head pitch 35, 0.7, test lights | 7.77 | 8.17 | 10.52 | 9.98 | 8.63 |
  | body, pitch 70 (off / per pixel / Quake's way / vertex) | 6.08 / 11.10 / 13.71 / 13.74 | | | | |
  | body, pitch 35 (off / per pixel / Quake's way / vertex) | 5.87 / 7.81 / 10.57 / 10.65 | | | | |
  Quake's way on the body is **slower** (+2.6 ms at 70, +2.8 at 35; period 50 ms at 70 for both of its forms), so it
  stays off; the Quest preset gets `vr_gl_world_dlmap 1` (all three levels) and `vr_gl_quake_dlights` stays 0.
- **Reliefs**: no relief on the Quest preset (vr_normalmaps 0), so the flatness there is the missing sheen and the
  16-unit grid, not bumps. A cheap fix exists for the PC look: a second texture (RGBA8) with the summed lights'
  dominant direction per texel (as AD's .lux), the shader bending the texel's light by the bumped normal and giving it
  the sheen: one more fetch and ~10 ALU a pixel, the direction summed on the CPU (+30% of the build). Not done: no
  gain where dlmap is meant to run.
- **Not done (budget)**: the per-part body table, `vr_depth_float 0`, the resolution step, Quest eyeshots of the pairs,
  the foveation measurement (`vr_xr_direct 1` + `-xrfoveation`, `vr_xr_foveation 3`). What blocks vr_xr_direct as a
  default (from its help and 6v): no post-process at all (no tone curve: bright colours clip; no bloom, grade, AA
  resolve), single-pass stereo off (each eye drawn alone: more CPU and draws), only the scene reaches the swapchain.
  Why Quake's way on the body is slower is open (both its forms the same: the form's program itself, not its light).
## Faster release tests: lanes, a beta profile, quicker batches (branch agent/testspeed, 2026-11-22)

- **run_test_suite.py**: tests in parallel lanes (`--jobs N`; 0: a lane per 8 CPUs, at most 4, 2 while the author's
  game runs; the kit's `QVR_LANE`: own game folder, lock and batch copies). `qvrtest.lane_keys` keeps apart lane-0
  scripts, "alone" ones (timing runs; mapgun_pickup's `quakevr/maps/e1m3.ent`), testbatch suites (at most
  `--batch-jobs` 2) and "tele" (the vrteleporters builders and stealth); the summary in the suite's order.
  `--profile full|beta` (PROFILES); scenario_check joined the suite.
- **make_release.ps1**: `-TestProfile full|beta` (default beta for an x.y.z-betaN version, or `-Beta`; a final
  release refuses beta), `-TestJobs N`. RELEASING.md "Tests before publishing", TESTING.md "The release suite: lanes
  and profiles".
- **testbatch.sh**: `tb_run_sh` starts no process (its index: the runs' arguments, in memory; was ~8 processes a run
  in each pass, each 0.1-1 s under Git bash on a loaded machine). `TB_COLLECT_STUBS=1` (the reload suites): the
  collect pass's grep/sed/cut/tr/head/tail/wc/paste/sort/python are no-ops (a run whose arguments then come out
  different is still played, alone: correct, only slower; `TB_STATS` lists them, with the replay's time).
- **Tests** (no case removed): reload_gunshape's and reload_magcollide's Box3D timing sections (`run.sh --exclusive`,
  waiting for every game on the machine: gunshape timed out at 1200 s in the 1.2.0-beta1 suite; numbers only, no
  check) run with `QVR_TEST_TIMINGS=1` only. throw_spin (18 games one after another) and mapflameburn (16) batched,
  undrawn, checked by builtins / one Python at the end; mapgun_pickup in one game (one fixture: a weapon of each kind on
  its own e1m3 item spot, each case reloading the map). reload_test's four screenshot games are two (the sights' and
  the clean blood's in one; the bloody one alone, so no blood reaches the clean hand), its PNGs read in name order (a
  PNG is written by a thread: by time they can come out of order).
- **Times** (s; before: one run; after: median of three (min-max); the machine shared with five workers, its load
  swinging ~5x: a suite's game time is 10-80 s, the rest the shell between runs): mapgun_pickup 295 -> 40 (16-51),
  throw_spin 651 -> 78 (33-91), mapflameburn 377 -> 96 (47-150), reload_gunshape 1200+ timeout -> 93 (76-313),
  reload_magcollide 399 -> 96 (22-127), reload_front 415 -> 102 (94-334), reload_contact 368 -> 177 (73-255),
  reload_eject 502 -> 272 (102-356), reload 1358 -> 621 (539-852).
- **Open**: reload_test is still the longest (its collect pass ~250 s: its own checks' subshells); splitting it into
  parts for the lanes would cut the suite's critical path. reload_worldparts failed once in six runs ("1 screens" at
  the old 320-unit range), reload_test's sights check once before the name-order fix. The kit's run_baseline.py has its
  own copy of the lane rules (qvrtest.lane_keys could replace it).
- **Proof**: map flames igniting at half vr_burn_self_time (QC, reverted): the batched mapflameburn failed 6 of 16.
  The beta profile in 4 lanes: 8.2 min, 9 passed; settings_page failed in lane 1 (a lane's config is put back before
  each game) and is now lane 0 (PASS); two failures not from this branch: update_notice ("same" serves 1.2.0, newer
  than this 1.2.0-beta1: the test's versions need the beta's) and scenario_check (ENGINE CRASH, access violation in
  qvr::visor update, vr_visor.cpp:230, map vrtesthall, 98 s in).

## Ropes (phase 2 of 3: climbing them in VR) (agent/ropes2, 2026-11-22)

Reference `ROPES.md` ("Climbing (VR)"). A grip at a rope takes it with either hand (`vr_climb.cpp` "Holds on ropes":
ropeHold before the ledges, the hold kept as the rope and its place on it, followed each frame); the ledges' hang does
the rest (hand over hand up and down, stamina, reach), no mantle. The climber rides the rope (`vr_climbrope.cpp`

## flatkeys: flat keys in Options > Controls, not a separate page (agent/flatkeys, 2026-11-22)

BACKLOG 3 (his call 2026-11-16, GitHub #83): "Integrate them into Options > Controls' key binding list (a "Quake VR (flat
screen)" group, same rebind/clear UI as the binds, conflicts with binds shown both ways), drop the separate page (or keep
only a link to Controls), and make the keys play nicely with the bind system (a key bound to both a bind and a flat key:
pick one rule and show it). Keep `vr_flat_key_*` working for configs."

- **Controls** (menu.c, keys menu): on the Keyboard & Mouse tab, after the binds, a blank line, the title "Quake VR (flat
  screen)", the rule "In flat play these win over binds", then a row per flat key (`menukeybind_t.flatkey` = 1 + its
  index; its command is the cvar's name). Enter + a key sets the cvar (`VR_FlatKeySet`, the default's spelling kept where
  it is the default's key), Backspace/Del clears it (""), Escape cancels: the binds' own UI and code paths, only the
  store differs. Headers are rows with a description and no command (not selectable, never merged as separators, not
  matched by the search).
- **The rule** (unchanged in the engine, now shown): in flat play a flat key's key does the flat action and its bind does
  not run (`VR_FlatKeyOwned`, keys.c Key_Event); out of flat play (VR, or flat play off) the bind runs. Both rows mark a
  clashing key with "!" after its name (a flat key's: also bound, or another flat key's; a bind's: a flat key's), and the
  cursor row's first clash is spelt out under the list (`M_Keys_Clash`): "! k in flat play: Drop, not Next weapon" (the
  short form without the key name past 40 characters), or "! 3 is also Swap hands" between two flat keys. Nothing is
  unbound automatically (conservative: the player clears the side he does not want; for #83, clear Force Grab/Shove and
  mouse 4/5 do their binds). Defaults already clash where the flat key wins anyway, e.g. Swap hands on 3 (Super Shotgun).
- **One list** (vr_flatmove.cpp): `flatKeyList` + `flatKeyLabels` (static_assert'ed the same length) feed
  `VR_FlatKeyOwned`, Controls (`VR_FlatKeyCount/Label/CvarName/Get/Set/For`, vr_api.h) and `VR_FlatKeysReset`.
- **VR menu**: the Flat Keys page is gone (pageFlatKeys, its 18 QVR_KEY rows, the menu table entry). Locomotion > Desktop
  Screen Play keeps "Flat Keys (Options > Controls)" (`M_Menu_Keys_At("vr_flat_key_lean_left")`: Controls opened, the
  keyboard tab, the cursor on Lean left) and "Reset Flat Keys". The VR menu's key row (Item::Key, M_VRKeyCapture) stays
  for Voice Chat's Push-to-Talk row (vr_menu_voicechat.inc: a VR page where the key belongs; also in the Controls group).
- `menu_keys [row]` (a command, a row's name or a `vr_flat_key_*` cvar) opens Controls on that row; with developer 1 it
  prints `menu_keys: at "<row>" (<command>) <clash note>`. Bug avoided: the row name is copied before M_Menu_Keys_f, whose
  bindlist.lst parsing re-tokenizes over Cmd_Argv.
- Gamepad tab: no flat group (flat play's keys are keyboard and mouse keys; decision, conservative).
- Test: `Misc/quakevr/flatkeybind_test.sh <agent>` (rewritten for Controls; flat-screen, fast mode, ends on
  "flatkeybind: done"): 9 passed, 0 failed (link, rebind, Escape, clash both ways, the new key fires (k drops) and the
  old does nothing, clear, reset).

## Quest C5h: why the body's Quake way was slower (its own program), fixed and on; D24 depth; the per-part table (questc5h, 2026-11-22; branch agent/quest)

- **Why vr_gl_alias_body 2 was slower** (posed head, 0.7, interleaved, gpu_span ms; levels 3 unless said). Not a CPU
  stall: the period's 50 ms is all in xrWaitFrame (41.9 ms), the runtime pacing the app down once the GPU crosses ~12 ms
  (the busy CPU only rises in that state; single-pass stereo is off on the Quest, so no multiview fallback). Two GPU costs:
  | probe (pitch 70) | per pixel (skin form) | body form (C5f) |
  |---|---|---|
  | models' fragments a constant (ALIASCONST) | 4.79 | 6.97 (old: ambient at the vertices) / 5.38 (ambient per pixel) |
  | 0.5 scale, same light data (vr_dlight_models 0) | 5.37 | 8.70 |
  | 0.5 scale, same code (QVR_APLAIN_NODLIGHTS) | 4.78 | 8.50 |
  The vertex ambient cost ~2 ms on the vertex side (gone with it per pixel), and the body's own program
  (glprogs.alias_body) ran the *same* code ~3.3 ms slower than the skin form running it, whatever the light data:
  something of the driver's for that program object (not found; the fix does without it).
- **The fix**: vr_gl_alias_body 2 draws your body by the form it takes anyway, with the light loop skipped for its batch
  (`BatchDlightsFlat`, the instance buffer's padding after EyePos; r_alias.c sets it when every instance of the batch is
  flat-lit), its lights added flat on the CPU as before. C5f's VFLAT form and its lite bit 29 are gone; the body form is
  vr_gl_alias_body 1's alone. Same picture as C5f's (PC -glescompat, the flashlight on: mean 5.03 at pitch 70, 2.09 at 35
  vs per pixel; C5f's 5.02 / 2.09).
  | 0.7, 3 rounds | off | per pixel | Quake's way | vertex (1) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | pitch 70 | 6.19 | 11.65 | **10.63** | 13.71 (period 50) |
  | pitch 35 | 5.74 | 8.71 | **7.98** | 10.96 |
  | frozen fight, 3 big lights, 0.55 (world in the texture / + body) | | | 6.90 / 7.02 | |
  The body's cost above off: 5.46 -> 4.44 ms at 70, 2.97 -> 2.24 at 35. **The Quest preset sets vr_gl_quake_dlights 1**
  (the world's light texture and the body's flat add, one choice).
- **The per-part table** (pitch 70, 0.7, 2 rounds; vr_gles_define probes act on every model): off 5.99, full 11.31,
  const 5.43, tex 6.12, look 5.69, light-end 9.93, rim-end 9.98, no dlights 8.07, no ambient 9.83, no skin 10.60, no
  wounds/dents 10.55, no fog 10.51, mediump 10.83, no specular AA 10.43, no fullbright 10.26. The light loop (-3.2 with
  every model's off) is the one big part; the rest are 0.3-1.0 each.
- **vr_depth_float 0** (D24S8; the eyes' targets are made again when it changes, so interleaved in one session, 4 rounds,
  no launch noise): pitch 0 5.30 -> 4.93, pitch 35 8.93 -> 7.74. Same picture on the PC (pairs within the flicker).
  **The Quest preset sets vr_depth_float 0** (near plane 1 unit; held items never cut).
- **Resolution** (levels 0): the frozen fight at 0.55 / 0.65 / 0.75: 7.02 / 7.99 / 11.30 ms (period held to 0.65);
  the posed head at pitch 35 at the base 0.9 / 1.0: 11.23 (period 35) / 12.83 (period 55), float depth. No room for a
  higher base; the floor could go to 0.65 in fights, but `questMusts` caps vr_dynres_min at 0.55 (C4o's live fights):
  left at 0.55, his call (a live fight at 0.65 first).
- **Quest eyeshots of the dlmap pairs**: setpos doesn't move the posed VR player on the Quest, so the e1m1 scenes came
  out at the spawn without their lights; only e1m2's torch wall is valid: means 28 / 26 (dlmap 1 two levels darker, as
  the PC's pair). Needs a scene-based placement (vr_scenario) next time.
- Checks: PC Dev 0 warnings, APK 0 warnings, check_apk 20/20, scenario_check (below).

## disarmfix: the player disarmed by enemies, by jolts (agent/disarmfix, 2026-11-22)

BACKLOG 6: "Player disarm: make it consistent, then on for PvE ... Very inconsistent: hard to predict whether a shot or
blow knocks your gun out; some enemy melee never disarms; enemies punching (fists) never disarm you. Needs tuning and
fixes (QC/vr_playerdisarm.qc: which blows count, the rolls, feedback before the drop)."

- Why it was inconsistent (the old PvE rule, kept for PvP): shots added up to 16 damage in 0.5 s, then rolled 25%+;
  a blow counted only with a line, landing on your weapon, with at least `vr_agrunt_disarm_damage` 10: a knight's sword
  (9 at most), an ogre's chainsaw (12 at most) almost never; fists, bites, claws never (no line: the guard's path).
- PvE now (QC `vr_playerdisarm.qc`, "PvE's own rule"; PvP untouched, as the brief said): no dice. Hits give jolts on a
  hand; `vr_player_disarm_jolts` 2 within `vr_player_disarm_window` 3 s (from the last) knock its weapon out, each one
  short warns (`VR_PD_Warn`: `handimpact` 4, a buzz, `weapons/tink1.wav` at `vr_player_disarm_sound`, "Your grip on
  your weapon loosens!"). The table:

  | Hit (landed: not parried, not on crossed arms) | Jolts |
  |---|---|
  | blow with a line (sword, axe, chainsaw, armed humanoid's swing) on your weapon or its hand, any damage | 1; heavy (`vr_player_disarm_heavy` 15+) 2 |
  | armed humanoid's fist, butt or shove on your body | 1 (the held weapon's hand nearest it) |
  | any other blow on your body | 1 if heavy, else none (bites, light claws, a blade on the body) |
  | shots and projectiles on your weapon or hand | each `vr_player_disarm_shot` 12 damage summed over 0.5 s: 1 (full grunt blast 24: 2, out; laser 15: 1; nail 9: none, two: 1; ogre grenade: out) |

  `vr_player_disarm_chance` is the knock-out's chance once the jolts are reached (1: certain; a lost roll leaves it one
  short). Projectiles count in full within `vr_agrunt_shotdisarm_proj_near` (4 units: a bolt has a size; at half they
  never reached a jolt). Blows are read where the parry resolves them (combat.qc `VR_Parry` now hands every landed blow to
  `VR_PD_Blow` with its line flag), so with `vr_parry` 0 only shots disarm. Settings: Armed Grunts > "Disarming: Your
  Weapon" (Jolts, Jolt Kept, Heavy Blow, Shot Damage).
- `vr_player_disarm` stays 0 (his OK needed to flip it). Tests: `vr_pd_test 3` (new, Debug > Tests > "Player Disarm: The
  Rules, Blow by Blow") 10/0, every rule once; `vr_pd_test 1` 13/0 (a full blast: out at once; a laser warns, a second
  out). `vr_pd_test 2` times out in case 0 (the gun-and-axe grunt backs off to ~200 units and shoots after its first
  blow) on this branch and on origin/next's QC alike: pre-existing, not chased. Scene `pd_jolts`.

  shortest. grappleStep (players, SP and each remote move) calls it; QC's prop, monster and loose-hook reels call the new

  `QVR_NET_VERSION` 44); his replay runs `moveguard::budget` (roomscale's rule, now shared) on a copy from it, so a walk

  showed both sides' cut speeds and budgets equal move for move; the runs that failed before A stepped aside were B's walk

- **mp_guard "A's honest moves: rewinds N held"** (a load flake: 0 of 6 idle, 3-4 of 4 with `--load 30`): the server held
  an honest client's view time when his move's `time` (his newest message) was older than 2 x rtt + 0.5 s at the moment
  the move *ran*. The new `mp_guard_held: ... rewind` lines (vr_mp_guard_debug) showed two causes, both from frame
  hitches under load: (a) a client hitch of 0.5-0.9 s, after which his frame's catch-up ticks send a burst of moves all
  naming his newest message from before it; (b) the server's move buffer then ran them one a tick, adding its own wait
  (e.g. time 36.644 run at 37.172-37.256, one tick apart). Now the age is judged at the move's first read
  (`netmove::serverCame`: each kept move's arrival) less a quiet allowance: the silence before its packet (from the
  slot's reset at its connection or map), spent as the server's time goes on (`quiet = max(gap, quiet - gap)` a packet).
  A liar gains only as much as he stays silent, and lag compensation stays capped by `vr_net_lagcomp_most`; the cheat's
  view a second back and newest message two back are still held (B's counts unchanged). The lockstep's moves are judged
  as they run, as before (the same every run).
- **mp_predict "at rest B stands where the server has him" 1.4-1.9 off**: the test's wait was counted from a planned
  state number; when the legs' polls had overshot it (load), the read came at once, B's own copy stopped and the
  server's still sliding to his stop a round trip behind. `rest_gap` (mp_test.py) now reads the server's copy until it
  stands still over 36 of B's states counted from then (at most 5 reads), then B's; it notes the old immediate gap too:
  at `--load 26` it was 9.90 and 0.20 units in 2 of 5 runs (both pass settled), 0.00-0.10 at `--load 12`. Used on the
  walk's and the lift's rest checks.
- **The lift landing** (ROUND25 "lift landing 1.354"): the bound is a unit when the server's buffer ran every tick one
  move during the segment, else a lift step; the ticks were counted from after B's prediction snapped over the lift, so
  a bunched tick between his put-over and that read (1 run of 10 had one) was missed and the strict bound applied. Now
  counted from before the put-over (`b_predict_lift_buffer_off_early` metric). Not reproduced in 20 runs (contact 0.000
  every run).
- Not player-facing beyond MULTIPLAYER.md's line on a stalled player (no PATCH_NOTES line). Seen only under extreme
  load (`--load 26-30` on 32 CPUs, games at normal priority): mp_predict's state-count checks (swam 144-149 of 150,
  flat ground 11-20 of 50, own move 5-16 moves) and mp_guard's B6 segment (11-19 of 20 compared), and joins timing
  out; not chased (the counts are of states that come slower under such load).
- Checks: mp_guard 10/10 and mp_predict 10/10 at `--load 12` (bases/mp; no honest rewind held, every settled rest gap
  0.00). The plain suite in 3 slices in order (10, 17, 15 min; each with mp_netsafe): 67 of 68 passed; mp_ground's

## ropes4: another player's rope-climbing pose in MP (agent/ropes4, 2026-11-22)

ROPES.md "Multiplayer", "Tests", "Known limits".
- Cause: another player's head and hands come from his client's origin, which on a rope (the server moves him with it)
  isn't where the server has him, and his holds were sent from that origin too: his drawn hands read 15-60 units off
  the server's holds, his body and feet off the rope with them; his trunk also hung behind the hands as off a ledge.
- Server: the holds go from his entity's origin as sent (`vr_server.cpp`, writeHolds' origin): every client draws him
  there. Client: holding a rope, his copy is moved by his held palms' mean way to the server's holds (`vr_mpavatar.cpp`
  ropeShift, 48 units at most, eased 0.15 s), each held hand then pinned on its hold (ropePinHands; a new hold eased to).
- Shared with your own body: a hand on a rope has its palm's middle 2.5 cm this side of it (`climb::ropeHandOffset`,
  `climb::ropeHold`), not the ledge offsets `vr_climb_hand_*` (which put it beside the rope); the trunk turns about the
  neck so the hips come in to 12 cm from the rope (`vr_avatar_climb.cpp` ropeHips, folded into solveTorso's turn, at
  most 45 degrees), yours and his. The rope-nearness tolerances went from 6 to 12 units (at a full swing the latest hold
  is a frame off the rope as drawn).
- `mp_test.py ropeclimb` waits for A hanging still before its first check and is in the MP suite: 3 runs 11/11
  (hanging wrists 1.6-3.3, ankles 1.8-7.8; swinging 10.5-12.5, 6.4-14.1). rope_climb_test.sh 8+6+6, rope_flat_test.sh,
  mp_test.py ropes 9/9 still pass.

## visorcrash: the headset's centre popup read a freed view leaf while a map loaded (agent/visorcrash, 2026-11-22)

- **Seen:** scenario_check (testspeed's run), an access violation at vr_visor.cpp:230 (`eyeUnderwater`, inlined in
  `update()`), vrtesthall ~98 s in; stack: CL_ParseServerMessage > Con_Printf > SCR_UpdateScreen > VR_End2D >
  `visor::renderHeadsetCenter` (vrcenterprint2).
- **Why:** vrcenterprint2 made the headset's centre popup step the visor's `update()` from VR_End2D, every VR frame
  (`centerPanelOn` is just `vr_center_panel` and VR). During a map load a console print redraws the screen, so that ran
  after Host_ClearMemory had freed the old world (the hunk's blocks are heap blocks since nohunk: freed memory can be
  decommitted) and before R_NewMap cleared `r_viewleaf`: `r_viewleaf->contents` read the old world's leaf. The flat
  visor's `update()` only ran from R_RenderView (a signed-on view), so it never saw this.
- **Fix:** Host_ClearMemory clears `r_viewleaf` with the world it pointed into (as R_NewMap does later; also guards
  vr_lighting.cpp's PVS read); `eyeUnderwater` reads the leaf only with a world signed on (`cls.signon == SIGNONS`).
  `vr_center_panel_info` now also prints "loading updates N, stale view leafs M" (updates with no world signed on; of
  those, r_viewleaf set but not a leaf of `cl.worldmodel`: a pointer compare, never a read).
- **Test** `Misc/quakevr/visorload_test.sh <agent>` (VR mock, -loopbackonly): vrtesthall, reloaded, e1m1, vrtesthall,
  then the counts: loading updates > 0 (the path ran: 12) and stale leafs 0. 2 passed, 0 failed (3 runs); with the
  Host_ClearMemory line disabled: stale view leafs 2 (each would have been the crash's read when the block was gone).
- **update_notice_test:** its "same" feed now serves VERSION whole (1.2.0-beta1, not 1.2.0: a beta's final is newer,
  semver), and it checks `vr_update_compare`'s prerelease order (1.2.0-beta1 > 1.1.0, < 1.2.0, < 1.2.0-beta2). The
  game's logic was already right (vr_update.cpp `comparePre`: a 1.1.0 feed gives a beta no notice, 1.2.0 does): all passed.

## ropes5: flat rope/chain polish from his test session (agent/ropes5, 2026-11-22)

ROPES.md "Tests", "Known limits". His words: chains work well, minor adjustments.
- **Jitter (2), cause:** the client's drawn rope (`shownOf`) was cached a host frame, and the frame's first ask came
  before the client's time moved (the server's tick), so a client faster than the server (144 Hz here) drew the rope a
  tick at a time; and the hands were pinned to the server's holds (a tick old, stepped each tick) while the body is
  interpolated. Now the rope is made again whenever cl.time moves, and a hand on a rope goes on the rope as drawn
  (`climb::ropePalm`, `climbrope::clientRopeNearest`: the drawn curve's point as far from the top as the hold).
- **Off the chain (3):** the holds were 2-8 units from the drawn rope (a tick ahead, and the rope below the hands bent
  off the rider's line by his body); the same snap fixes it; the palm sits 0.4 of the thickness out (a thick chain: a
  little in). Another player's hands too (vr_mpavatar ropePalmTarget).
- **Grip (1):** `vr_rope_hand_grip` 1 (flat play): the rope through the fist, the knuckles away from the body (vr_climb.cpp
  ropeTurn, turnOn); 2 VR too; 0 the ledge's turn (`vr_climb_hand_pitch` 60 pointed the knuckles up). VR unchanged.
- **Paused (5):** single player's menu/console kept stepping the ropes (only `pause` was checked); Host_ServerFrame now
  passes whether SV_Physics ran (`VR_ServerFrameEnd(worldran)`), the ropes' step skips (new ropes still made). F8 is
  `vr_clip` here, not pause. Other VR_ServerFrameEnd steps still run paused (not checked).
- **Sounds for chains (4): not done** (budget).
- Tests: rope_hands_test.sh 6/0 (hanging jitter max 0.27-0.54, off 0.47-0.49, were 4.8 off; swinging means 0.06 and 0.2,
  were 1.9 and 5.5), rope_pause_test.sh 4/0 (menu moved 267 units before, 0.000 now), rope_flat_test.sh 6/0,

## mpbothands: floating fists and holsters on MP bots (branch agent/mpbothands, 2026-11-22)

- His report: in the MP scenes every bot carried an extra pair of fists, an open hand, a gun and a shovel beside its
  body. Cause: a bot's holsters come from its QC fields (vr_server.cpp `botHolstered`), and the QC names the fists'
  model (`progs/hand.mdl`, WID_FIST) for an empty holster; every client drew it as a holstered weapon
  (view::drawHands), so the four empty holsters (shoulders, uppers) each showed a hand. A human's client never sends
  one (view::netHolsters drops hand models), so only bots were hit; not the ropes4 or onemodel changes.
- Fix (shared by every copy, flat or VR viewer, bots and players): view::drawHands draws nothing for a holster whose
  model is a hand's (`isHandModel`, as your own holsters). Also a bot's holstered weapon now takes its own Holstered
  pose (weapons::holsteredPose, poseHolstered in the holster's frame) as yours does: view::holsterOnOther takes the
  weapon. The Hotspots page's turns stay yours alone (not put on others).
- `vr_mp_gearcheck [ent]` (Debug > Reports > Network: Other Players' Gear): per other copy its hand models (two
  expected), holstered weapons, sheaths, the farthest of them from its trunk (pelvis to neck; at most 0.5 m) and its
  hands from its arms' wrists (at most 0.15 m); `mp_gearcheck: N players, M bad`. In mp_dm_passive before the fix:
  `hands=6 ... ok=0`; after: `hands=2 holsters=2 sheaths=4 trunk=9.0 (most 15.7) wrist=2.7 (most 4.7) ok=1`.
- `mp_test.py botgear` (in the suite): dedicated DM, the VR A and the flat B; B held in front of A (vr_dm_test 16),
  A checks B and B checks A; then a bot held there, A checks it. 10 passed.

## vrnotes1122a: MP bots from his DM voice notes (agent/vrnotes1122a, 2026-11-22)

His notes dm3_2026-11-22_16-15-02, 16-17-59, 16-18-21.
- **Revolver bot never shoots:** bot logic, not the revolver. A bot never reloads (VRIsWeaponReloadingEnabledFor: humans
  only), so its guns fire from its ammo, never a clip; bot_can_fire counted the held gun's clip. A revolver it took
  loaded (his, by a disarm: "Hal takes your weapon!" 3 s before 16-15-02) with no shells of its own was picked, then
  clicked or was dropped for the axe. Fix: `bot_clips_to_ammo` (frikbot/bot_fight.qc, each AI frame from bot_ai.qc): a
  gun in its hands puts its clip's rounds with its ammo; bot_can_fire counts the ammo only. `vr_dm_test 14` now counts
  slugs (shells spent), not trigger pulls (attack_finished also moves on a dry cock): its own revolver 3 slugs; a taken
  loaded revolver in its main hand, no shells: 0 slugs in 10 s before, 3 in 4.2 s after; in its off hand beside its
  shotgun: 3. New `mp_test.py botrevolver` (in the suite): dedicated DM, A adds a bot, the server runs test 14: 5/0.
- **Bot holsters' orientation:** solveBotGear put the hips beside the hip joints facing straight out, the very side the
  holster frame takes as its outwards: holsterFrame normalised a zero vector, so the hip guns' frames were NaN (drawn
  anywhere). Now (vr_mpavatar.cpp): the trunk's yaw from the drawn shoulders (`trunkYaw`), the hips and uppers on the
  front of its belly and chest rings (round 45 and 35 degrees) facing the ring's surface there
  (`body::frontRingPlate`, sharing `ringPlate` with your own plateOnTheRing), the frame as yours (plate out and up;
  shoulders down the back), and the standing holster turns yours take (`holsterTurnStanding`: tuning constants, not a
  player's settings). `view::holsterOnOther` takes the plate's up.
- **vr_mp_gearcheck** adds per copy: `finite` (every piece's place and angles), `tilt` (worst sheath up vs the trunk's,
  at most 70), `facing` (worst sheath out vs straight out of the trunk, at most 60), `hang` (gun to its sheath, at most
  0.25 m), `turned`; ok needs them. `mp_test.py botgear` checks them for each copy and that the bot's tilt and facing
  are within 20 degrees of player B's (whose client drew his own): bot 63.6 / 41.0, B 50.0 / 27.9; 14/0.
  `MP_BOTGEAR_SHOTS=1` saves A's view of the bot (low-res here: his game was running).
- **Dropped weapons in DM:** `VR_WPN_DM_LIFETIME` 20 s (vr_wpnholster.qc; was 10, doubled as asked; a backpack lies
  120 and vr_dmloose.qc's cap holds their number). Every thrown or dropped weapon in deathmatch (players' too).
  vr_dm_test 1: 22/0.
- **Not done (budget): the dead body's look synced to the live player** (plates gained after his respawn). Cause:
  vr_mpavatar.cpp setupBody reads `agarmor::clientState(e)` with e the owner for a doll slot too. Planned fix: QC
  VR_DeathDoll_Make copies `.vr_pp_type/.vr_pp_mask` to the body; vr_agarmor.cpp stateOf serves those fields for a

## vrnotes1122b: revolver flicks, Haste on every gun (agent/vrnotes1122b, 2026-11-22)

- **The flick down with a shell held** (dm3_2026-11-22_16-14-25): the eject push (`VR_Revolver_ReloadFrame`) waited
  `vr_revolver_spin_hold` after `rvh_held_at`, which `VR_Revolver_OtherHand` refreshes every frame the other hand holds
  anything: with a shell ready in the off hand no push ever counted. It now waits on `rvh_loaded_at` (a shell just went
  in) only; the spin keeps `rvh_held_at`.
- **Wrist flick against arm swing** (vrfiringrange_2026-11-22_16-11-57): the old guard refused a flick open with the
  hand at 2 m/s or faster (`vr_revolver_open_swing_speed`, retired). His replay shows why it refused everything: his
  flicks roll 150-360 degrees at 2000-3500 deg/s and the controller, 5-15 cm off the wrist's axis, moves 3.5-5.6 m/s
  from that turn alone. `VR_Revolver_Flick` now keeps two fading sums over `vr_revolver_flick_motion_time` (0.2 s): the
  wrist's (its roll in radians x `vr_revolver_flick_wrist_lever`, 0.1 m) and the arm's (the hand's speed less its turn
  rate x the lever, i.e. travel the turn doesn't explain). A flick open is refused when the arm's share is over
  `vr_revolver_open_flick_arm_share` (0.45; menu: Weapons > Reloading > Heavy Revolver > Flick Open Arm Share; 1 no
  guard), then for `vr_revolver_open_swing_hold` (0.35 s), and after a landed blow as before. The flick home is never
  refused. Offline on his two revolver replays (the trigger simulated at the flick's thresholds): his flicks 0.03-0.31,
  his swings (hand 8-10 m/s, 1-1.7 m travel) 0.53-0.75. `vr_reload_debug 1` prints the share on each open and refusal.
- **Haste on every gun** (vrtesthall_2026-11-22_15-59-17): Haste (Dwell's; Dissolution's Hell Magic rune alike) works
  through `RuneApplyHell` on a weapon's next attack time; the frame-driven guns (nailguns, lava nailguns, lightning gun,
  laser cannon) fire once per 0.1 s animation frame and never asked it. `VR_Haste_FramePace` (rogue_runes.qc) paces
  those frames by it (0.06 s hasted), their attack times too; the Mjolnir swing, the proximity gun, AD's plasma gun and
  the lightning gun's first bolt now pass through it as well. Dry clicks stay unhasted.
- **Full auto under Haste** (15-59-37): `vr_haste_full_auto` (1; Combat > Weapon Damage > Guns) lets the nail pistol,
  the heavy revolver and the flare gun skip their re-arm (`VR_Haste_FullAuto`) while hasted: they fire again while the
  trigger is held, each at its cooldown x Haste's 0.6 (the nail pistol 0.072 s, the revolver 0.18 s). Empty or spent,
  still one click a pull.
- Tests: `vr_np_test 7` (nphaste, Debug > Tests > Nail Pistol): 12/0 (nailgun 15 -> 24 shots in 1.5 s, lightning 16 ->
  25, shotgun 3 -> 5; nail pistol 1 -> 12, revolver 1 -> 6, flare gun 1 -> 2). `vr_rv_test 1` 49/0 (step 12 now a 7 m/s
  swing rolling the wrist: refused, arm share 0.78; then a still-hand wrist flick: out, share 0.18; step 13 pushes the
  shells out with the other hand holding). Its tests need `developer 1` (dprint). Scenario `haste_guns`. nptest 39/0,
  flaretest 22/0. His replays played in the game (`vr_motion_play <notes>/<take>_replay.csv`, `vr_reload_debug 1`):
  vrfiringrange_16-11-57 5 flicks open (arm share 0.06-0.43), 7 swings refused (0.50-0.73); e1m1_2026-11-21_01-03-41
  7 open (0.06-0.26), 7 refused (0.54-0.80). (The replays live in his notes folder, not the repo: no committed test.)
- Note: `VR_RVT_Flicks` sets `vr_revolver_flick_hand_weight` / `_cap` with `cvar_set`, but they are tunables
  ("Cvar_Set: variable not found"): its force check runs at the defaults (150, 1), which it expects anyway.

  is a vertical trace at its goal, so it ends touching it) and its step physics' fall trace touched the wall each frame
  it could: 8 to 29 hurting touches in 20 s. Now a togglewall with `dmg` (AD's and Hipnotic's) sets
  `.vr_monster_avoid`; `SV_movestep` refuses a monster's step that ends nearer than 12 units to such a solid entity
  unless the step keeps it as far or takes it farther (`VR_MonsterAvoidsField`, vr_hull.cpp: an area query, both
  walking and flying branches), so the chase picks another way and one already near is never stuck. A trigger_hurt is
  left as it is (maps use them on monsters). Test: `quothfield_test.sh` (vr_ad_test 223, kellbase1): the field's
  emitter made (colour 47, 50 sparks), its sparks sent with you near, and an armed enforcer chasing you from behind it
  for 20 s touches it 0 times (29 before): 4 passed.

  bars: 24 apart on the catwalk's, 32 on the pillars'), so the volume's own rungs (16 apart down from its top) never
  matched them. `ladderHold`'s volume fallback now asks `drawnRung` (vr_climb.cpp) first: the up-facing faces of
  every brush submodel with no solid or trigger entity (an illusionary edict, or a static one) over the volume's
  footprint (12 units before and behind it, across its thinner side, so not its rails' caps), their exact vertex
  bounds; the bar nearest the hand is the rung, the hold on its ridge (its top faces' vertices at the top) across and
  where the hand is along it. A ladder with no drawn rungs keeps the 16-unit rungs, and so does flatscreen play's
  ladder (`findRungs` sets `flatRungSearch`): its window over the feet is about 31 units, so bars 24 or 32 apart left
  it one rung and it never mounted (flatladder 0 of 3 with drawn rungs, 3 of 3 now). Flat hands therefore still close

  modladder_test.sh's VR-hands expectations moved to the bars (hold y -664, tops 704 + 24 k; the pillars' ridge y
  -1354, tops 508 + 32 k): 10 passed.

## buildaudit: build-speed audit; process starts are the cost (agent/buildaudit, 2026-11-22)

Full write-up: `BUILD_SPEED.md` (measurements, top TUs and headers, what landed, what's proposed).
- **Finding**: on this PC a process start costs 0.1-2.7 s and starts are mostly serialised (16 `where.exe` starts in
  a row: 17-19 s), so a build's fixed cost was mostly processes: a no-op build.sh took 23-28 s (~20 small processes in
  the script, fteqcc recompiling unchanged QC, the version step's 4 cmd.exe + 4 git). A full rebuild: 350 s wall for
  327 CPU-s of compiling (875 clang-cl starts).
- **Landed** (`quakevr.props`, `ironwail.vcxproj`): `QvrBuildVersion` in one Exec (one cmd.exe, three gits; same
  header text); the run-time DLLs by MSBuild's Copy (only changed ones, no cmd.exe); `/p:QvrSkipQcCompile=1`.
- **Proposed kit patch** `qvr-kit/scratch/buildaudit_kit.patch` (build.sh, qc_hash.py): skip the QC compile when its
  inputs' hash matches the last clean compile; bash builtins instead of small processes. With it: no-op 23-28 -> 5.5-9 s,
  a .cpp touch 33-38 -> 6-11 s, a QC edit 36 -> 12 s, vr_hands.hpp 166 -> 98 s (noisy, shared machine).
- No source includes or std:: touched (the zancle worker's area): the heaviest headers are listed for it in BUILD_SPEED.md.

## flatnumkeys: flat-screen number keys for hands and holsters (agent/flatnumkeys, 2026-11-22)

His request 2026-11-22. FLATPLAY.md's keys table. Holsters on (`vr_flat_holsters 1`, the default) only.
- **Keys** (flat keys: Options > Controls' "Quake VR (flat screen)" group after Drop, rebindable, Reset Flat Keys, the
  "!" clash): `vr_flat_key_cycle_left` 1, `_cycle_right` 2, `_holster_left` 4, `_holster_right` 5, `_drop_left` 6,
  `_drop_right` 7; 3 stays the swap. "Left"/"right" are the holster menu's (the off hand, the main hand). Before: with
  the holsters on 1, 2, 4-7 did nothing (owned, impulses swallowed); off, they were Quake's binds (1/2 the flat hand
  cycle, 4-7 weapon picks). No flat key default moved. `flatplay::keyActive` keeps the six off (not owned, not read) with
  `vr_flat_holsters 0`, so the old number keys work there unchanged.
- **One path with the menu and VR.** `pollHandKeys` (vr_flatplay.cpp) sends impulses: 86/87 cycle, 88/89 holster
  (QC `VR_FlatHolster_Cycle`, `VR_FlatHolster_Put`, vr_flatholster.qc), 78/79 the menu's own DROPs. The moves are the
  headset's steps (`VRDrawHolsterWeapon`, `VRPutWeaponInHolster`, `VRHolsterHandWeapon`, `VRHolsterRefused`), so MP
  clients send the same impulse and the holster stats/models carry it to everyone.
- **Cycle order**: holster slots 0..5 (the menu's: L/R shoulder, L/R hip, L/R chest) after the one the hand's weapon was
  drawn from (`.vr_flatcyc_slot0/1`, valid while the hand still holds that weapon's record `.vr_flatcyc_inst0/1`); the
  old weapon goes back to its own holster, else the first free (`VR_FlatHolster_FreeFor`: the hand's side's hip, chest,
  shoulder, then the other side's; the vacated one counts, so with all full it is a trade); after the last, the empty
  hand. A holstered weapon is never in the other hand, so "skip the other hand's" is automatic. Too big (AD's
  hammer/mace/flail...): refused with the headset's line; no free holster: "No free holster for the X."; a carried
  prop: "That hand carries something: drop it first." 2H: no forced emptying (VR forces none); the empty other hand
  leaves and retakes the grip on its own (flat's pinToGrip).
- **Tests**: `vr_flatswap_test 6` (Debug > Tests > "Flat Holster Number Keys") 22/0: 16 key steps and the rocket
  launcher's grip; flatkeybind_test.sh gained 3 numkeys checks.
## zancle: std:: to Zancle, includes trimmed (agent/zancle, 2026-11-22)

His standing rule restated: our C++ uses Zancle wherever it has an equivalent and includes only what it uses.

- **The mapping:** `docs/vr-port/ZANCLE.md` (std -> Zancle, its header, the traps: exact-type math templates, integer
  `abs`, `min`/`max` types, `remainder` vs fmod, sort stability, atomic orders; the no-equivalent list: allocator hooks'
  `std::align_val_t`/`nothrow_t`, `std::filesystem` behind `qvr::files`, `std::source_location` in the jobs, the
  ordered map in vr_motion_review, `vr_zancle_diag.cpp`'s std comparison, third-party interfaces). Zancle's swap is
  `za::genericSwap`.
- **The check:** `qvr_checks std_uses` (Tools/qvr_checks/std_uses.cpp, in `all`, so every build): counts `std::<name>`
  in the code (comments and strings ignored) and every C++ standard header include except the C ones Zancle has
  nothing for (cstdio, cstdarg, cstdlib, ctime, cctype, ...), per file in Quake/vr (not external/), against
  `Misc/quakevr/std_uses_allowlist.txt` (`<file> <name> <max>  # why`; `*` for a whole file). Over a cap fails.
  `python Misc/quakevr/std_uses_allowlist.py` rewrites the caps from `qvr_checks std_uses --list`, keeping each why.
- **Phases:** 1 (42 files a..h: AD, box3d, flat play, hit reactions, holster zones), 2 (36 files h..v: humans, impacts,
  menu, monster groups, net ragdolls and snapshots, active ragdolls, temporal, view, visor). Mechanical: C string calls
  -> `ZA_STRCMP`..., math -> `za::` templates, traits -> `ZA_IS_...`, int types -> `za::U32`..., `std::array` ->
  `za::Array`, `std::span` -> `za::Span`, `std::size` -> `za::getArraySize`, sorts -> `za::quickSort`/`stableSort`,
  `lower_bound` -> `za::lowerBound`; C stdio/stdlib (`sscanf`, `snprintf`, `atof`, `atoi`, `strchr`) lose the `std::`
  (no Zancle equivalent); `<cmath>`, `<cstring>`, `<cstdint>`, `<algorithm>`, `<type_traits>`, `<utility>`,
  `<array>`, `<span>`, `<initializer_list>` dropped where nothing std-qualified is left (unqualified C calls come from
  quakedef.h's C headers). Every converted call compiled against the exact-type templates (no mixed promotions
  found). One ordering change: vr_admelee.cpp's normal welding sorts equal vertices by index (a total order, so each
  run's normals sum in one fixed order; std::sort left ties in an unspecified one). Sorts on unique keys (cvar names,
  snapshot record keys) are unchanged; vr_netsnap's per-class byte table (a diagnostic print) may order ties
  differently.
- **Counts:** std:: uses in code 441 -> 208, standard header includes 90 -> 29 (`qvr_checks std_uses --list`).
- **Left (phase 3):** the atomics (`std::atomic` -> `za::Atomic`: no operators, so every `++`/`+=`/implicit load in the
  hull/box3d/disk caches' stats, imgprefetch, warmup, startlog, xr_runtime, jobs needs its explicit order:
  `std::atomic`'s operators are seq_cst), `std::chrono` in vr_mptest/vr_voicechat (-> `za::Clock`), vr_tracy.cpp
  (mutex, deque, unordered_map, strings: -> `za::AtomicMutex`, ankerl, `za::String`), and the kept list above. Not in
  scope and noted: ~2,600 unqualified C string calls (`strcmp`, `memcpy`, ...) could become the `ZA_` builtins too.
- **Tests:** release build 0 warnings each phase; phase 1: smoke e1m1, flat_gate_aim 6/0, hitreact_test exit 0,
  struggle_test 6/6 (armdrag, shoulderdrag drag: vr_box3d_struggle.cpp's only change was std::str* -> the same
  builtins, so not this branch's; not chased); phase 2: smoke e1m1, mp_test ragsync 11/0, active_test no fail,
  NaN or crash line.

testaudit #3 and #7 (kit `F:\QVR-Parked\2026-11-22\testspeed\kit\testaudit_report.md`); TESTING.md "Batching a suite,
-QuitOn and -NoDraw".

- **-QuitOn in a batch** (it made every such run a game of its own, and the flat suites and the agrunt cases all use it):
  `vr_test_quiton "<regex>"` (engine, vr_testbatch.cpp: a small backtracking regex, .NET's subset the tests use,
  case-insensitive; else plain text) armed at the case's start, the case's closing `waitN` -> `vr_waitquiton N`, which
  holds the commands after it aside (Cbuf_PendingText/Cbuf_DropPending, cmd.c) and puts them back at the server tick
  after the match (VR_TestTick, host.c). A first version looped like `wait`: what QC queued meanwhile (localcmd) sat
  behind the batch, and flatitems' cases (scripts with no closing wait) all timed out. `-Low` and `-NoDraw` batch too.
  `Misc/quakevr/testbatch/selftest.sh`: 5/5. `TB_COLLECT_STUBS=2` also stubs awk and cat in the collect pass.
- **The clock:** runs alone play fast mode at `vr_fixed_frames_rate` 72; the batches' default is still 250. The
  converted suites set `TB_RATE=72` (at 250 flatitems' QC tests timed out too). flatplay plays a game a case
  (`TB_ISOLATE=1`): its pose case's `tune vr_flat_gun_near 999` read 24 (not the 60 clamp) after an earlier case's
  `tune_reset` in the same game: open (a tunables reset/restore interaction).

## zancle2: atomics, clocks, Tracy and the C string calls on Zancle (agent/zancle2, 2026-11-22)

- **struggle_test's failures predate zancle:** before the zancle merge (0ea5f3574) 7 passed / 7 failed, the same drag
  cases (legpull, legpull1, headdrag, shoulderdrag "walked 6 units", armdrag's swat > 0.4, legpull's no weights;
  legdrag also counted that run); origin/next 6/6. Not chased here.
- **Phase 3:** `std::atomic` -> `za::Atomic` (box3d gun pieces and hull disk counts, diskcache, imgprefetch, jobs,
  warmup, startlog, xr_runtime, bodytrack_xr): every implicit operation (`++`, `+=`, `x = v`, `.load()`,
  `.exchange()`, `compare_exchange_strong`) is now its explicit SeqCst call, as std's operators were; explicit
  orders map 1:1 (`fetchAddRelaxed`, `storeRelease`, `za::atomicThreadFence<...>`). vr_voicechat's steady_clock
  timings -> `za::Clock::nowNanoseconds()`. vr_tracy.cpp (compiled only by Release-Tracy; checked with an MSBuild
  ClCompile of that configuration into scratch): Atomic (the source table's spin lock an exchange/store),
  `za::AtomicMutex`/`LockGuard`, ankerl maps, `za::String`/`StringView`/`Vector`, ZA_ string calls; its two
  `std::deque`s stay (stable addresses). Kept and allowlisted with reasons: `wallMs` (system_clock epoch ms) in
  vr_mptest/vr_voicechat, compared across processes (`za::Clock`'s epoch is unspecified). The Quest merge's 7 uses
  converted; the Android native build compiles (build-android, `cmake --build ... --target ironwail`).
- **Phases 4-5:** unqualified (and `std::`) `strcmp strncmp strlen strstr memcpy memset memcmp memmove memchr` ->
  `ZA_STRCMP`... (`Zancle/Base/<Name>.hpp`, `__builtin_*`: the same calls) in 80 files, vr_ad .. vr_cleanskins (644
  calls); comments and strings untouched; `<cstring>`/`<string.h>` dropped where no other string.h name is left
  (quakedef.h's `<string.h>` stays the source for `strchr` and friends). Left: ~1,980 calls in 217 files.
- **Counts (the allowlist):** std:: 156 -> 40, standard header includes 31 -> 9.
- **Tests:** release build 0 warnings each phase; smoke e1m1 with vr_hull_stats, vr_gun_pieces_cache_stats,
  vr_image_prefetch_info, vr_cache_warmup_info (counters move); startuplog 3/0; vr_voicechat_selftest 24/0;
  vr_android_test (-fakeandroid) 16/0. Not yet run: Misc/quakevr/check_nopch.sh (after the last phase).

## questogg: Ogg Vorbis music on the Quest (agent/questogg, 2026-11-23)

- The PC decodes Ogg with libvorbisfile (`Windows/codecs`, prebuilt; pkg-config on Linux): no source in the
  repository, so the Android build had no Ogg codec (WAV music only). Now `Quake/vr/external/stb_vorbis` (stb's
  v1.22, one file, MIT or public domain; README.md says where from, its hash) is built on every CMake build
  (`qvr_stb_vorbis`, vr.cmake) and in the PC's `quakevr.props`; a build without libvorbisfile (the Quest's) defines
  `USE_CODEC_VORBIS VORBIS_USE_STB` (CMakeLists.txt). `snd_vorbis.c` is one codec with two decoders (the same
  `vorbis_codec`, the `ogg` extension, bgmusic.c's whole music path: CD tracks, the map's music, mod folders): stb_vorbis
  on Android and in the PC's fake-Android mode (`-fakeandroid`, `QVR_STB_VORBIS`), libvorbisfile otherwise. stb_vorbis
  reads the stream's part of its file itself (`stb_vorbis_open_file_section`: a pak entry or a rerelease file in place).
- Size: +53 KB of code in libquakevr.so (arm64, -O2), 0.2%. Licence shipped as `licenses/stb_vorbis.txt`; CREDITS.md.
- `vr_music_decode [track] [ms]` (bgmusic.c; Debug > Tools "Music Decode"): decodes the start of a track as the music
  plays it: the file, format, decoder, rate, channels, frames, peak, PCM hash, and whether the loop's rewind reads the
  start again. Needs the sound on (the codecs start with it).
- Test: `Misc/quakevr/questogg_test.sh` (SDL's dummy audio driver, `-Sound`): the PC and `-fakeandroid` decode the
  rerelease's track02.ogg identically (132300 frames, 44100 Hz stereo, peak 21126 both), the rewind ok, start's track 4
  plays through stb_vorbis, no error: 12/0. music_test 7/0; vr_menu_path_check 0 missing; Android native build compiles.
- Installer (`QuestFiles.MusicFormats`, on agent/questinstall, not on next): add `.ogg` there when both are merged.

## questreal2: the Quest installer passes on the real headset; adb push, folder groups, the game's own folders (agent/questinstall, 2026-11-23)

Follows "questreal" above. origin/next merged again (Ogg on the Quest): `QuestFiles.MusicFormats` = WAV + Ogg (MP3 stays);
the test fixture has track02.ogg copied, track04.mp3 left behind. Release build 0 warnings; `quest:` self-tests 9/9.
- **Real-headset test: ALL 7 STEPS PASS** (run `scratch/qi_realtest/20261123-012908`): 4,605 files planned, 101 copied
  (222 MB) over 4,498 unchanged, the again-run "app unchanged, 0 files copied", every earlier file still there, the
  game's own 18 files (saves, configs) unchanged in size and time. The Ogg soundtrack is in `id1/music/` (track02-11).
- **The copy is `adb push` now, not one tar stream into `adb exec-in`.** With ustar headers the stream extracted, but
  adb's server took 2.8 GB in ~3 s, the headset's tar got ~400 MB (pak0 whole, pak1 cut at 142 MB) and an 830 MB test
  killed the server ("daemon not running"): the cause of the earlier "offline". `adb shell -T` with stdin: "tar: EOF:
  Illegal seek" after 21 KB. `QuestInstaller.PushBatches`: files of one headset folder under their PC names in one push
  (256 MB, 16,000 characters a push), any renamed file (PAK1.PAK -> id1/pak1.pak) alone; ~150-300 MB/s.
- **Folders before pushing: the storage's group, set-group-ID** (`chgrp ext_data_rw`, `chmod 2777`). adb push into a
  folder of the shell's group failed "remote fchown failed"; a folder push makes itself "secure_mkdirs failed". The
  installer's own old `chmod 0777` cleared the bit (id1), so folders made in it got the shell's group; now 2777.
- **Folders the game made itself** (u0_a207, 770: his `quakevr/doom` and `doom/wads`, made by `vr_doom.cpp
  doomFolder()` when Doom was opened before its WADs came): adb cannot write there, so their 6 files (the Freedoom WADs)
  are reported (`QuestResult.NotWritable`, a warning, the Done card says which folder), the rest copied, not a failed
  install. Only the game (or uninstalling) can clear it. Open: `doomFolder()` could avoid making the folder on the Quest
  when the WADs are missing.
- A push adb's server lost under it ("cannot connect to daemon": another adb version on the PC took the server) is
  retried 4 times. The SDK's adb (37.0.1) and the installer's (37.0.3) restart each other's server: use one.
- **Gib-fight measurement: no result.** The only APK (`qvr-agents/quest/build-android/apk`, 2026-11-22 15:26) predates
  `vr_blood_near` and `vr_standalone_preset` ("Unknown command"), so both parts ran the same settings. What it does
  show for that APK: the frozen gib fight (six grunts gibbed 56-90 units ahead, `vr_limb_test 10`) at GPU median
  14.8-15.5 ms, frame period median 15.8-16.9 ms, 64-80% of frames over 15.3 ms: 72 Hz does not hold. Needs a current
  APK build, then `scratch/qr_run.sh gore1 600 qr_gore.cfg +vr_standalone_preset 0` with the test progs.dat pushed
  (then `qvr-setup quest` puts the shipped one back, as done here: "1 files copied").
## flatjitter: the gun at a wall looking down settles; the level forward probe (agent/flatjitter, 2026-11-23)

Built on origin/next with agent/flatgreen2 merged in (its test fixes are what flatsweep and flatlagbob are judged by).

- **flatsweep's `settled wall/long/stand/hip` at 25 down** (0.947 units a frame for 500 frames): a limit cycle of the
  muzzle-up tilt (`vr_flat_wall_tilt`, fixed: all 40 degrees or none). Its trigger, the level gun 0.25 units deep at the
  most the way back takes it, read 0.24-0.27 there, and the reading moved with the tilt's own ease: the tilt went on
  and off every three frames. Two paths fed the drawn (tilted) gun back into the pose's level gun:
  - modelcollide's recorded weapon (`weaponShape`, handpose's gun depth): `toHand` is the drawn model in the drawn hand's
    frame, and tilted it stood up to 0.3 units elsewhere (18 degrees: the model doesn't turn exactly round `s.pos`). Now
    `shapeToHand`, kept while flatplay's `drawnWallTurn` turns or shifts the gun (same model and frame); the drawn
    points (`drawnWeaponPoints`) still use the drawn one. VR: the turn is always identity there, so unchanged.
  - flatsight's hotspot in the gun's frame (`spotLocal`, the stance's keepSpot holds it in the free arm's reach, which
    moved the hand 0.04 units with the tilt): kept the same way while the wall tilt or slide is on.
  With both, the 25-degree row settles (wall run: 140 rows, 0 unsettled; it was 1). A hysteresis on the trigger alone
  (0.1 units) didn't help: the hand then crept to the lower edge. The check is flatsweep_check's own unsettled-row
  failure. Tests: flatsweep 383 passed, 27 known, 0 failed (was 382/1); flatwall 17/0. flatxhair 27/4 (flatgreen2 had
  28/3; the new one, "pixels open: drawn on the centre (4 px, centroid 479.5 vs 480.0)", came in the low-impact mode with
  his game running: low-res mock eyes; not re-run). flatsight could not run (its runs wait for his game to close).
- **flatlagbob's level case** (fwd 0 range 1.01, fwd 2 1.94; wants +1.0): **not the sway**. At a run the level fwd-0
  range is 0.94 with `vr_flat_sway 1` and 1.05 with 0 (walking 0.67); the sway's forward part peaks at 0.15 on the run
  (its kicks are the start and e1m1's stairs down, mostly up and down). Per frame, the main hand *and its shoulder* move
  together along the view by about +-0.45 at the stride's rate (period ~31 frames, 2.3 Hz) while the run goes down
  e1m1's stairs: the body rides something at the step rate with `vr_flat_bob_fwd 0` (looking 40 down the shoulder's range
  is 0.00, so it is level-forward and up together, not along the view). Since that motion and the forward bob aren't in
  phase, the ranges don't add: 1.01 + 1.2 gives 1.94. Open: which commit put a stride-rate forward ride on the body (a
  bisect from 97446fada of the shoulder's range, not done: budget), or the check measures the bob's own amplitude
  (fwd 2 minus fwd 0 per frame) instead of the ranges' difference.
